title: Error in temperature and brightness when using lightOperation
body:
Only tested on "TRADFRI bulb E27 WS opal 980lm" with firmware 1.2.217 (Gateway firmware is 1.2.42).

To reproduce, first set the brightness of the light with

```javascript
client.operateLight(light, {"dimmer":3})
```

When inspecting `light` it will have its `dimmer` property set to 4. Likewise, 
```javascript
client.operateLight(light, {"colorTemperature":100})
```
will result in a `colorTemperature` of 98 in the light object.

There are several more values that will not get set correctly in similar fashion. I suppose this is due to conversion between values used by the gateway and the [0,100] scale used in the API.

It would be great if the proper ranges for both brightness and temperature were usable in the API, since it allows finer granularity control. You probably already know this but:
   - brightness (property 5851) accepts values in [0,254]
   - color temperature (property 5711) accepts any value but WS bulbs will show values in [250, 454]. CWS bulbs supposedly can't use this property but I wouldn't know since I don't own any.

title: Causes crashes in OctoPrint's login when disabled
body:
I just had a user report an odd issue in foosel/OctoPrint#2442. They have the Astroprint plugin disabled, and that makes them not able to login anymore.

A closer look at OctoPrint's plugin subsystem reveals that contrary to what I so far assumed, plugins are still loaded even when disabled. Which means that in your case the plugin's implementation will be initialized, and in its constructor functions will be attached to Flask Login's loggedIn and loggedOut signals that try to send messages to the frontend via `self._plugin_manager` - however, if your plugin is disabled, your plugin won't be fully initialized, `self._plugin_manager` hence not injected and that means things crash inside Flask Login when trying to call your signal handler and the login fails with an HTTP 500.

I'll have to do something about this on OctoPrint's side, however I strongly suggest to not attach any stuff to the system as long as the plugin is not fully initialized (read: the `initialized` method on it is called). 

Could you fix this on your end? As I said, I'll also look into finding a good fix on mine. If push comes to shove, disabled plugins will simply get the same treatment that blacklisted ones get, meaning some metadata will be missing in the plugin list but no code will be executed at all, preventing such issues in the future.

Wrong status from IoTHubDeviceClient_LL_GetSendStatus during reconnect
body:
**Development Machine, OS, Compiler (and Other Relevant Toolchain Info)**

Ubuntu 16.04

**SDK Version (Please Give Commit SHA if Manually Compiling)**

Release 2019-05-16

**Protocol**

AMQP

**Describe the Bug**

Hi,

the application I am building is supposed to establish an IoT Hub connection when it is needed and close it after a certain timeout when there are no new messages and after all messages in the queue have been sent (IoTHubDeviceClient_LL_GetSendStatus() returns IOTHUB_CLIENT_SEND_STATUS_IDLE).

As a measure against losing messages when the network goes down, I am resending messages in the confirm callback if the result is IOTHUB_CLIENT_CONFIRMATION_MESSAGE_TIMEOUT or IOTHUB_CLIENT_CONFIRMATION_ERROR.

If the connection stays down long enough for the SDK to run into a timeout and start attempts to reestablish the AMQP connection, the confirm callback is called with result IOTHUB_CLIENT_CONFIRMATION_ERROR. Sending the message again now via IoTHubDeviceClient_LL_SendEventAsync() returns IOTHUB_CLIENT_OK, but IoTHubDeviceClient_LL_GetSendStatus() returns IOTHUB_CLIENT_SEND_STATUS_IDLE.

If the IoT Hub client is destroyed now because my application assumes that there are no pending messages, the confirm callback for the message that has just been put into the queue is called with result IOTHUB_CLIENT_CONFIRMATION_BECAUSE_DESTROY.

I would expect IoTHubDeviceClient_LL_GetSendStatus() to return IOTHUB_CLIENT_SEND_STATUS_BUSY as long as there are messages waiting to be sent, no matter if they were enqueued while the transport is connected or not.
Or is there a different official way to find out if there are any pending messages in the queue?

EDIT: The behavior does not occur with the MQTT transport

title: IoTHubDeviceClient_SendReportedState / IoTHubDeviceClient_SendEventAsync only allows one callback for all reports
body:
(Note that below applies to `IoTHubDeviceClient_SendEventAsync` as well by analogy)

When invoking `IoTHubDeviceClient_SendReportedState` (or its module cousin), we only record the last callback function.

Consider for example

```c
IoTHubClientCore_SendReportedState(handle, "state-data-1",..., callback1);
IoTHubClientCore_SendReportedState(handle, "state-data-2",..., callback2);
```

`IoTHubClientCore_SendReportedState` (which does all the work) is saving the callback function at a handle-wide level, namely
```c
iotHubClientInstance->reported_state_callback = reportedStateCallback;
```

This makes the code above not work, because the `callback2` will end up over-writing `callback1` in the per-handle.  While this is OK for stuff like taking incoming device methods and properties to just have 1 dispatcher per handle, for device initiated sending there maybe legit reasons for having different callbacks for different types of reported properties / telemetry.

Note that the `LL` layer does this correctly - it tracks the callback function per the context (e.g. `IOTHUB_DEVICE_TWIN`) that is created per sending property.

title: AMQP <-> Eventhub <-> C SDK <-> C# SDK system properties mismatch
body:
I have noticed a couple of mismatches in behavior as well as interface between the different SDKs and the IoT Hub documentation.

If you take a look at the [documentation for messages](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/iot-hub/iot-hub-devguide-messaging#message-format) you can see that a message should have fields `To` and `UserId`. From the client side, the `To` field isn't necessary since it's implicitly defined as the corresponding IoTHub. The `UserId` field, should be defined as far as I understand it.

Furthermore, the [C# SDKs Message Class](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/microsoft.azure.devices.client.message?view=azuredevicesclient-1.2.6) allows me to set both fields. The [C SDKs equivalent](https://github.com/Azure/azure-iot-sdk-c/blob/master/iothub_client/inc/iothub_message.h), as far as I know, is not able to set either field. I can see why there is no method for the `To` property, but there should be one for the `UserId` property, even if it should be the same as the DeviceId.

When I receive a message from the C SDK with the [C# EventData Class](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/microsoft.servicebus.messaging.eventdata?view=azureservicebus-4.0.0) and take a look at the system properties, both fields are missing. This is unexpected, because the documentation as well as the [AMQP Protocol](http://www.amqp.org/sites/amqp.org/files/amqp.pdf) Chapter 3.2 let me believe that both fields should exist.

On the other hand, in the [C SDKs EventData class](https://github.com/Azure/azure-event-hubs-c/blob/master/eventhub_client/inc/eventdata.h) does not even provide me with a way to access system properties like the C# SDK does.

I have also discussed this issue on [stackoverflow ](http://stackoverflow.com/questions/43200966/how-do-i-set-certain-system-properties-with-the-azure-iot-c-sdk-for-the-amqp-pro) with Rita Han - MSFT, who proposed a workaround solution by setting the `To` and `UserId` properties via the application properties instead of the system / message properties.

So I wonder:

- Is this mismatch between the APIs and behaviors intentional?
- Is there some "proper" way of setting those properties with the C SDK?
- What is the actual semantic of `UserId` and when should it be set?
- Is this an issue with the C SDK? If so, is it going to be fixed?

Kind Regards,
Christopher Czyba

title: Remove duplicate STRING_construct_sprintf call in dt_interface_client.c
Reported twin info can enter no-free state on MQTT
body:
Acknowledgements to @markrad who did great investigation here and whose issue I'm basically copy/pasting below.

I've put a preliminary fix up https://github.com/Azure/azure-iot-sdk-c/tree/mqtt-twin-timeout-cleanup.  Cleaned up some of code so it's more common and of course removing reported properties.  UT's are passing but we clearly need more to cover this case.  I'll create PR after I sleep on this some and get UT.

--
Each time a device twin packet is sent to the IoT hub, the SDK will queue an item to the list ack_waiting_queue in iothubtransport_mqtt_common.c. This item will remain on the queue until the IoT hub sends a acknowledgment for the twin update.

At issue though is if there's a network disconnect (and I believe specifically that MQTT layer hasn't been alerted by underlying network stack) these packets have never been sent. Since these ack items do not have any kind of time out mechanism they will continue to collect on the ack queue and will never been removed.

There is a function in iothubtransport_mqtt_common.c called removeExpiredGetTwinRequestPendingAck that will clear the ack_waiting_queue of expired items but it specifically only processes items that are flagged as RETRIEVE_PROPERTIES. The end result is that the ack_waiting_queue will continue to grow every time there is a failure of the connection to the IoT hub.

title: PnP Environmental sensor does not follow HTTP status code conventions
body:
Our environmental sensor PnP sample interface today has an async command as part of its DTDL.

The way the code works:
* Returns a 202 on the initial acceptance of the request.
* A second later sends another 202 back indicating request is in progress.
* A second later sends a 200 to show the request is done.

The subsequent send of the 202 is not correct per my reading of HTTP status codes and some discussions.  We need instead to return a 102 to show processing on step2 above.

See https://httpstatuses.com/202 and https://httpstatuses.com/102.

title: Missing statement in switch()
PropertiesUpdatedCallback should be renamed to PropertiesNotificationCallback
body:
"PropertiesUpdatedCallback" causes confusion as it is being triggered for 2 scenario:
1) During device initialization on get Twin call 
2) writable property updates from the service side

For 1), the callback could be triggered without any "real" updates on the properties' values.  Rename it to "notification" to minimize confusion.

title: Components should be notify for stand-alone reported properties on initialization
body: During device initialization where get Twin is called for syncing with the service's side of the stored properties values, SDK provides the current value of the Desired AND the Reported (if the Reported exists) property to the user callback function.  Stand-alone reported properties values (in the full twin) should be provided to the components as well using the same callback function.

title: PnP should provide reported properties to app always
body:
Currently for C SDK, when we get a full twin we report properties to application *only* if there are desired properties in the list.  If there is a reported property but not a desired property, we just swallow it.

This isn't right.  We should always provide reported properties.  This will help bandwidth conscious interfaces to be thoughtful about whether they report back a given reported property again or whether they realize the server has what they were going to send up anyway and save the round-trip.

title: IoTHubClient_LL_SendEventAsync/IoTHubMessage_Destroy - memory management and example consistency
body:
The question is when is it safe to destroy the message - call IoTHubMessage_Destroy?

E.g. the following code immediately calls Destroy after SendEventAsync - which seems strange to me, because of the asynchronous character!? So couldn't it be that the message is freed before it is even sent?

https://github.com/Azure/azure-iot-sdk-c/blob/241b66eb6499e2c019682f252d911ef2b28d1302/iothub_client/samples/iothub_ll_client_sample_amqp_shared/iothub_ll_client_sample_amqp_shared.c#L283-L297

Also other code - like...

https://github.com/Azure/azure-iot-sdk-c/blob/241b66eb6499e2c019682f252d911ef2b28d1302/iothub_client/samples/iothub_client_sample_module_filter/iothub_client_sample_module_filter.c#L151-L154

https://github.com/Azure/azure-iot-sdk-c/blob/241b66eb6499e2c019682f252d911ef2b28d1302/iothub_client/samples/iothub_client_sample_module_filter/iothub_client_sample_module_filter.c#L86-L91

only destroys the message if the call to SendEventAsync fails - and otherwise postpones the disposal into the confirmation callback - this seems logically more correct. But if this is correct, then there is the bonus question - what happens if the callback is NULL - is the message freed implicitly by SendEventAsync in this case? Or are we just having a memory leak since there is no defined event at which we can be sure it is ok to dispose the sent messages?

Unfortunately the documentation (https://docs.microsoft.com/de-de/azure/iot-hub/iot-c-sdk-ref/iothub-client-core-ll-h/iothubclientcore-ll-sendeventasync) is just not meaningful and the sample code is as explained contradictive.

Thanks in advance for any hints and please don't hesitate to ask if I kept to short and you need additional input to get the intention.

title: Don't directly reference `DIGITALTWIN_CLIENT_SDK_VERSION` in SDK Information
body:
PnP's sample of SDKInformation has a hardcoded reference of `DIGITALTWIN_CLIENT_SDK_VERSION` in it to specify the version.

If the dev updates the SDK and statically links the code in, then we'll be fine because `DIGITALTWIN_CLIENT_SDK_VERSION` will be updated and they'll recompile.

If they're using pnp_sdk.dll and not recompiling, directly referencing `DIGITALTWIN_CLIENT_SDK_VERSION` is a problem.

Instead we should:
* Fix SDKInformation to use `DigitalTwin_Client_GetVersionString`.
* Remove `DIGITALTWIN_CLIENT_SDK_VERSION` from the header so that other people don't make the same mistake.

title: AV in IoTHub client when reconnecting on AMQP
body:
<!--
Hi there! thank you for discovering and submitting an issue!

Please first tell us a little bit about the environment you're running:
-->


- **OS and version used:** <VERSION> <!-- Windows 10, Ubuntu 15.04... -->

- **SDK version used:** <VERSION> <!-- Please include the SDK version -->
4b9b17fb45a04c79e271c54a09bad2b12b19a9b3

# Description of the issue:
<!-- Please be as detailed as possible: which feature has a problem, how often does it fail,  -->
I setup a client sending to IoTHub continuously every 1 second by modifying iothub_client_sample_amqp.c to send every 1s.
Then I blocked traffic from the server to the client by specific means until the reconnect was triggered.
At the reconnect time => AV.

# Code sample exhibiting the issue:
<!-- Please remove any connection string information! -->

// Copyright (c) Microsoft. All rights reserved.
// Licensed under the MIT license. See LICENSE file in the project root for full license information.

#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

#include "azure_c_shared_utility/platform.h"
#include "azure_c_shared_utility/threadapi.h"
#include "azure_c_shared_utility/crt_abstractions.h"
#include "iothub_client.h"
#include "iothub_message.h"
#include "iothubtransportamqp.h"

#ifdef MBED_BUILD_TIMESTAMP
#include "certs.h"
#endif // MBED_BUILD_TIMESTAMP

/*String containing Hostname, Device Id & Device Key in the format:                         */
/*  "HostName=<host_name>;DeviceId=<device_id>;SharedAccessKey=<device_key>"                */
/*  "HostName=<host_name>;DeviceId=<device_id>;SharedAccessSignature=<device_sas_token>"    */
static const char* connectionString = "hagauaga, insert your credentials here, blah";

static int callbackCounter;
static bool g_continueRunning;
static char msgText[1024];
static char propText[1024];
#define MESSAGE_COUNT       50000
#define DOWORK_LOOP_NUM     3

typedef struct EVENT_INSTANCE_TAG
{
    IOTHUB_MESSAGE_HANDLE messageHandle;
    size_t messageTrackingId;  // For tracking the messages within the user callback.
} EVENT_INSTANCE;

static IOTHUBMESSAGE_DISPOSITION_RESULT ReceiveMessageCallback(IOTHUB_MESSAGE_HANDLE message, void* userContextCallback)
{
    int* counter = (int*)userContextCallback;
    const unsigned char* buffer = NULL;
    size_t size = 0;
    const char* messageId;
    const char* correlationId;

    // Message properties
    if ((messageId = IoTHubMessage_GetMessageId(message)) == NULL)
    {
        messageId = "<null>";
    }

    if ((correlationId = IoTHubMessage_GetCorrelationId(message)) == NULL)
    {
        correlationId = "<null>";
    }

    // Message content
    IOTHUBMESSAGE_CONTENT_TYPE contentType = IoTHubMessage_GetContentType(message);

    if (contentType == IOTHUBMESSAGE_BYTEARRAY)
    {
        if (IoTHubMessage_GetByteArray(message, &buffer, &size) == IOTHUB_MESSAGE_OK)
        {
            (void)printf("Received Message [%d]\r\n Message ID: %s\r\n Correlation ID: %s\r\n BINARY Data: <<<%.*s>>> & Size=%d\r\n", *counter, messageId, correlationId, (int)size, buffer, (int)size);
        }
        else
        {
            (void)printf("Failed getting the BINARY body of the message received.\r\n");
        }
    }
    else if (contentType == IOTHUBMESSAGE_STRING)
    {
        if ((buffer = (const unsigned char*)IoTHubMessage_GetString(message)) != NULL && (size = strlen((const char*)buffer)) > 0)
        {
            (void)printf("Received Message [%d]\r\n Message ID: %s\r\n Correlation ID: %s\r\n STRING Data: <<<%.*s>>> & Size=%d\r\n", *counter, messageId, correlationId, (int)size, buffer, (int)size);

            // If we receive the work 'quit' then we stop running
        }
        else
        {
            (void)printf("Failed getting the STRING body of the message received.\r\n");
        }
    }
    else
    {
        (void)printf("Failed getting the body of the message received (type %i).\r\n", contentType);
    }

    // Retrieve properties from the message
    MAP_HANDLE mapProperties = IoTHubMessage_Properties(message);
    if (mapProperties != NULL)
    {
        const char*const* keys;
        const char*const* values;
        size_t propertyCount = 0;
        if (Map_GetInternals(mapProperties, &keys, &values, &propertyCount) == MAP_OK)
        {
            if (propertyCount > 0)
            {
                size_t index;

                printf(" Message Properties:\r\n");
                for (index = 0; index < propertyCount; index++)
                {
                    printf("\tKey: %s Value: %s\r\n", keys[index], values[index]);
                }
                printf("\r\n");
            }
        }
    }

    if (size == (strlen("quit") * sizeof(char)) && memcmp(buffer, "quit", size) == 0)
    {
        g_continueRunning = false;
    }

    /* Some device specific action code goes here... */
    (*counter)++;
    return IOTHUBMESSAGE_ACCEPTED;
}

static void SendConfirmationCallback(IOTHUB_CLIENT_CONFIRMATION_RESULT result, void* userContextCallback)
{
    EVENT_INSTANCE* eventInstance = (EVENT_INSTANCE*)userContextCallback;
    (void)printf("Confirmation[%d] received for message tracking id = %zu with result = %s\r\n", callbackCounter, eventInstance->messageTrackingId, ENUM_TO_STRING(IOTHUB_CLIENT_CONFIRMATION_RESULT, result));
    /* Some device specific action code goes here... */
    callbackCounter++;
    IoTHubMessage_Destroy(eventInstance->messageHandle);
}

void iothub_client_sample_amqp_run(void)
{
    IOTHUB_CLIENT_LL_HANDLE iotHubClientHandle;

    EVENT_INSTANCE messages[MESSAGE_COUNT];

    g_continueRunning = true;
    srand((unsigned int)time(NULL));
    double avgWindSpeed = 10.0;

    callbackCounter = 0;
    int receiveContext = 0;

    (void)printf("Starting the IoTHub client sample AMQP...\r\n");

    if (platform_init() != 0)
    {
        printf("Failed to initialize the platform.\r\n");
    }
    else
    {
        if ((iotHubClientHandle = IoTHubClient_LL_CreateFromConnectionString(connectionString, AMQP_Protocol)) == NULL)
        {
            (void)printf("ERROR: iotHubClientHandle is NULL!\r\n");
        }
        else
        {
            bool traceOn = true;
            IoTHubClient_LL_SetOption(iotHubClientHandle, "logtrace", &traceOn);

#ifdef MBED_BUILD_TIMESTAMP
            // For mbed add the certificate information
            if (IoTHubClient_LL_SetOption(iotHubClientHandle, "TrustedCerts", certificates) != IOTHUB_CLIENT_OK)
            {
                printf("failure to set option \"TrustedCerts\"\r\n");
            }
#endif // MBED_BUILD_TIMESTAMP

            /* Setting Message call back, so we can receive Commands. */
            if (IoTHubClient_LL_SetMessageCallback(iotHubClientHandle, ReceiveMessageCallback, &receiveContext) != IOTHUB_CLIENT_OK)
            {
                (void)printf("ERROR: IoTHubClient_SetMessageCallback..........FAILED!\r\n");
            }
            else
            {
                (void)printf("IoTHubClient_SetMessageCallback...successful.\r\n");

                /* Now that we are ready to receive commands, let's send some messages */

title: [MQTT] ConnectionStatus / EventConfirmation callback behaviors are not consistent when network is disconnected
body:
In the release of "2016-11-17", when running the test cases to disconnect/resume network, the callback behaviors could be different, hence making the program to use Azure IoT device SDK become difficult to manage network situations.

Usually we expect "ConnectionStatus" callback will report connection status once the connection status is changed. However when disconnect/resume network manually, we'll found it's not true always. If the program starts with network disconnected, "ConnectionStatus" callback might not be called, and this might happened maybe 7 times out of 10 tries, and there are 3 times the ConnectionStatus callback will be called when doing the first call to "IoTHubClient_LL_DoWork()". This kind of behavior make it difficult to detect network disconnection, if the program is waiting for C2D message from IoT Hub.

"EventConfirmation" callback for "IoTHubClient_LL_SendEventAsync()" is also inconsistent. If the network disconnection is detected during the time trying to send the message, "EventConfirmation" will get a error callback, and this message is then aborted/dropped, hence a message level retry could be handled within this callback. If network is not resumed, then for the next message, "EventConfirmation" callback will never be called (if "messageTimeout" is not set) to reflect network error.

So the message sent callback might have two different result in corresponding to network disconnection, one is callback with error, the other is no callback or a callback with timeout error.

Please help to make the behavior consistent, so to avoid potential defects.

title: Azure IoT SDK C - Issue during reconnection attempt when utilizing openSSL and amqp over websockets
body:
Hello,
I have encountered an issue during the reconnection attempt when using openSSL and amqpWS as Protocol. (Windows)
<!--
Hi there! thank you for discovering and submitting an issue!

Please first tell us a little bit about the environment you're running:
-->


- **OS and version used:** Windows 7
- **SDK version used:** 1.1.21 
-  Dev environment set up according to : https://github.com/Azure/azure-iot-sdk-c/blob/master/doc/devbox_setup.md#windows 
- Visual Studio 2015
- openSSL 1.0.2j or 1.0.2l (should also be reproducible with 1.0.2.k)
- target platform x86


# Description of the issue:
Within c-utility\src\tlsio_openssl.c, the tlsio_openssl_setoption function expects the value as pointer to int during evaluation of the tls_version option. This works fine when invoking IoTHubClient_SetOption. 
However, on a reconnection attempt the tlsio_openssl_setoption function will be invoked like this:

 	exampled.exe!tlsio_openssl_setoption(void * tls_io, const char * optionName, const void * value) Line 1548	C
 	exampled.exe!OptionHandler_FeedOptions(OPTIONHANDLER_HANDLE_DATA_TAG * handle, void * destinationHandle) Line 236	C
 	exampled.exe!xio_setoption(XIO_INSTANCE_TAG * xio, const char * optionName, const void * value) Line 184	C
 	exampled.exe!OptionHandler_FeedOptions(OPTIONHANDLER_HANDLE_DATA_TAG * handle, void * destinationHandle) Line 236	C
 	exampled.exe!uws_client_set_option(UWS_CLIENT_INSTANCE_TAG * uws_client, const char * option_name, const void * value) Line 1841	C
 	exampled.exe!OptionHandler_FeedOptions(OPTIONHANDLER_HANDLE_DATA_TAG * handle, void * destinationHandle) Line 236	C
 	exampled.exe!wsio_setoption(void * ws_io, const char * optionName, const void * value) Line 670	C
 	exampled.exe!OptionHandler_FeedOptions(OPTIONHANDLER_HANDLE_DATA_TAG * handle, void * destinationHandle) Line 236	C
 	exampled.exe!xio_setoption(XIO_INSTANCE_TAG * xio, const char * optionName, const void * value) Line 184	C
 	exampled.exe!OptionHandler_FeedOptions(OPTIONHANDLER_HANDLE_DATA_TAG * handle, void * destinationHandle) Line 236	C
	exampled.exe!restore_underlying_io_transport_options(AMQP_TRANSPORT_INSTANCE_TAG * transport_instance, XIO_INSTANCE_TAG * xio_handle) Line 613	C
 	exampled.exe!get_new_underlying_io_transport(AMQP_TRANSPORT_INSTANCE_TAG * transport_instance, XIO_INSTANCE_TAG * * xio_handle) Line 659	C
 	exampled.exe!establish_amqp_connection(AMQP_TRANSPORT_INSTANCE_TAG * transport_instance) Line 716	C

When invoked like this, the transport_instance->saved_tls_options OPTIONHANDLER_HANDLE gets evaluated which instead of containing a pointer to the value, contains the value itself.
The issue occurs in c-utility\src\tlsio_openssl.c on lines 1548ff, when the passed void pointer gets cast and accessed.

# Code sample exhibiting the issue:
` const int* version_option = value;`
                
`if ((int)(intptr_t)*version_option == 0 || (int)(intptr_t)*version_option == 10)`
`                {`
`                    tls_io_instance->tls_version = VERSION_1_0;`
`                }`

# Console log of the issue:
Exception thrown: read access violation.
version_option was 0x2.

title: No reconnection after network disconnection
body:
Hi,

I'm facing the some problems with the connection to the IoTHub after connection lose.

## Setup
I'm running the last version of the SDK `2017-10-09` on Ubuntu 16.04.
Ubuntu is running on a VM on a Windows 10.

## Description 

I'm running a simple client that send every 5 seconds a message on the IoTHub.
The transport protocol used is MQTT.

### Case 1 (working)
When the device is disconnected "locally" (see schema below) the SDK handles the reconnection properly after some time when the connection is back. The messages are correctly enqueued and are sent as soon as the connection is back.
`|device|---------|Ubuntu(VM)|----X----|Windows|---------|Internet|---------|IoTHub|`

### Case 2 (not working)
When the device is disconnected from windows (we cut the connection), The socket in the SDK receive a signal 13 (SIGPIPE) and the connection is not recovered.
`|device|---------|Ubuntu(VM)|---------|Windows|----X----|Internet|---------|IoTHub|`


In fact, we observed the same behavior on a real device, when the internet connection is lost by a switch. 
`|device|---------|switch|----X----|Internet|---------|IoTHub|`

    }

title: Connection is not re-established after network interruption (AMQP/WS, x509)
body:
- **OS and version used:** Ubuntu 16.04.3 LTS

- **SDK version used:** bac8131fd232c7bbc7ac4243d6b2860c9668d6c6

- **Protocol:** AMQP over Websockets

# Description of the issue:
After a successfull connection the network is disconnected and reconnected later. Depending on the timing the connection is not re-established again.

# Code sample exhibiting the issue:
(similar setup as in issue #251)
Take the `iothub_client/samples/iothub_client_sample_x509/iothub_client_sample_x509.c` and:

1. adapt connection string, certificate and key
1. change `#define MESSAGE_COUNT 5` to `#define MESSAGE_COUNT 5000`
1. add `IoTHubClient_LL_SetRetryPolicy(iotHubClientHandle, IOTHUB_CLIENT_RETRY_IMMEDIATE, 0)`
1. change the `ThreadAPI_Sleep(1)` in the while loop to `ThreadAPI_Sleep(1000)`

# Reproduction steps

1. start the application 
1. wait until connection is established and first messages are confirmed
1. disconnect network
1. disconnection is detected after 4min, I guess this is the AMQP idle timeout?
1. wait another 4min, then reconnect network
=> no connection is established

if I re-connect within a 4min window after the disconnection is detected the connection is established successfully. But not immediatly (as the IMMEDIATE retry policy would imply) but only at the end of this 4min window.
After this 4min window the IMMEDIATE retry policy seems to come into action and tries to re-connect continuously but without success. Based on the log and on a network capture with Wireshark I can see that the connection is continuously opened and immediatly closed (by the device). No logical link is established, e.g. no message callbacks are called).

# Description of the issue:

I'm working on a custom implementation of the MQTT sample, put in a state machine and set to push a single message in a user-selectable time interval (between 5 minutes and 1 hour). The requirements of the company I'm working for do not involve receiving C2D messages for now.

Having disabled a device in the IoT Hub and trying to connect to it for sending messages, the result is the client being stuck in an "idle" state after reaching the retry policy timeout (1 minute on IOTHUB_CLIENT_RETRY_EXPONENTIAL_BACKOFF_WITH_JITTER).

# Code sample exhibiting the issue:
<!-- Please remove any connection string information! -->
**Setup:**
_iothub_client_sample_mqtt_ modified in these points:
- Added Connection Status callback: it basically quits the main do-while loop after _CONN_RETRY_NUM_ (set to 4) unsuccessful connection attempts.
```
static void ConnStatCallback(IOTHUB_CLIENT_CONNECTION_STATUS result, IOTHUB_CLIENT_CONNECTION_STATUS_REASON reason, void* userContextCallback)
{
    int* counter = (int*)userContextCallback;

    if (result == IOTHUB_CLIENT_CONNECTION_AUTHENTICATED)
    {
        IOTHUB_LOGDEBUG("Attempt %d of %d: MQTT connection established", *counter, CONN_RETRY_NUM);
    }
    else
    {
        (*counter)++;

        if (reason == IOTHUB_CLIENT_CONNECTION_BAD_CREDENTIAL)
        {
            IOTHUB_LOGDEBUG("Attempt %d of %d: Invalid Device Id or Shared Access Key", *counter, CONN_RETRY_NUM);
        }
        else if (reason == IOTHUB_CLIENT_CONNECTION_COMMUNICATION_ERROR)
        {
            IOTHUB_LOGDEBUG("Attempt %d of %d: Communication error", *counter, CONN_RETRY_NUM);
        }
        else if (reason == IOTHUB_CLIENT_CONNECTION_DEVICE_DISABLED)
        {
            IOTHUB_LOGDEBUG("Attempt %d of %d: Device disabled by IoT Hub", *counter, CONN_RETRY_NUM);
        }
        else if (reason == IOTHUB_CLIENT_CONNECTION_EXPIRED_SAS_TOKEN)
        {
            IOTHUB_LOGDEBUG("Attempt %d of %d: SAS Token expired", *counter, CONN_RETRY_NUM);
        }
    }

    IOTHUB_LOGDEBUG("ConnStat callback counter = %d", *counter);
    if (*counter >= CONN_RETRY_NUM)
    {
        IOTHUB_LOGDEBUG("Maximum number of attempts reached, exiting IoT Hub Client");
        g_continueRunning = false;
    }
}
```

```
static void SendConfirmationCallback(IOTHUB_CLIENT_CONFIRMATION_RESULT result, void* userContextCallback)
{

    if (callbackCounter >= MESSAGE_COUNT)
    {
        g_continueRunning = false;
    }
}

body:

title: Mqtt not timing out messages when can't reconnect
body:
Initially opened on https://github.com/Azure/azure-iot-sdk-python/issues/216

If MQTT is unable to establish a connection, it will keep trying and once it succeeds queued messages will be sent to the Cloud.

However, if for some reason we can't get past the initial connection phase, then SDK does not respect message timeouts.  An easy way to repro this is to just send a few messages with networking enabled via convenience sample, then disable your network in middle.

What is happening is that in `IoTHubTransport_MQTT_Common_DoWork`, we have logic that will compare max # of retries and ultimately call `sendMsgComplete(mqttMsgEntry->iotHubMessageEntry, transport_data, IOTHUB_CLIENT_CONFIRMATION_MESSAGE_TIMEOUT);` which tells caller that we should timeout.

However - if the initial call to `InitializeConnection` at the top of this function fails, then we never get into the correct spot in the loop to check the timeouts.  

Note there is at IoTHub_Client layer a `DoTimeouts` API.  However it doesn't save us here because its already transferred the messages from its pending queue to MQTT's waitingForAck.

To fix this
A) Checking for message timeouts should not be conditional on state of MQTT itself.  And 
B) It feels more natural to be the timeout based on actual timing, instead of checking whether a retry has occurred or not.  
C) The code in the block `Codes_SRS_IOTHUB_TRANSPORT_MQTT_COMMON_07_057` also needs review.  After we timeout the 1st timed out message, it looks like we unconditionally run through the queued messages and reset their retryCount=0.  If we just did (B) though, this would be moot.
symptom: Message delivery issues, Disconnetion issues, Reconnection issues

title: Crash when deleting device on IoT Hub while registering on MQTT_WS
Add a way to check on low-level AMQP or MQTT connect failures
body:
- **OS and version used:** Linux

- **SDK version used:** release_2018_10_03

# Description of the issue:
The problem to be solved is that the attempt to connect to Azure sometimes fails at the low level, and the low level debug messages make this plain, but nothing is communicated back to the high level functions that we are using. (Either they return void, or the cases where they return an opaque handle only fail when something seriously bad happens, like a malloc failure or null input argument.) Examples would be an unauthorized ConnectionString or bad proxy settings. Without this, much time passes until you find that you can’t send messages; that is your clue that the connection was not opened.

The callback for the Connection Status change is not being invoked here, presumably because it has not yet *changed*.

Looking at the existing Azure APIs, none is quite right for getting at this. Adding a getter for the Connection Status would be one option, though that may be a fair amount of work since the mocking function must also be provided, and tests to validate it.

What I chose to do was to patch the closest of the existing APIs, GetSendStatus. Normally this returns IOTHUB_CLIENT_OK if it is able to get the SendStatus (which is either Idle or Busy, returned as an output parameter). My simple patch was to return IOTHUB_CLIENT_ERROR from the low level IoTHubTransport_AMQP_Common_GetSendStatus() function if transport’s state is not Connected or Connecting.

I think a better choice, if still using the same API signature for GetSendStatus, would be to extend the set of enums from just Idle and Busy to add NotConnected or somesuch. The justification for leaning on this API could be that NotConnected is an indication of "why you can’t Send right now".

# Code sample exhibiting the issue:
My patch, for AMQP over websockets, is provided here. I recommend adding the new enum instead of what I did, but the patch shows the way. I think MQTT will have a similar solution.
[ll_ampq_extensions.patch.txt](https://github.com/Azure/azure-iot-sdk-c/files/2634678/ll_ampq_extensions.patch.txt)

typedef struct MESSAGE_INSTANCE_TAG
{

	size_t messageTrackingId;  // For tracking the messages within the user callback.

MESSAGE_INSTANCE;

size_t messagesReceivedByInput1Queue = 0;

// SendConfirmationCallback is invoked when the message that was forwarded on from 'InputQueue1Callback'
// pipeline function is confirmed.
static void SendConfirmationCallback(IOTHUB_CLIENT_CONFIRMATION_RESULT result, void* userContextCallback)
{
	// The context corresponds to which message# we were at when we sent.
	MESSAGE_INSTANCE* messageInstance = (MESSAGE_INSTANCE*)userContextCallback;
	printf("Confirmation[%zu] received for message with result = %d\r\n", messageInstance->messageTrackingId, result);
	IoTHubMessage_Destroy(messageInstance->messageHandle);
	free(messageInstance);
}

// Allocates a context for callback and clones the message
// NOTE: The message MUST be cloned at this stage.  InputQueue1Callback's caller always frees the message
// so we need to pass down a new copy.
static MESSAGE_INSTANCE* CreateMessageInstance(IOTHUB_MESSAGE_HANDLE message)
{
	MESSAGE_INSTANCE* messageInstance = (MESSAGE_INSTANCE*)malloc(sizeof(MESSAGE_INSTANCE));
	if (NULL == messageInstance)
	{
		printf("Failed allocating 'MESSAGE_INSTANCE' for pipelined message\r\n");
	}
	else
	{
		memset(messageInstance, 0, sizeof(*messageInstance));

		if ((messageInstance->messageHandle = IoTHubMessage_Clone(message)) == NULL)
		{
			free(messageInstance);
			messageInstance = NULL;
		}
		else
		{
			messageInstance->messageTrackingId = messagesReceivedByInput1Queue;
		}
	}

	return messageInstance;
}

static IOTHUBMESSAGE_DISPOSITION_RESULT InputQueue1Callback(IOTHUB_MESSAGE_HANDLE message, void* userContextCallback)
{
	IOTHUBMESSAGE_DISPOSITION_RESULT result;
	IOTHUB_CLIENT_RESULT clientResult;
	IOTHUB_MODULE_CLIENT_LL_HANDLE iotHubModuleClientHandle = (IOTHUB_MODULE_CLIENT_LL_HANDLE)userContextCallback;

	unsigned const char* messageBody;
	size_t contentSize;

	if (IoTHubMessage_GetByteArray(message, &messageBody, &contentSize) != IOTHUB_MESSAGE_OK)
	{
		messageBody = NULL;
	}

	printf("Received Message [%zu]\r\n Data: [%s]\r\n",
		messagesReceivedByInput1Queue, messageBody);

	// This message should be sent to next stop in the pipeline, namely "output1".  What happens at "outpu1" is determined
	// by the configuration of the Edge routing table setup.
	MESSAGE_INSTANCE *messageInstance = CreateMessageInstance(message);
	if (NULL == messageInstance)
	{
		result = IOTHUBMESSAGE_ABANDONED;
	}
	else
	{
		printf("Sending message (%zu) to the next stage in pipeline\n", messagesReceivedByInput1Queue);

		clientResult = IoTHubModuleClient_LL_SendEventToOutputAsync(iotHubModuleClientHandle, messageInstance->messageHandle, "output1", SendConfirmationCallback, (void *)messageInstance);
		if (clientResult != IOTHUB_CLIENT_OK)
		{
			IoTHubMessage_Destroy(messageInstance->messageHandle);
			free(messageInstance);
			printf("IoTHubModuleClient_LL_SendEventToOutputAsync failed on sending msg#=%zu, err=%d\n", messagesReceivedByInput1Queue, clientResult);
			result = IOTHUBMESSAGE_ABANDONED;
		}
		else
		{
			result = IOTHUBMESSAGE_ACCEPTED;
		}
	}

	messagesReceivedByInput1Queue++;
	return result;
}

title: concurency issue with blob upload
body:
- **OS and version used:** Ubuntu 18.04

- **SDK version used:** lts_10_2018

# Description of the issue:
Hi,

From the [iothubclient_requirements](https://github.com/Azure/azure-iot-sdk-c/blob/master/iothub_client/devdoc/requirement_docs/iothubclient_requirements.md#overview), the high-level API should be thread-safe (unlike the low-level one). However, the blob upload interface does not respect this. 

When the `IoTHubClientCore_UploadToBlobAsync` function is called, a dedicated thread is spawned. the low-level function `IoTHubClientCore_LL_UploadToBlob` is then called within this thread, triggering the process of blob upload. 

If the function `IoTHubClientCore_UploadToBlobAsync` is called multiple times, nothing prevent threads to be launched. On Linux platform using curl adapter, `HTTPAPI_Init` function will be called multiple times. This may result in a concurrent access of the `nUsersOfHTTPAPI` variable, thus interfering with the calls to `curl_global_init` and `curl_global_cleanup`.

How can we prevent this? Is allowing only one blob upload at a time the correct behavior?

Regards,
Alexis.

# Description of the issue:
Dear All,

I’m writing this issue about some difficulties in the managing of X.509 certificate and of private key in my IoT device.

I use the 1.2.13 release version of C Device SDK in my embedded platform and I choose the MQTT protocol for the communication between my IoT device and IoT Hub. The MQTT is made secure through the TLS layer implemented by the mbedTLS library.

In the first part of my test I use a Sas authentication device and all works fine. I set only one client option, _OPTION_TRUSTED_CERT_, in way to guarantee a successfully one way TLS authentication.

In the second part of my test I use a self signed authentication device. So I set three client options:  _OPTION_TRUSTED_CERT_, _SU_OPTION_X509_CERT_ and _SU_OPTION_X509_PRIVATE_KEY_. However my device, during the TLS handshake, provides a null certificate, then the IoT Hub can’t authenticate my device.
The client options are configured successfully through the _IoTHubClient_LL_SetOption_ function. 
In order to run my MQTT client I invoke the _IoTHubClient_LL_DoWork_ function.
Before the establishment of the MQTT connection between my IoT device and IoT Hub I notice that the client options are resetted inside the _ResetConnectionIfNecessary_ function. Theoretically all the existing client options are first retrieved and then saved before the cancellation through the _xio_retrieveoptions_ and _set_saved_tls_options_ functions respectively. However the _xio_retrieveoptions_->_tlsio_mbedtls_retrieveoptions_ function don’t retrieved the _SU_OPTION_X509_CERT_ and _SU_OPTION_X509_PRIVATE_KEY_ client options, so they aren’t saved.
Before the MQTT connection, the client options previously saved are restored through the _GetTransportProviderIfNecessary_->_OptionHandler_FeedOptions_ function. Unfortunately the _SU_OPTION_X509_CERT_ and _SU_OPTION_X509_PRIVATE_KEY_ client options isn’t saved and so they can’t be restored.
For this reason during the TLS handshake my IoT device provides a null certificate and this invalidates the authentication procedure in IoT Hub.

At this point I would ask how can I fix this problem? Should I implement custom code inside the _tlsio_mbedtls_retrieveoptions_ function in order to retrieve the _SU_OPTION_X509_CERT_ and _SU_OPTION_X509_PRIVATE_KEY_ client options? Or is there some other function already ready?.

Thanks in advance.
Regards.
Matteo

title: Mqtt twin timeout cleanup
body:
Fixes #1210 which has additional details.

If a reported property ended up timing out, we got into states where we weren't cleaning it up in a timely manner. It would be destroyed on closing the client handle, but this could be well off into the future.

After this fix make it so in our timer queue, remove message after too much time has elapsed.

This corrects the initial fix - #1217 - which was subsequently reverted.  Initial fix for #1217 had a bug where it was not always setting message creation times in the messages.  This change takes initial #1217 but also renames some variables so message time creation is more obvious, consolidates how we create these messages into more common code paths, and sets the Unit Test clock so that it starts at 30 minutes (instead of 0) to flush out timer-not-initiated type issues.

body:

title: Exception while closing gateway
nodejs_simple_sample does not save data to IoT Hub
body:
Hi,

I have noticed that the sample does not upload data to IoT Hub. I figured this out by using the Device Explorer tool and monitoring the device which I used to execute the sample.

I particular, I noticed that the `Message` object is being created with empty data on this line:
```js
var m = new Message(message.content ? message.content.buffer : []);
```

Replacing this with the following solves the problem:
```js
var m = new Message(JSON.stringify(message.content));
```

title: segmentation fault in Java binding's Module_Start
body:
Hi team,
thank you for great work and quick response!

I saw segmentation fault (or access violation in Windows) from `Gateway_CreateFromJson`. The debugger said that the exception had been thrown from jvm.dll which had been called https://github.com/Azure/iot-edge/blob/master/bindings/java/src/java_module_host.c#

### Environment

* Windows 10 x64 with CU
* Using NuGet package (https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.Azure.Devices.Gateway.Native.Windows.x64/)
   * I manually extracted the dll and pdb from the package's `runtime` folder to investigate.
* Oracle JDK 8u 131

### Additional information:

* My code calls `Broker#publish()` and wait for "response message" for request-response style messaging for initialization in `GatewayModule#start()`.
* When I commented out `Broker#publish()` call from `GatewayModule#start()`, the segfault looked disappear.
* As of our logging code in Java, `GatewayModule#start()` finished successfully.
* Another module sent messages to the Java module continuously.
* The debugger said that the invalid address is almost '0x270' and '0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF` once.
    * I failed to check call stack when I saw '0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF`. 

### Hypothesis

As far as I look, I found similar error in [Xamarin Android](https://bugzilla.xamarin.com/show_bug.cgi?id=13521#c17), it is race condition of `JNIEnv*`.
So, my hypothesis of this issue is race condition of `env` field of `MODULE_JAVA_DATA` as following:

1. The java host module initializes `JAVA_MODULE_HANDLE_DATA` as module data in [this line](https://github.com/Azure/iot-edge/blob/master/bindings/java/src/java_module_host.c#L116).
2. The `module_worker` created from the broker, passing `module_info` in [this line](https://github.com/Azure/iot-edge/blob/master/core/src/broker.c#L373).
3. The `JavaModuleHost_Start` calls JNI's `AttachCurrentThread` and stores `JNIEnv*` in the field of `module` argument in [this line](https://github.com/Azure/iot-edge/blob/master/bindings/java/src/java_module_host.c#L473). I will call this thread as "main-thread".
4. The `module_worker` calles `JavaModuleHost_Receive` simultaneously, and it also calls JNI's `AttachCurrentThread` and then stores `JNIEnv*` in the field of `module` argument in [this line](https://github.com/Azure/iot-edge/blob/master/bindings/java/src/java_module_host.c#L407). This step overwrites `JNIEnv*` for "main-thread". I will call this thread as "worker-thread"
5. The `GatewayModule#start()` is finished, then ``JavaModuleHost_Start` calls JNI's `ExceptionOccurred` with overwritten. It causes segmentation fault.
    * If the "worker-thread" already called `DetachCurrentThread`, it is reasonable the `env` field was invalidated with jvm as `-1L`.

So I think that `JNIEnv*` should be stored in the local variable instead of "effectively global" variable in the struct, ant it may solve this problem. In fact, it just works in our testing environment.

Any idea?

Thank you for always.

title: [v2 request] Can modules be allowed to start when there is no network

This is perfectly fine. But, currently, if the gateway is started without internet connectivity, only the edgeAgent module is started. All other modules including the edgeHub are not even started. We are trying to migrate a v1 application to v2. The failure to start the modules will result in failure to even collect data and hence we will lose data.

Can v2 modules be allowed to start even if there is no internet connectivity? Please see that request is only to allow modules to start. There is no necessity the modules be allowed to connect to edgeHub. This module to edgeHub connectivity could be delayed till there is internet connectivity (until then SendEventAsync/IoTHubClient_LL_SendEventToOutputAsync will fail).

We are ok write code to persist data locally within modules when there is no connectivity. We are ok to live with a local copy of module twin when there is no connectivity.

title: Broken access to homedir/sockets causes service failure after installing Azure IoT Edge runtime on Raspbian
body:
Hi,

I hope you'll be able to help, perhaps I'm missing something obvious, but I figured I'll share the issue and the results of my troubleshooting.

Issue:
After following the default how-to guide ([here](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/iot-edge/how-to-install-iot-edge-linux-arm)) the `iotedge.service` fails to start.

Situation:
* Architecture/OS: Raspberry Pi 3 Model B+ freshly flashed with Raspbian Stretch (image dated on 2018-06-27); After flashing there was only: `sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade`, SSH server enabled, public SSH key copied
* The version of the runtime - I suppose the one the how-to points to is V1 (later in my troubleshooting I noticed `mcr.microsoft.com/azureiotedge-agent:1.0` and `mcr.microsoft.com/azureiotedge-hub:1.0` being used)
* Docker version:
```
Client:
 Version:      18.03.1-ce
 API version:  1.37
 Go version:   go1.9.5
 Git commit:   9ee9f40
 Built:        Thu Apr 26 07:17:20 2018
 OS/Arch:      linux/amd64
 Experimental: false
 Orchestrator: swarm
Server:
 Engine:
  Version:      18.03.1-ce
  API version:  1.37 (minimum version 1.12)
  Go version:   go1.9.5
  Git commit:   9ee9f40
  Built:        Thu Apr 26 07:15:30 2018
  OS/Arch:      linux/amd64
  Experimental: false
```

Description:
While troubleshooting (`journalctl -u iotedge --no-pager --no-full`) I noticed that by default the home directory for the IoT Edge Agent container is set to a non-existing `/tmp/iotedge` - running manually `sudo -u iotedge /usr/bin/iotedged -c /etc/iotedge/config.yaml` confirmed a _file not found_ error on `/tmp/iotedge`. I fixed that by setting `homedir` in `/etc/iotedge/config.yml` to a pre-existing directory.

At this point the service could make some more progress but it was still failing - this time with an `access denied` error. Checking the output of the manually ran service command showed that the issue was related to the socket files in `/var/run/iotedge/`.

I explored and experimented with the user IDs and permissions and noticed that by default:
* The IoT Edge Agent container (`mcr.microsoft.com/azureiotedge-agent:1.0`) is launched by a systemd process running as `iotedge` user & group
* The IoT Edge Hub container (`mcr.microsoft.com/azureiotedge-hub:1.0`) runs as an `edgehubuser` host user and internally has an `edgehubuser` with the UID set to 1000 and the GID set to 1000
* To further complicate the matters Raspbian's `pi` user has already UID 1000 & GID 1000
* It is possible to override the internal user of the IoT Edge Hub container by setting the value of _EdgeHubUser_ but that does not change the user with which the container itself is executed
* On the other hand attempting to override that with a setting in _Create Options_ (see contents below) on the Azure Portal is not effective either:
```
{
  "HostConfig": {
    "PortBindings": {
      ... [ default content of this key removed for readability] ...
      ]
    }
  },
  "Config": {
    "User": "root"
  }
}
  ```

Poking around further I used the following workarounds to make the service start:
* I created user & group "aliases" for both `iotedge` & `edgehubuser` (with UIDs & GIDs set to 1000) prior to installation (having multiple users with the same UID can lead to potential issues though)
* I relaxed the file/directory modes in `/lib/systemd/system/iotedge.mgmt.socket` & `/lib/systemd/system/iotedge.socket` (but this opens up a potential security hole)

I automated the whole installation process including workarounds with Ansible - see the repo [here](https://github.com/altermarkive/install-azure-iot-edge-on-raspbian-with-ansible)

I also noticed that others are also struggling with similar issues:
* [https://stackoverflow.com/questions/50244863/iot-edge-hub-exception-unable-to-start-kestrel](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/50244863/iot-edge-hub-exception-unable-to-start-kestrel)
* [https://mistywest.com/docker-more-than-a-cute-whale/](https://mistywest.com/docker-more-than-a-cute-whale/)

I don't know enough to suggest a solution (perhaps using `iotedge` user instead of `edgehubuser` could help) but maybe you will have an idea what is wrong. Of course, I'll be glad to provide any particular diagnostics/logs/outputs to help resolve the issue.

And thanks for reading the long post!

title: Edison build fails during config due to host linker being invoked instead of cross linker
body:
Using the Intel Edison toolchain and build corresponding script in "tools" subdirectory fails with 
**cannot find crt1.o: No such file or directory**
On analysis, during the CMake config steps where it tries to validate the C compiler, it correctly uses the Edison cross-compiler, but then the link step uses the host's linker (/usr/bin/ld)

That is obviously not correct behavior, and leads to the above error early in the build.

Adding this "hack" to the inteledision_c.sh script works around the problem:
**-DCMAKE_LINKER=/opt/poky-edison/1.7.2/sysroots/core2-32-poky-linux/usr/bin/i586-poky-linux-ld**

But CMake should behave when CMAKE_C_COMPILER and CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER are properly set to point to the compilers, which they are.

title: cmake drops build settings when descending into submodules - compiler checks fail
body:
I have prototyped a build script modeled after Intel Edison build script and it's corresponding environment setup script from Intel Edison toolchain.  When my build script starts, it sets up the environment, and calls cmake on build_root, the top level CMakeLists.txt performs the compiler checks and they pass.

`-- Check for working C compiler: /home/chris/mgc-cedar-minnowmax/embedded/codebench/bin/i686-pc-linux-gnu-gcc -- works`

But as soon as the build system descends into any submodule, these checks fail: (some debug messages() have been added)

`-- CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR:         /scratch/sandbox/azure-iot-gateway-sdk/deps/ctest`
`-- Check for working C compiler: /home/chris/mgc-cedar-minnowmax/embedded/codebench/bin/i686-pc-linux-gnu-gcc -- broken`

Upon further inspection, the variables that were set in the toolchain_file passed to cmake (using cmake's SET() directive) are blank, ie they have not been propagated into the submodule. Therefore, all my CFLAGS and LDFLAGS are effectively null, and the compiler check naturally fails.

What I know about cmake could fill a paragraph, and not more (well, actually I'm learning way more than I ever wanted to about cmake LOL!)

Where am I going wrong?
Note that I faced a similar failed compiler check running the Intel Edison example using the stock Edison toolchain and corresponding build script.  I documented that in https://github.com/Azure/azure-iot-gateway-sdk/issues/71

title: Add better error handling for non-Ascii/UTF-8 encoded JSON config files
body: Currently the `parson` lib seems to only supports `utf-8` and `ascii` encoded files for calls to `json_parse_file`, and the gateway just errors out with a generic "can't open file" message.  Given that many text editors and shells (e.g. PowerShell) will default to creating/saving files as "Unicode" (e.g. PowerShell's Out-File function, *which should be codepage 1252?*), it would be helpful to have the Gateway error out with a more useful message on file open issues that suggest encoding problems as a starting point for troubleshooting.  There should also likely be documentation that notes potential file encoding problems.

from grovepi import *

title: fix - firmware bugs for version 1.3.0
body:
### Taken out of the documentation

- Fixed synchronization bugs which led to very small IO rates

    - Also caused values to overlap on other ports [#412](https://github.com/DexterInd/GrovePi/issues/412)
    - Caused I2C errors when functions were called with no delay between them [#409](https://github.com/DexterInd/GrovePi/issues/409)

- Small refactorization of the code to something slightly better
- Fixed the dust sensor [#408](https://github.com/DexterInd/GrovePi/issues/408)
- Mitigated abnormality caused by the Raspberry Pi not supporting clock stretching on the I2C [#411](https://github.com/DexterInd/GrovePi/issues/411)
- Debugged and sped up the rate of acquisition of the DHT sensor [#418](https://github.com/DexterInd/GrovePi/issues/418)
- Add IR receiver functionality for any remote control and fix inherent issues with the library [#416](https://github.com/DexterInd/GrovePi/issues/416)
- Add option to set the flow meter and the dust sensor on different ports other than D2 [#421](https://github.com/DexterInd/GrovePi/issues/421)
- Added documentation -> [Preview Docs while it's still hot](https://robertlucian.github.io/GrovePi)

title: feature - add interrupts on all pins (release 1.4.0)
body:
This PR comes with 2 significant improvements to the GrovePi for version 1.4.0:

- Add support for setting up interrupt events on each digital port of the GrovePi, thus breaking the limit of just two available hardware interrupts [#446](https://github.com/DexterInd/GrovePi/pull/447)
- Enable the Grove Dust Sensor, the Grove Encoder and the Grove Flow Meter to work on any digital port of the GrovePi and support 7 or 3 or respectively 7 devices at the same time [#447](https://github.com/DexterInd/GrovePi/pull/446)

Along with these 2 improvements, the following changes were also made:

- Update documentation to reflect the newest changes.
- Curate root README to a slimmer version of it and add badges for the docs and license as an attempt to make the documentation popup easier.
- Update example programs for the aforementioned devices.
- Fix broken images in the documentation.

title: Bug in routing
body:
From express/server.js - you set the routes like
'/db' - routeDatabase
'/device' - routeDevice
'/' - routeDeviceRegistration

'/db/search' for device search
'/db/{0}' where device definition

'/device/xxx' - device discovery/set/get values

'/xxx' - adapter subscription

The problem really occurs with the last one - where 'xxx' is defined as '/:adapterName/yyy'

What if I was very bad and decided to name my adapter "db" or "device"?!?  Routing would get really screwed up since I was able to match a different route.  Same goes if you change the device ID to a string - then I could have a device id of "search" and screw that part up.

The routes should be more explicit - something like

title: "sudo" is not available for root user in docker container
body:
**Hi!**

and thank you for publishing your code!
I tried the application to get started with docker an get following exception:
```
Exception in thread Thread-10:
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.7/threading.py", line 917, in _bootstrap_inner
    self.run()
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.7/threading.py", line 865, in run
    self._target(*self._args, **self._kwargs)
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.7/site-packages/amazon_dash/listener.py", line 84, in execute
    result = self.execute_instance.execute(root_allowed)
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.7/site-packages/amazon_dash/execute.py", line 167, in execute
    output = execute_cmd(cmd, self.data.get('cwd'))
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.7/site-packages/amazon_dash/execute.py", line 58, in execute_cmd
    p = subprocess.Popen(cmd, cwd=cwd, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE)
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.7/subprocess.py", line 756, in __init__
    restore_signals, start_new_session)
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.7/subprocess.py", line 1499, in _execute_child
    raise child_exception_type(errno_num, err_msg, err_filename)
FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'sudo': 'sudo'
```
I think the last message ``No such file or directory: 'sudo': 'sudo'``is the key. Everytime you log in or running a docker image, you are the user _root_ inside of the running container. An _root_ doesn't know the command ``sudo``:

https://github.com/Nekmo/amazon-dash/blob/96e5493f1ea61a4bb014bd52f367985cf987f031/amazon_dash/execute.py#L48

Is root really needed in this case?

devices:

    name: Kitchen button 1

title: [bug] Device is re-added to HA after changing name/location
body:
**Version**

Build/Run method
- Docker
- ~PKG~
- ~Manually built (git clone - npm install - npm run build )~

Zwave2Mqtt version: 2.0.6
Openzwave Version: ? (don't know which is used in Docker image)

**Describe the bug**
When using Home Assistant discovery both the `identifier` of the device as the `unique_id` of the entity are based on the location and name of the device. This means that if you rename (or "move"/change location) a device that the device will be rediscovered in Home Assistant as the `identifier`/`unique_id` changed. So persistent ids must be used, this most likely could be the node id which will be unique in the network.  Preferably prefixed with something else (either some unique identifier of the Z-Wave network, or something like the MQTT prefix). This so the id will also be unique when you're running multiple instances of Zwave2Mqtt / having multiple ZWave networks. So the `identifier` of the device will then be some prefix with the node id, and the `unique_id` of the entity will then be the same (prefix + node id) but having the ValueID (I believe it's called) appended to it, which already is the case.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
I'm not sure if these are the proper steps, but I believe they are
1. Make sure you have Home Assistant discovery enabled
2. Check that the device is also shown in Home Assistant (so auto discovery works)
3. In Zwave2Mqtt change either the location, or name, of one of the devices/nodes
4. Restart Zwave2Mqtt / change settings and apply them (this will re-send the Home Assistant discovery messages)

**Expected behavior**
When checking Home Assistant again there still is only one device shown. But instead two devices are shown, one for the node were all entity ids etc have the old name/location, and one where the entity ids etc have the new name/location.

**Additional context**
Changing this behavior would be a backwards incompatible change as after an upgrade all devices a user has will be rediscovered by Home Assistant (because of the new `identifier` for the device and `unique_id` of the entity). But this at last makes sure that the same device will never be rediscovered (/show up twice, and one being "dead"). But I believe that's acceptable, and Home Assistant already has done changes like such many more times, where the automatically generated entity ids are changed after an upgrade to have more consistent and reliable ids from then on so they never have to change again. Furthermore the automatically generated entity id can still be changed in Home Assistant so the user doesn't have to use those awkward names anyway (when changing them manually) and other integrations, like zigbee2mqtt also use those kind of "random numbers" as unique id and thus generated entity ids (zigbee2mqtt does use the serial of the device)

```
  <!-- COMMAND_CLASS_SWITCH_MULTILEVEL. This class is in the list reported by the device, but it does not respond to requests -->

```

Zwave2Mqtt version: 2.1.1
Openzwave Version: 1.6.0

**Describe the bug**
Double click button on LogicHome ZHC5010 not published correctly to MQTT.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Double click on any of the four buttons on a LogicHome ZHC5010 switch. 
2. This should send a central scene event with scene id for the button double activated and an key attribute of 3. 
3. Verify messages published to MQTT. Only a single message is published for command class 91 and the value is Inactive. 

**Expected behavior**
I would expect two messages published to MQTT. One with value "double click activated" and one with value "Inactive". 

**Additional context**

body:
**Version**

Openzwave Version: 1.6
Home Assistant 0.106.4
Yale YD-01-CON + Yale Zwave module 2 a.k.a Keyless Connected (YD-01-CON) (0x0001) by Assa Abloy 

**Describe the bug**
Home Assistant autodiscovered lock stopped working after zwave2mqtt update from 2.2.0 to 3.0.0

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Install / Update zwave2mqtt 3.0.0
2. Go to Home Assistant and try to Unlock/Lock. Lock will remain in "unlocked" state. Lock does not respond to commands

**Expected behavior**
Locking and Unlocking should operate the lock. Status should be reflected in Home Assistant

**Additional context**
This seems to be related to the attempt to fix lock discovery changes in Home Assistant 0.104+ - https://github.com/OpenZWave/Zwave2Mqtt/issues/203

**Workaround**
Tweaking the discovery json payload in Z2M > [Lock Configuration] > Home Assistant - devices fixes the issue and restores the lock functionality.

1. Quote true/false value around lock state booleans
Replace
```
    "state_locked": true,
    "state_unlocked": false,
```
With
```
    "state_locked": "true",
    "state_unlocked": "false",
 ```
2. Add payload_(lock|unlock) booleans as Home Assistant sends "LOCK" "UNLOCK" json payloads by default which seems to be ignored by Z2M. 

```
    "payload_lock": "true",
    "payload_unlock": "false",
```

After changes, discovery payload should look like this:
```
discovery_payload": {
    "command_topic": "[prefix_topic]/2/98/1/0/set",
    "state_locked": "true",
    "state_unlocked": "false",
    "payload_lock": "true",
    "payload_unlock": "false",
    "value_template": "{% if value_json.value == false %} false {% elif value_json.value == true %} true {% else %} unknown {% endif %}",
...
```

body: **Version** Got this bug in version in the latest stable and the current head. Steps:~ -add a new node -Choosing in the UI the controller option "Add node", cancel the secure option -Including the node by pressing the including option on the node -The node is added successful The new node is displayed in the list but with an empty type and product. title: [bug] GE Fans show up as light switches
body:
Build/Run method:
- [x] Docker
- [ ] PKG
- [ ] Manually built (git clone - npm install - npm run build ) 

Zwave2Mqtt version: 2.0.1
Openzwave Version: 1.4.1

**Describe the bug**
GE fans show up as lights in hass rather than fans (see image below):

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/11232787/61327783-b1931080-a7e7-11e9-9599-2db960f541ed.png)


The zwave protocol is using command class 38, which is supposed to be reserved for lights, so this likely needs to be fixed using a manual hard-coded approach. Maintaining a list of anomalies might be a good idea.

So far, I've seen this issue with the following device ids:
99-12340-18756
99-12593-18756

The configuration for the fans can be found here:
https://github.com/OpenZWave/open-zwave/blob/master/config/ge/12724-dimmer.xml

**Version**

Build/Run method

- [ ] PKG
- [X] Manually built (git clone - npm install - npm run build )

**Describe the bug**
Split of from #23, devices now appear correctly from a cold start!

body:
**Version**

- [ ] PKG
- [x] Manually built (git clone - npm install - npm run build ) 

Zwave2Mqtt version: master @ 20190805
Openzwave Version: 1.6.848

**Describe the bug**
Once of the devices I have is missing configuration in OpenZwave, while in the progess of writing a config file for it. I noticed values of type`short` are not handled properly.

**To Reproduce**
Per the manual, parameter 10 should be `short`:
https://manuals.fibaro.com/content/manuals/en/FGWOEF-011/FGWOEF-011-T-EN-v1.0.pdf

![param10](https://imgur.com/PXCOp6e.png)

```xml
    <Value type="short" index="10" genre="config" label="LED frame - power limit" value="36800" min="500" max="36800" size="4">
      <Help>This parameter determines maximum active power. Exceeding it results in the LED frame flashing violet. Function is active only when parameter 11 is set to 8 or 9.
500-36800 (50.0-3680.0W, step 0.1W) - power threshold</Help>
    </Value>
```

With `short` (above) it shows up as a negative value, when I switch to `int` (below) it shows up correctly with the default value of '36800'

```xml
    <Value type="int" index="10" genre="config" label="LED frame - power limit" value="36800" min="500" max="36800" size="4">
      <Help>This parameter determines maximum active power. Exceeding it results in the LED frame flashing violet. Function is active only when parameter 11 is set to 8 or 9.
500-36800 (50.0-3680.0W, step 0.1W) - power threshold</Help>
    </Value>
```

I think it might be a signed vs unsigned issues here, not sure if is in zwave2mqtt or in node-shared-openzwave. But accoriding to https://github.com/OpenZWave/open-zwave/wiki/Adding-Devices a `short` is the correct type to use as it more closely matches the range. 

```
o int - A integer can represent a number from 0 to 4294967295
o short - A Short can represent a number from 0 to 65535
```

**Expected behavior**
Values of type short to be disaplyed correctly.

**Additional context**
n/a

We're facing provisioning issues of SparkFun Blynk Board from iOS devices. From the logs it is seen as the board just can't connect:
```
SSID: freud

Host: qa.blynk.cc
Port: 8442
Connecting to qa.blynk.cc
Connecting to: freud
..............
Timed out connecting to WiFi.
```
I've noticed, that in such case, the iPhone is still connected to board's WiFI AP (e.g. "BlynkMe-BBYR"). This seems to be an issue.

This is not the case with Android, because Android drops connection to board after sending `config` http request. Unfortunately, there is no way to do the same on iOS.

As experiment, we've tried to provision board from Android without explicitly dropping connection to it after `config` http request. The result was the same as on iOS: board couldn't connect to instructed WiFi network.

title: Request queuing multiple downlink packets close together causes duplicate fCnt numbers
body:
### Is this a bug or a feature request?
Bug

### What did you expect?
When using the /api/devices/{devEUI}/queue POST API with requests very close together, the downlink packets that are queued up should each get different fCnt numbers. The 'getting' of the next fCnt number and saving the record needs to be wrapped in a transaction so that no two queued packets get the same fCnt number.

### What happened?
When calling /api/devices/{devEUI}/queue POST from another app to queue up multiple downlink packets at the same time / very close together, some packets are being given the same fCnt.

This causes ERROR webhooks to be sent for the second packet when all the packets get transmitted next time the end device checks in (class A)

            resp_json = await resp.json()

            # Make some arbitrary data for the packet payload

title: 6LBR+RPi Crashing with large number of CC1310 nodes
body:
I'm experiencing an issue with 6lbr where the router crashes randomly when there are over 30 nodes in range. 

My setup is:
- One Raspberry Pi with a CC1310 based slip-radio as a BR running 6LBR 1.4.1
- 40 CC1310 based nodes running the latest Contiki commit with the `hello-world` example (only sending network maintenance data, no application data packets)

All nodes are positioned within 5 meters of the BR and connect directly to it (don't mesh through other nodes). Up to 30 nodes on the network works fine, all OK on the 6LBR dashboard and always pingable.  I've run this for a few hours without issue.

Once I start to add more nodes on the network the dashboard will crash at some random time after startup.  Once crashed, the dashboard will be unreachable, 6LBR will not be pingable and none of the nodes will be pingable.  However, `tail`ing the 6lbr.log file shows no error and packets apparently continue to be received and transmitted by the slip radio (`wireless_input` and `wireless_output` messages still continue to appear).

The crash seems to happen more quickly with more nodes.  (e.g. 35 nodes will take up to a minute minute to crash, 40 nodes will crash within the first 30 seconds)

body:

https://github.com/cetic/6lbr/blob/develop/examples/6lbr/platform/native/6lbr-conf-native.h#L116

It should check for:
```
__BYTE_ORDER__ == __ORDER_LITTLE_ENDIAN__

Rather than:

__BYTE_ORDER__ == __LITTLE_ENDIAN__
```

Source:
https://gcc.gnu.org/onlinedocs/cpp/Common-Predefined-Macros.html

I expect this is a copy paste error. The check for big endian is correct.

Thanks!

title: First packet towards an Ethernet new neighbour contains RPL HBH extension header
body: The first packet towards an Ethernet new neighbour (the packet that has triggered a NS/NA handshake) contains RPL Hop-by-Hop extension header. Because of that extension header, the packet is dropped by the host. This explains why sometimes the connexion towards 6LBR seems to hang but is fine when we refresh the page.

title: Neighbor cache can only hold one IP per link local address
body:
Hello,
I could not manage to set up 6lbr in SMART_BRIDGE mode (develop branch) on a Raspberry Pi to reach IP addresses NDP_Proxied IPs from docker containers on a host in my network.

This led me to take a look at the source and I was surprised to see, that the IPv6 neighbor cache implemented in `core/net/ipv6/uip-ds6-nbr.c` is uniquely indexed on the link local address.
In my understanding it should be very well possible to have multiple IP entries for the same link local address in an IPv6 neighbor cache. Or am I mistaken? In fact, `ip -6 neigh` yields lots of duplicate lladdrs for me and seems to be just fine with it.

This limitation already becomes a problem when you have hosts with Privacy Extensions enabled on your network, since they will configure two IP addresses but only one of them can ever be stored by 6lbr at the same time - an issue I have also encountered already when trying to reach my dev machine from 6LoWPAN.

title: tcpip_icmp6_call( ) problem in tcpip.c
body:
Hi Everyone,

I was recently having issues running my 6LBR implementation for long periods of time while connected to the internet. 

In the file, tcpip.c, there is a function tcpip_icmp6_call, which has a “XXX hack” message.

It seems as though for internet-enabled applications (as in the ping6 example), the icmp6_new function is called with NULL to initialize the uip_icmp6_conns structure.

However, after some amount of time, the memory used by “uip_icmp6_conns” is overwritten, causing the line: 

```
           “process_post_synch(uip_icmp6_conns.appstate.p, tcpip_icmp6_event, &type);” 
```

to throw a hard-fault on the MCU when an icmp6 message is received from the internet (i.e. NDP).

I have found that this is because “uip_icmp6_conns.appstate.p” is not a static object. When it is used properly, it points to a process and all that process’ properties. When this pointer’s target has been overwritten, the “process_post_synch” function fails, since the process it calls is some arbitrary memory location, not a process at all.

My solution is to move the declaration of uip_icmp6_conns from uip6.c to the top of tcpip.c, and add the “static” declaration modifier.

i.e. globally declaring the variable as:

```
            static struct uip_icmp6_conn uip_icmp6_conns;
```

instead of: 

```
            struct uip_icmp6_conn uip_icmp6_conns;
```

at the top of tcpip.c (the only file that uip_icmp6_conns is used in).

Additionally, in uip.h, the extern declaration of uip_icmp6_conns should be removed, since it is not even used in uip.h.

With uip_icmp6_conns set as a global static structure in tcpip.c (the only file in which it is used), the memory it uses will never be overwritten during the lifetime of the program, and therefore, when the internet-enabled application receives an icmp6 message such as an NDP handshake it will be able to run the appropriate process.

I have implemented this on my 6LBR and apparently eliminated the issues causing the hard-faults.

Thoughts?

Jordan

title: Handling Override off->on when triggered by EC
body:
## Description
It's possible that I'm misunderstanding the expected behavior, but I'm not sure the overrides are behaving properly. 

## Configuration
```yaml
entity_controller:
  closet:
    sensor: binary_sensor.0x00158d0003cc4255_occupancy
    entity: light.shelly1_2c76fa_relay_0
    sensor_type: duration
    delay: 30
    overrides:

1. Trigger motion sensor (light turns on)

EC stops changing the state; the light that was on remains on forever.

When playing around with AMQP 0.9.1 Connections, i found a bug in the reconnect mechanisms of Ditto.

If the AMQP broker (to which a connection is pointing) is unreachable for a while, Ditto will try to reestablish the connection and finally succeed when the broker is reachable again.

title: Sending responses to Azure Service Bus via AMQP 1.0 fails after some time
body:
When connecting to [Azure Service Bus](https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/services/service-bus/) via AMQP 1.0 from Ditto's connectivity service, after some time the Azure Service Bus seems to close the AMQP link (the connection stays open) or seems to no longer accept new links.
From that point on no responses can be sent to that AMQP address.

This was observed for *responses*. The *commands* are still received via another AMQP address - a "reply-to" address was specified for those commands via AMQP header, to which the response is sent.

Following log occurs in the log:
```
org.eclipse.ditto.services.connectivity.messaging.amqp.AmqpPublisherActor: Failed to send JMS message: [IllegalStateException] The MessageProducer was closed due to an unrecoverable error.
```

Maybe the Ditto connectivity creates too much links (e.g. when each "reply-to" is a new address, e.g. a UUID) so that Azure Service Bus prevents adding new ones.

title: closed AMQP 1.0 consumer after idle timeout is not restored
body:
Azure Service Bus has the behavior that idle AMQP 1.0 links are closed after ~10 minutes of idle timeout.

We get following log message and afterwards the AMQP 1.0 Azure Service Bus connection is in a strange state:
```
Consumer <org.apache.qpid.jms.JmsMessageConsumer@3b8f105d> closed due to JmsConnectionRemotelyClosedException: The connection was inactive for more than the allowed 120000 milliseconds and is closed by container '...'. [condition = amqp:connection:forced]
```

"Strange" because: after that message we get following messages:
```
May 23rd 2019, 06:56:14.973 Session closed: org.apache.qpid.jms.JmsSession@3230bc47 - Unknown error from remote peer
May 23rd 2019, 06:56:14.975 Connection interrupted: amqps://<...>.servicebus.windows.net:5671?amqp.saslMechanisms=PLAIN&transport.trustAll=true&transport.verifyHost=false
May 23rd 2019, 06:56:16.229 Connection restored: amqps://<...>.servicebus.windows.net:5671?amqp.saslMechanisms=PLAIN&transport.trustAll=true&transport.verifyHost=false
```

The last 2 messages repeat themselves each second.

We could/should react on `org.eclipse.ditto.services.connectivity.messaging.amqp.AmqpClientActor.StatusReportingListener#onConsumerClosed` and restore the connection.

What also can be seen: the default JMS client timeout seems to be 120s (see error message above) - we should increase that to at least 5 min.
Azure Service Bus' timeout seems to be ~9-11 minutes.

I'm not sure why this only happens on Service Bus - as for Eclipse Hono we also have consumers which are "idling" 2 minutes. Maybe the AMQP endpoint does however keep them open infinitely.

@kaizimmerm : could you please have a look on this?

body: A cancelable wasn't checked before canceling.

title: When hitting a (valid) URL while not logged in, user is redirected to login page over http
body: When hitting a (valid) URL while not logged in, user is redirected to login page over http, even if the original request has been done over HTTPS. It does not seem to be a problem on bluemix, but e.g on Predix, the unsecured http access is simply not enabled, so the redirect would need to use the same protocol to prevent this defect.
