title: [CVE-2019-10240][SECURITY] Releases are built/executed/released in the context of insecure/untrusted code
body:
[CWE-829: Inclusion of Functionality from Untrusted Control Sphere](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/829.html)

The build files indicate that this project is resolving dependencies over HTTP instead of HTTPS. Any of these artifacts could have been MITM to maliciously compromise them and infect the build artifacts that were produced. Additionally, if any of these JARs or other dependencies were compromised, any developers using these could continue to be infected past updating to fix this.

This vulnerability has a CVSS v3.0 Base Score of 8.1/10

* https://github.com/mveytsman/dilettante

### MITM Attacks Increasingly Common

* [Comcast continues to inject its own code into websites you visit](https://thenextweb.com/insights/2017/12/11/comcast-continues-to-inject-its-own-code-into-websites-you-visit/#) (over HTTP)

### Source Locations

- https://github.com/eclipse/hawkbit/blob/7870f9f87f12c047a3ee818fb0ea5edeb95bc432/pom.xml#L122-L127

### Original Report
https://bugs.eclipse.org/bugs/show_bug.cgi?id=544852

This was originally responsibly disclosed privately, but I was asked to make it public by @waynebeaton.

### Public Disclosure

#### Option 1: File for a CVE

A project maintainer for this project should probably file for a CVE number to inform the public about this vulnerability in the build for this project. The goal is to inform the public that there was a potential for published build artifacts to have been maliciously compromised in earlier releases.

If a maintainer on this project works for or is associated with a CNA, please have them file it with them:
[cve.mitre.org/cve/request_id.html](https://cve.mitre.org/cve/request_id.html)

Otherwise, an open source CVE should be filed for here:
[iwantacve.org](https://iwantacve.org/)

#### Option 2: Manually validate the release artifacts

If this project's build is [fully reproducible](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reproducible_builds). An alternative to filing for a CVE is to go back and build the earlier releases (with the HTTPS patch applied) to confirm the artifacts were not tampered when they were built. This can be done by comparing the hashes of the artifacts built locally with the ones published. If the hashes of all previous artifacts match those that are published, you can safely assume that the releases were not tampered with.

Again, this assumes that the build if fully reproducible and will require significantly more work.

title: Example device registry overwrites existing config when restarting in openshift
body:
The init container for openshift of the device registry copies the example configuration to the configuration folder using following command: 
`cp -u /etc/examples/example-credentials.json /var/lib/hono/device-registry/credentials.json && cp -u /etc/examples/example-tenants.json /var/lib/hono/device-registry/tenants.json`.  
However, this command overwrites the existing configuration. I think this is because the configmaps (example-credentials and example-tenants) are reacreated in the pod when it starts.  
This can be solved by replacing the -u flag with the -n flag resulting in following command:
`cp -n /etc/examples/example-credentials.json /var/lib/hono/device-registry/credentials.json && cp -n /etc/examples/example-tenants.json /var/lib/hono/device-registry/tenants.json`.  
From the [cp command page](http://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man1/cp.1.html):  
- -n, --no-clobber
              do not overwrite an existing file (overrides a previous -i
              option)
- -u, --update
              copy only when the SOURCE file is newer than the destination
              file or when the destination file is missing

The corresponding change in Hono is still missing. This leads to a `ServerErrorException` (with `HTTP_UNAVAILABLE`/"failed to connect") being thrown. It should be a `ClientErrorException` (`HTTP_UNAUTHORIZED`) instead.

title: Hono server continuously replenishes clients with additional credits
body:
When a client (e.g. a protocol adapter) connects to Hono in order to upload telemetry data or events it is provided with *credits* at the AMQP protocol level indicating to the sender (the client) how many messages the Hono server is willing to accept and process.
Hono itself gets credits analogously from the downstream container it is connected to (the Dispatch Router). However, Hono server erronously *adds* the credits it receives from the downstream container to the credits the client has been given which leads to a continuously increasing amount of credits being granted to the client.
Hono server needs to consider the (unused) credits already granted to the client when replenishing the client with credits received from the downstream container.

title: Fix encoding of OpenTracing span in AMQP messages
body:
My understanding is that the current encoding of OpenTracing information in AMQP messages could cause some issues it is not compliant with the AMQP spec.

About annotations the spec says (http://docs.oasis-open.org/amqp/core/v1.0/os/amqp-core-messaging-v1.0-os.html#type-annotations):

> The annotations type is a map where the keys are restricted to be of type symbol or of type ulong. All ulong keys, and all symbolic keys except those beginning with "x-" are reserved. Keys beginning with "x-opt-" MUST be ignored if not understood. On receiving an annotation key which is not understood, and which does not begin with "x-opt", the receiving AMQP container MUST detach the link with a not-implemented error. 

What seems to happen right now is that the `MessageAnnotationsInjectAdapter` is being used in combination with the `TEXT_MAP` format, which would directly inject `uber-trace-id` and `uberctx-*` into the message annotation map (see: `io.jaegertracing.internal.propagation.TextMapCodec`):

So it might happen, that a receiver simply closes this link when the annotation is present in the map.

The proposal would be to use something like `x-opt-opentracing-trace-id` and `x-opt-opentracing-ctx-` instead.

title: Fix cache handling in RegistrationClientImpl (concerning multiple gateways)
body:
Relates to #930, #1093:
In order to support the scenario of a device connecting via different gateways (not at the same time but alternating between gateways), the caching logic concerning `assertRegistration` requests has to be adapted.

Scenario:
- device `dev-A` connects via gateway `gw-1` => no cache hit, assertRegistration is invoked (last-via is updated), new cache entry with key `(assert, dev-A, gw-1)` is created
- device `dev-A` connects via gateway `gw-2` => no cache hit, assertRegistration is invoked (last-via is updated), new cache entry with key `(assert, dev-A, gw-2)` is created
- device `dev-A` again connects via gateway `gw-1` => **cache hit** => assertRegistration is NOT invoked and last-via is NOT updated - that is an error

Possible solution:
When writing the cache entry `(assert, dev-A, gw-2)` above, we have to delete all other cache entries concerning `assert` and `dev-A`.

EDIT: We shouldn't cache `RegistrationResult` objects representing devices with multiple `via` entries at all (see below).

title: Concurrency issue while authenticating devices with SHA encoded passwords
body:
`MessageDigestPasswordEncoder` is not thread-safe as it uses the same `MessageDigest` instance for all `matches()` calls. However since `UsernamePasswordAuthProvider` executes password check within different threads this leads to wrong results and thus to failed device authentications. 

Possible solutions might be
- Use new `MessageDigest` instance for every request
- Use separate `MessageDigest` instance per thread
- Add some locking to `matches()`

If creating of `MessageDigest` is not an expensive operation option 1 should be easy and legit to implement.

WDYT?

title: Delivery outcome is always 'accepted' in northbound side while sending commands
body:
A northbound application sends a command to a device. The protocol adapter (tried with _MQTT_ and _AMQP_ adapters) sends back a _rejected_ disposition. This information is not cascaded to the northbound application and thereby the application waits until the time out expires.   

`CommandClient` implementation uses `AbstractRequestResponseClient.sendRequest(Message message, Handler<ProtonDelivery> onUpdated)` to send the AMQP messages. And the delivery state is always received as _accepted_ irrespective of the disposition sent by the protocol adapters.

title: TTL unit assumed in seconds but AMQP 1.0 specification defines it in milliseconds
body:
The feature to set a default TTL for tenants is documented roughly in the example tenant json. [There a default TTL of `30` is set](https://www.eclipse.org/hono/docs/api/tenant/#tenant-information-format). I guess it was assumed that the TTL should be set in seconds as 30 milliseconds is most often not enough time to get a message through an AMQP network. However the AMQP 1.0 specification defines the TTL in milliseconds.
From the AMQP 1.0 specs:
>ttl time to live in ms
> Duration in milliseconds for which the message is to be considered “live”. If this is set then
a message expiration time will be computed based on the time of arrival at an intermediary.

So there are two possibilities:
* Either the unit in Hono has to be changed to milliseconds
* Or the TTL defined in the tenant json should be converted to milliseconds

In any case we should explicitly document the time unit which is used for the TTL.

title: Conceptual problem in connection handling
body:
To me it looks like we have a conceptual problem in the handling of connections to other services.

Every now and then, I recognized cases, where the adapters just don't become ready. And so I was digging into the issue. In the log you can then find something like:

~~~
2019-09-02T17:11:38.515Z INFO  [HonoConnectionImpl] stopping connection attempt to server [host: iot-device-registry.enmasse-infra.svc, port: 5671] due to terminal error
javax.security.sasl.AuthenticationException: Failed to authenticate
~~~

This "terminal error" will stop the client from trying to re-connect, and it seems like it never will re-try again. For as long as process is alive. So effectively, the process would be dead now.

My assumption was, that the pod would get cleaned up at some point, due to failing health checks. However that also doesn't seem to be the case. Taking a look at `org.eclipse.hono.service.AbstractProtocolAdapterBase`, you can see that the connections are checked in `registerReadinessChecks`, but not in the `registerLivenessChecks` method.

In that case, the "liveness check" would still always succeed.

Taking a look at the Kubernetes documentation (https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/configure-liveness-readiness-probes/):

> The kubelet uses liveness probes to know when to restart a Container. For example, liveness probes could catch a deadlock, where an application is running, but unable to make progress. Restarting a Container in such a state can help to make the application more available despite bugs.
> The kubelet uses readiness probes to know when a Container is ready to start accepting traffic. A Pod is considered ready when all of its Containers are ready. One use of this signal is to control which Pods are used as backends for Services. When a Pod is not ready, it is removed from Service load balancers.

It looks to me, as if the correct way to signal the "terminal error", is not through the "readiness" check, but through the "liveness" check instead.

Additionally, I would question the idea of a terminal error altogether. From what I see in our case, it has to do with an invalid service credential. So that problem will go away in a minute.

I think we should:

1. Trigger a liveness failure in case of a terminal error.
1. Event for a terminal error, allow to try again.

Fixing the first point is required to solve the issue. The second point would only allow the pod to recover itself, before it get killed by Kubernetes, and might be more of an improvement to the situation.

I also think we should fix this before 1.0.0!

title: Inconsistent validation of request payload in tenant registration operations.
Device management API credential example does not match scheme
body:
The _Device Management API Spec_ shows the following example request when making a _credentials PUT_: 
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1345394/66826379-9f428300-ef4c-11e9-911e-390bd8a39775.png)
https://www.eclipse.org/hono/docs/api/management/#/credentials/setAllCredentials

This does not match the scheme of `CredentialsSet` which defines that instead of a single credential an array of credentials should be given in the body.

title: Demo certs cannot be used for PEM file based TLS configuration
body:
The demo keys included in the demo-certs module are ECC based (not RSA) and the corresponding key and certificate PEM files not in PKCS8 format. This prevents them from being used for configuring the Hono server based on the `HONO_SERVER_KEY_PATH` and `HONO_SERVER_CERT_PATH` because vertx only supports RSA keys in PKCS8 PEM files.

It would therefore be better to use RSA based keys and use PEM files based on PKCS8.

title: HTTP adapter: "message consumer already in use" error for TTD requests
body:
The HTTP adapter may get into a state where each new telemetry/event request with a `ttd` param for a specific device will fail to create a command consumer. Internally, a `message consumer already in use` is thrown because there already is a command consumer from a previous request that didn't get closed. 
This only gets resolved when the AMQP messaging network closes the existing command consumer link or if the adapter gets restarted.

Looking at a heap dump of an adapter instance that got into this state revealed that the command consumer didn't get closed at a particular HTTP request when there was an error creating the AMQP message sender (`not connected`).

The Credentials API provides means to include arbitrary *client context* information in the request to the *get* operation. However, the MQTT adapter does not include the MQTT client identifier yet.

title: AMQP adapter: command response from gateway has wrong device id property
body:
When a northbound application sends a command to a device that is connected via a gateway, the device gets the command with a `reply-to` address that contains the gateway id instead of the device id.
When processing a command response message with that address, the AMQP adapter will then set the `device_id` property to the gateway id, not the device id.
This leads to the northbound application getting a command response message with the wrong `device_id` property value in such a scenario.

Using the `docker-compose.yml` from the Hono Getting Started guide causes authentication failure errors in the protocol adapters.

PR #208 addresses issues concerning wrong credentials and wrong auth host name.

However, after applying these changes, there is still a `Failed to authenticate` exception on protocol adapter startup. The reason isn't directly obvious to me. Log output of the Auth container appears to show no issue. In the Hono log there is this output:
````
09:29:22.801 [vert.x-eventloop-thread-1] DEBUG o.e.h.s.auth.HonoSaslAuthenticator - authentication failed: Timed out after waiting 1000(ms) for a reply. address: 1
09:29:22.863 [vert.x-eventloop-thread-1] DEBUG o.e.h.s.auth.HonoSaslAuthenticator - authentication failed: Timed out after waiting 1000(ms) for a reply. address: 2
````

title: Link counters are not decremented on client disconnect
body: If a protocol adapter disconnects (unexpectedly) from the Hono Messaging component, then the counters reflecting the upstream links and downstream senders are not decremented accordingly.
symptom: Device connection status issues, Disconnetion issues

title: OutOfMemoryError in MQTT adapter
body:
We get a OutOfMemoryError in the current version of MQTT adapter by using with docker stack on AWS.
The adapter is running without heavy load, 1-3 messages per minute.
For trace please see attachment:
[mqtt_oom.txt](https://github.com/eclipse/hono/files/1124928/mqtt_oom.txt)

title: MQTT adapter : keep alive doesn't work properly
body:
Due to a bug in the current MQTT server 3.4.2 version, the keep alive mechanism doesn't work properly and if a client doesn't send PINGREQ for the specified timeout, the server doesn't close the connection (waiting one and half such timeout) as defined by the MQTT 3.1.1 spec.
It's fixed in the future 3.5.0 release but we need a workaround today in the MQTT adapter.

title: Configuring device registry with sharedSecret that is too short causes no error
body:
If the device registry is run with a `hono.registry.svc.signing.sharedSecret` config value smaller than 32 bytes, there is no error being thrown and there is also no error in the log output.

The `IllegalArgumentException("shared secret must be at least 32 bytes")` thrown in `SignatureSupportingConfigProperties#setSharedSecret` seems to get caught somewhere.

title: Device Registry REST API: "enabled" field cannot be created/updated via POST/PUT request with urlencoded form data input
body:
When trying to create/update device registration data that has "enabled" set to "false", there is a 400 "bad request" response if the request was made with urlencoded form data input.

Example:
````
curl -i -X POST -d device_id=4711 -d enabled=false http://127.0.0.1:8080/registration/DEFAULT_TENANT
````

Internally there is a "ClassCastException: String cannot be cast to Boolean" in `BaseRegistrationService.getRequestPayload()`.

title: MQTT adapter doesn't send messages anymore after access token expiration
body:
After the access token expiration and reconnection to the messaging, device registry and credentials services, the MQTT adapter isn't able to publish messages downstream anymore.
It seems to me that the problem is reaching the Credentials service which doesn't return any information on getting credentials for the device.

title: MQTT adapter stops working as soon as AMQP credits run out
body:
Hey,

I think there's an issue with the current protocol adapter imeplementations.

I ran some load tests against the mqtt adapter and have some findings. I wonder if there are any configuration gotchas or something I might have missed.

Let's start with the test scenario:

6 AWS EC2 instances fire against the hono mqtt adapter using jmeter. Device authentication is enabled (pwd, sha-512). The hono cluster is rather small, 3 t2.medium nodes running kubernetes with 3 masters. 
One message has a 512 byte payload.

Everything works fine with a total throttled throughput of 200 messages/sec. (10 devices on 1 tenant)
As soon as I ramp up the load everything breaks (2000 messages/sec total from 10 devices and 2000 messages/sec from 200 devices). 

The problem as far as I can tell is: 

The mqtt adapter runs out of credits and closes the connection, see this log message:

VertxBasedMqttProtocolAdapter - cannot process message for device [tenantId: DEFAULT_TENANT, deviceId: loadTestClient-4, topic: telemetry/DEFAULT_TENANT/loadTestClient-4, QoS: AT_MOST_ONCE, cause: no credit available for sending message

Closing the conncetion also deletes the registration assertion which in turn makes it necessary to gather the registration data from the device registry service on the next message. The device registry gets overwhelmed by those requests (100k in a 10min test run in my case).
The messaging service does not receive any more messages the mqtt adapter failes to recover by itself. I would expect the system to behave differently: Drop new messages from the affected tenant, instead it tries to accept them and 'kills' backend services. 

Are there any problems with my setup as far as you can tell? Imo the behavior is not acceptable, as there is a hard limit on throughput that brings down a deployment and requires manual intervention.

I'm happy to provide more information, just give me some pointers if necessary

Cheers

title: HTTP adapter does not wait for downstream to settle and accept event
body: The HTTP adapter currently sends a 202 Accepted response to the client as soon as it has been able to forward a message downstream. This is correct behavior for telemetry messages but for events the adapter needs to wait for the downstream container to accept the message, i.e. it needs to wait for the message being settled with the *accepted* outcome.

title: Unble to publish MQTT messages
body:
Currently I am unable to publish MQTT messages. I think this issue was introduced by commit f7924edaf94dfc59532d2f6c6717dd79459ec1bd

The behavior is see is:

In the MQT adapter:
~~~
13:42:20.473 [vert.x-eventloop-thread-0] DEBUG o.e.hono.client.impl.HonoClientImpl - reusing existing message sender [target: telemetry/DEFAULT_TENANT, credit: 1]
13:42:20.474 [vert.x-eventloop-thread-0] DEBUG o.e.h.c.impl.TelemetrySenderImpl - message [message ID: TelemetrySenderImpl-422] rejected by peer: amqp:decode-error, malformed message 
~~~

And in the messaging service:

~~~
14:27:42.474 [vert.x-eventloop-thread-2] DEBUG o.e.h.m.HonoMessagingMessageFilter - message [TelemetrySenderImpl-300] has no content type
~~~

Now the check in `org.eclipse.hono.messaging.HonoMessagingMessageFilter.verify(ResourceIdentifier, Message)` requires the "content type" to be set:

~~~java
} else if (msg.getContentType() == null) {
  LOG.debug("message [{}] has no content type", msg.getMessageId());
  return false;
~~~

However the MQTT adapter only calls `org.eclipse.hono.service.AbstractProtocolAdapterBase.newMessage(String, String)` which will always provide `null` as content type.

body: When using the `createEventConsumer()` or `createTelementryConsumer()`methods on a `HonoClient`, the given `creationHandler` param should fail if the "attach" on the link fails (i.e. "detach" was received).

title: Propagate detach(close=false) back und allow reopen
body: As a receiver (link) in the Hono client a detach(close=false) needs to be answered the same way and later a open on this detached link need to be handled.

title: Protocol handlers may wait indefinitely on delivery updates
body:
When a protocol adapter sends a message downstream and Hono Messaging looses its link to the downstream AMQP Messaging Network, then the adapter may wait indefinitely for a delivery update because the senders created by `HonoClientImpl` do not set a time limit for waiting for a delivery update from the peer.
The adapters may thus leak memory when it accumulates stale delivery update handlers for such messages over time.

title: Grafana & influxDB are not getting deployed to Kubernetes/Openshift
HonoClient does only re-connect one time if no disconnect handler was provided in connect()
body:
Hi,

when I use hono client connect() without disconnect handler, re-connection just works fine for the very first time. But when client looses connection again there are no more re-connects. As JWT token expires every 10 minutes, hono clients configured like this do never re-connect after 20 minutes. This is also already mentioned #239 

Problem seems to be that when no disconnect handler is set, a handler gets set for reconnect that just invokes onRemoteDisconnect(): https://github.com/eclipse/hono/blob/6777c3e048a46d95c7985d441c7ac485eeb23858/client/src/main/java/org/eclipse/hono/client/impl/HonoClientImpl.java#L251-L269

Then during next re-connect, disconnect handler is not longer null and gets invoked, i.e. onRemoteDisconnect gets invoked. However, before invocation, connection gets set to null. But now failed connection and current connection (which is null now) are not the same and re-connect stops with a warn log statement: 

https://github.com/eclipse/hono/blob/6777c3e048a46d95c7985d441c7ac485eeb23858/client/src/main/java/org/eclipse/hono/client/impl/HonoClientImpl.java#L241-L249

Was there a reason why reconnect gets called with a disconnect handler, even when the user did not set one? Why not just invoke reconnect with null disconnect handler?

Thanks 
Daniel

title: MQTT adapter does not wait for accepted outcome when sending QoS 1 telemetry messages
body: The MQTT adapter is supposed to support clients publishing telemetry using (MQTT) QoS 1 as described in #508. The adapter indeed accepts telemetry messages published using QoS 1 but does **not** wait for the downstream AMQP message being accepted before issuing the MQTT PUBACK packet to the client.

title: http-client OSGi bundle doesn't allow instantiation of HonoClient
body:
AFAIK the only way to use HoneClient is to instantiate it via calling the direct constructor of org.eclipse.hono.client.impl.HonoClientImpl.
The org.eclipse.hono.client.impl, however, is not expored by the hono-client bundle. Only the org.eclipse.hono.client is exported.
So, the hono-client shall export org.eclipse.hono.client.impl (exporting impl, IMHO, is not recommended) or the org.eclipse.hono.client package shall provide meant to instantiate HonoClient without directly refer org.eclipse.hono.client.impl

title: Possible NP dereference of vertx in HonoClientImpl
body:
While looking into issue #500, I came across a potential NPE in the HonoClientImpl code. During instantiation, when the supplied `vertx` instance happens to be `null`, then `vertx.getOrCreateContext()` will thrown a NPE. This PR fixes that + apply constructor chaining (since both constructors looks pretty similar)

title: UsernamePasswordCredentials does not handle illegal Base64 strings

title: Set initial credits for Command Client in HTTP Adapter
body:
Currently an explicit `flow()` call is issued, which throws an exception if initial credits were not set to `0` in the setup.

This prevents calls to the http adapter with `hono-ttd` request param set and effectively leads to an unresponsed HTTP request.

Instead, the initial credits must be set to `1` and the direct call to `flow(1)` needs to be eliminated.

title: HTTP adapter leaks CommandConsumer instances
body:
The HTTP protocol adapter creates an instance of CommandConsumer for each request that includes the *hono-ttd* request parameter or header in order to receive a pending command for the device.
However, the CommandConsumer object created doesn't get GCed anymore.

title: Hono Server does not propagate a consumer's drain request upstream
body: When a consumer of telemetry data issues a drain request to Hono, the upstream producer(s) of the data should also be drained accordingly in order to prevent Hono from being *flooded* with data for which there is no consumer.

title: Caching of CommandConsumer make receiver links unusable
body:
After very few opened ProtonReceiver links the cache introduced in ebf7193cd708710c459c0345537bc264274d0df2
breaks `Command and Control` in the HTTP adapter.
The effect is that no receiver link will be opened anymore, since the cached version of the ProtonReceiver cannot be resurrected.

In any case, the caching of multiple ProtonReceivers (one per device) in memory would probably run into a large memory footprint and thus seems to be not desirable.

title: Services can be flooded with requests
body:
Pushing "too many" requests towards the Hono HTTP protocol adapter make it behave rather poorly. My expectation would be that Hono would still be able to handle the amount it can handle, but it looks to me as if the HTTP adapter mostly breaks down.

I tried to dig a little bit into this and I think I know one reason why this could be. Pushing HTTP requests  make the HTTP protocol adapter issues requests towards the device registry. If such a request cannot be handled in a specific amount of time (default 200ms) then it will be aborted and the HTTP request failed.

My understanding of the message flow is the following:

![request handling](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/202474/43648168-f907dc12-9739-11e8-9054-6c62f032e8d9.png)


<details>
title Request handling

Client->+Endpoint: Send request
note right of Endpoint: Validate Request
Endpoint->EventBus: Publish request
Endpoint-->-Client: Accept request

note over  Client: New credits are available

note right of EventBus: Process request
EventBus->Endpoint: Publish response

Endpoint->+Client: Send response
Client-->-Endpoint: Accept response
</details>

This would mean that the client (the protocol adapter) can push at a higher rate than the EventBus/RequestProcessor/Verticle can handle. Building up requests and slowing down the process.

That would also mean that, if requests stay longer than 200ms in some kind of queue on the EventBus side, then they would time out on the Protocol adapter side. So once your are in state that the EventBus queue is at a size that requests have to wait more than 200ms, then all requests will timeout. Which in fact means that no HTTP requests will be accepted any more.

A possible solution for that problem would be to delay the accept of the request until the response was send. The reject or release could still be sent directly after the validation of the request.

Another possible solution would be to get rid of the EventBus completely. As some initial profiler run showed that most of the time is spent processing EventBus messages.

This may as well relate to issue #735.

title: New Bcrypt credentials enables DoS attack on the protocol adapters.
body:
As per Credentials API, Hono is using Spring security for Bcrypt password encoding.

Spring security supports bcrypt password encoding with log rotations from 4 to 31, 10 being default (i.e:- 2^10 hash iterations). Once hashed, the log rotation used is part of the password like 

`$2a$21$LQdzaDSINBpHmYRiGEVtkOVt2GScZ6bPvEyoAIpiVIE6F4rviemdm`

where $21 represents the log rotation used. There is currently no max limit defined in Hono. If a user, say stores the password with higher rotation, then it could enable a DOS attack on the adapters.

I tested the time taken for `BCryptPasswordEncoder.matches` with higher log rotation on my laptop (Intel Core i7 - 2.7GHz 8 core, 32 GB RAM) it took

- 10 - 105 milliseconds
- 12 - 360 milliseconds
- 18 - 21 seconds
- 21 - 178 seconds
- 31 - more than 1 hour and I had to abort it.

Setting 31 as log rotation will definitely block the protocol adapters.

As a best practise, I would restrict the log rotation to 12 or 14, document them as part of credentials API and have this checked in 

org.eclipse.hono.util.CredentialsObject.hasValidSecrets()

title: DefaultFailureHandler expects response message to be set correctly
body:
The `DefaultFailureHandler` uses the status message of the request if the context has a status code set: https://github.com/eclipse/hono/blob/c947ae6be19e27e24938335c8b508a1f3fc331e2/service-base/src/main/java/org/eclipse/hono/service/http/DefaultFailureHandler.java#L73
but in some cases the status message was not yet set and the default message ("OK") is used: 
https://github.com/eclipse-vertx/vert.x/blob/6aafd1733bb82ef71a69675c4414c1a0210d7fcf/src/main/java/io/vertx/core/http/impl/HttpServerResponseImpl.java#L89
For example this is the case when using the Vertx AuthHandler which will fail the context but doesn't set a status message: 
https://github.com/vert-x3/vertx-web/blob/af922fb2b6b46ccbb18568ca5ac4123be8a33491/vertx-web/src/main/java/io/vertx/ext/web/handler/impl/AuthHandlerImpl.java#L193-L200

In this case when the authorization fails, the status will be `401` but with a body of `OK`.

Maybe the DefaultFailureHandler should defer the status message from the status code?

title: [#1781] Fix use of command response topic with device but no tenant
body:
This fixes #1781.
Fix use of command response MQTT topic with device but no tenant (`command//${device-id}/res/${req-id}/${status}`). Such a topic is to be used by authenticated gateways.
Also fixes integration tests - that topic wasn't used there.

title: [#1785] Fix gateway id getting set in reply-to address
body:
This fixes #1785.
The target device id instead of the gateway id has to be set in the reply-to address of a command message. Otherwise command response messages will get the wrong `device_id` property value.
AMQP integration tests now check for the correct property value.

title: Groups should not be assignable for non groupable permissions
body:
When granting permissions to a user or a role, it is always allowed to assign a group while, for some domain it doesn't make sense. For example the domain "broker" is not groupable hence the group field should not be assignable. Here is a first list of (currently) non groupable domains:
* Domain
* Account
* User
* Group
* Tag
* Role
* Access Info
* Access Token
* Credential
* Broker
* Device connection
* Device events
* Device lifecycle
* Device managements
* Job

title: Device management operations hide errors
body:
During a device management operation if the communication does not incur in TimeoutException or other communication-related errors but the device returns an error code while processing the message, no error code or error alert is returned to the caller of the device management operation.

So if you perform any operation in which the device does not respond 200 as responseCode the only way to see the device management operation result is to look at the DeviceEvent created.

It would be more appropriate that, if an error occurs, an appropriate exception si thrown to notify the caller.

title: `sys_housekeeper` table is not compatible with MySQL/mariaDB
body:
`sys_housekeeper` if your deployment is on mySQL with charset set to `utf8_unicode_ci`.

This is because MySQL/MariaDB has a limit of 767 bytes of length for the whole index. 
The field has a length of `255` and the charset `utf8_unicode_ci` uses 4 bytes per chars.

title: Allow creation of DeviceConnection as DISCONNECTED
body:
Currently is not possible to create a `DeviceConnection` with `status` set to `DISCONNECTED`. 
This is hardcoded in https://github.com/eclipse/kapua/blob/develop/service/device/registry/internal/src/main/java/org/eclipse/kapua/service/device/registry/connection/internal/DeviceConnectionDAO.java#L41

This means that if your application requires a 'pre-seeding' of a device connection you are required first to create the `DeviceConnection` and then update it as `DISCONNECTED`.

It would be easier to make this editable. Maybe we can set the `CONNECTED` status by default.

Given this, passwords should be unescaped when looking for a valid credential.

title: Lockout policy conflicts with Swagger UI
body:
Hi,

It is a very annoying and rare problem I have experienced, but I could not repeat until now. When I am using the Swagger UI and the Kapua WebConsole simultaneously, after switching from one to another I lose my authentication credentials, so I have to log in again. The problem is, that if I change the System Admin (kapua-sys) password, he could get locked out. It does not depend on whether the Lockout Service is enabled or not, or if it is how it is configured. The system admin gets locked out with the preset Lockout Service settings.

Note: The lockout happens instantly, you don't even have to type a wrong password...

Here is the test sequence:

1. Install Kapua and log in with _kapua-sys_
2. Create a child account ("c_account")
3. Enable infinite child users
4. **Disable Lockout service**
5. Create a new user of c_account (c_user, pass: new_password)
6. Grant him ALL permissions
7. **Change system admin password** (clicking change password in the top right corner)
[new pass: new_password]
8. Go to Swagger UI
9. Request authentication/user and log in with c_user/new_password (not with sys-admin)
10. Go back to web console (you will be dropped out after a few seconds)
11. Try to log in with kapua-sys/new_password
12. It will say that the account is locked contact System Administrator...

NOTE: I also observed some things which can be helpful
- As in my example the child account's user password and the system admin changed password was the same. (but I don't think that matters)
- The system admin has been locked out, however I still could use the child account's user
- The system admin was useless both in the web console and the Swagger UI
- The system admin lockout was resolved after a day passed from last login attempt (but I think that was just the default 10800 seconds of the Lockout Service)
- It **only** occured **when I changed the** system admin **password**
- Because of the long resolution time I couldn't run more experiment on this matter
- I cannot change the Kapua settings until I create a child account (the settings are grey)
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/26169252/37404990-ba40bf5a-2793-11e8-91cd-e92f455527eb.png)
- After I have a child account I switch to that account, go to settings, change back to kapua-sys, refresh, and THEN I can change the settings.

It was extremely frustrating the first time and now that I can recreate it and have fears using the web console and the Swagger UI simultaneously because of that. Thank you for your help.

title: service events - error during locator initialization
body:
#### Description 
The error occurs during the startup phase of the REST API. The log reports the following:

> Caused by: com.google.inject.ProvisionException: Unable to provision, see the following errors:
>  
> 1) Error injecting constructor, java.lang.NullPointerException
>   at org.eclipse.kapua.service.user.internal.UserServiceImpl.<init>(UserServiceImpl.java:72)
>   while locating org.eclipse.kapua.service.user.internal.UserServiceImpl
>   at org.eclipse.kapua.locator.guice.KapuaModule.configure(KapuaModule.java:121)
>   while locating org.eclipse.kapua.service.user.UserService
>     for field at org.eclipse.kapua.service.user.internal.UserServiceModule.userService(UserServiceModule.java:27)
>   while locating org.eclipse.kapua.service.user.internal.UserServiceModule
>   while locating org.eclipse.kapua.commons.core.ServiceModule annotated with @com.

The error is due  to the fact that the list of service modules are retrieved (and instantiated) before completing the initialization of the locator (for the Guice implementation). The retrieve of the service modules triggers the initialization of some service implementations which in turn try to access the locator.

#### Expected behavior
Objects managed by the Kapua locator do not have to be created before the locator itself is completely initialized (for the Guice implementation). The solution is to defer the instantiation of any object until the locator is fully initialized.

title: Device Management - Missing `ConnectionStatus` check
body:
Hi all, 

we are currently missing a check on the `DeviceConnection.getStatus()` attribute.
When performing a device management operation we should check that the `Device` has a `DeviceConnection` and that this `DeviceConnection` has a `status` which is `CONNECTED`. 

Without this check any operation performed by `Job`s or REST API device management will end up in a operation executed which will always timeout.

Regards, 

_Alberto_

title: Device management - Missing existence checks
body:

When performing a device management operation we should check that the Device exists, otherwise in the processing we will end up in a `NullPointerException` since some methods extract data from the `Device`.

Regards,

Alberto

title: Filtering Through Kapa Not "Unified"
body:
For now, filtering is not "unified". For example, some of the fields require that searched string is exaclty the same as "target" string (e.g. Custom Attributes fields in Device filter), others require that a character entered is anywhere in the "target" string (e.g. Job name). Is this OK, or not? What is the proper filter operation? 

**_Connections:_**
**- Connection CLiend ID:** Finds match if character or string entered appears anywhere in Cliend ID
**- Conncetion Client IP:** Finds match if character or string entered appears anywhere in Connection Client IP

**_Devices:_** 
**- Device Client ID:** Finds a match if string of characters matches beginning of the target string (if a device's ID is "device123", Kapua will not find it, if users enters "evi" or "123", but will find if entered "d", "dev" or "devic")
**- Device Display Name:** Finds a match if string of characters matches beginning of the target string (if a device's Display Name is "device123", Kapua will not find it, if users enters "evi" or "123", but will find if entered "d", "dev" or "devic")
**- Serial Number:** / non-testable
**- IoT Framework Version:** String has to be complete match (e.g. KURA_3.1.1, not even "K" or "KURA" will suffice, user has to enter "KURA_3.1.1" into search field)
**- Applications:** Finds match if character or string entered appears anywhere in Applications field
**- Custom Attribute No. 1:** String has to be a complete match (e.g. if attribute is "device123", user has to enter "device123", "dev", "123", device12" will not work)
**- Custon Attribute No. 2:** String has to be a complete match (e.g. if attribute is "device123", user has to enter "device123", "dev", "123", device12" will not work)

**_Jobs:_**
**- Job Name:** Finds match if character or string entered appears in any job name

**_Tags:_**
**- Tag Name:** Finds match if character or string entered appears in any tag name

**_Users:_**
**- Username field:** Finds match if character or string entered appears in any username

**_Roles:_**
**- Role Name:** Finds match if character or string entered appears in any role name

**_Access Groups:_**
**- Access Group Name:** Finds match if character or string entered appears in any group name

**_Child Accounts:_**
**- Account Name:** Finds match if character or string entered appears in any account name
**- Account Organization Name:** Finds match if character or string entered appears in any organization name
**- Account Email:** Finds match if character or string entered appears any email name

title: Console - Data view metric filtering not working properly
body:
Looking at the code of the GwtDataServiceImpl it seems that the filtering by headers is not properly working.

It shows the only selected metric, but It does not add the datastore predicate (it should use the `metricPredicate`)  to the query.

[GwtDataServiceImpl:450](https://github.com/eclipse/kapua/blob/54f5bd4f9e7348372341de219d8d2ab53b67637f/console/module/data/src/main/java/org/eclipse/kapua/app/console/module/data/server/GwtDataServiceImpl.java#L450): header are passed and never added to the query

[GwtDataServiceImpl:469](https://github.com/eclipse/kapua/blob/54f5bd4f9e7348372341de219d8d2ab53b67637f/console/module/data/src/main/java/org/eclipse/kapua/app/console/module/data/server/GwtDataServiceImpl.java#L469):  header are passed and never added to the query again.

[KapuaGwtDataModelConverter:73](https://github.com/eclipse/kapua/blob/54f5bd4f9e7348372341de219d8d2ab53b67637f/console/module/data/src/main/java/org/eclipse/kapua/app/console/module/data/shared/util/KapuaGwtDataModelConverter.java#L73): header are used to extract specific metric from the message payload, but it could be that one of the extracted messages hasn't the requested metric.

The result is that you'll end up with empty cell in the result table, while the correct behaviour should be that the messages should be skipped from the results.

title: Paging Toolbars Freeze if User Constantly Refresh Pages

title: Kapua Reporting Locked User Because Of Password Expired Date
body: If we create a user with expired password, Kapua reports (when we are trying to login as this use) that "User has been locked. I propose three solutions: 1) If user sets Expiration Date for a Credential in the past, _Status_ (the "key" icon) or the _Lock Status_ should turn red. This introduces some security "risks" as potential attacker then knows that password has expired and user has not been actually locekd. 3) Changing the Kapua message to "User has been locked or password has expired. body:
**Describe the bug**
Using `XmlUtil.unmarshalJson()` to unmarshal a JSON string representing a `KapuaListResult` throws an exception:

```
javax.xml.bind.UnmarshalException: Line -1, Col: -1.
    Error message: 
Exception Description: Cannot add the object [org.eclipse.kapua.service.user.internal.UserImpl@486b35d5], of class [class org.eclipse.kapua.service.user.internal.UserImpl], to container [class java.util.Collections$UnmodifiableRandomAccessList].
Internal Exception: java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException
    Linked exception message:
Exception Description: Cannot add the object [org.eclipse.kapua.service.user.internal.UserImpl@486b35d5], of class [class org.eclipse.kapua.service.user.internal.UserImpl], to container [class java.util.Collections$UnmodifiableRandomAccessList].

- with linked exception:
[Exception [EclipseLink-6065] (Eclipse Persistence Services - 2.6.3.v20160428-59c81c5): org.eclipse.persistence.exceptions.QueryException
Exception Description: Cannot add the object [org.eclipse.kapua.service.user.internal.UserImpl@486b35d5], of class [class org.eclipse.kapua.service.user.internal.UserImpl], to container [class java.util.Collections$UnmodifiableRandomAccessList].
Internal Exception: java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException]
```

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Using REST API, get a JSON representing a `KapuaListResult` object (e.g. GET /users)
2. Try to unmarshal such JSON via `XmlUtil.unmarshalJson()`

title: Database schema: act_account table / parent_account_path length issue
body:
There is a possible inconsistency in the **act_account** table, specifically the **parent_account_path** field.
The current create script (**act_account_create.sql**) defines this field as a **VARCHAR(64)**. Given that there is no limit to the depth of sub-account creation this seems to be too short.
Specifically, this length is exceeded even with an account tree 3 levels deep. An example is as follows.
When creating 3 account levels, the resulting parent path is
'\1/-4796103609285693743/-4305601355848753009/-1017280879925618445'
Please note that this string is 65 characters long and as such it causes an JdbcSQLException.
As it looks it seems that this inconsistency was introduced when the old (and shorter) IDs were replaced with the new BigInteger (far longer) IDs.

title: Service events - uncorrect ServiceEvent stack handling on nested calls
body:
The ServiceEvent bean stack is not correctly managed by the ServiceEventScope. The end method cleans the stack regardless if there is more than one object in the stack.
So if a main event raises a child event, the end call of the child event will clean the ServiceEvent stack leading the end call of the main event to throw a KapuaRuntimeException.

To fix it the end call should check for the stack size before cleaning it from the ThreadContext.

title: Database schema: General issue with IDs
body:
There is a general issue regarding the ID fields in the database.
The table creation scripts define all IDs as BIGINT(21) UNSIGNED (i.e. **scope_id    BIGINT(21)  UNSIGNED NOT NULL**).
Nevertheless it is possible to create an ID from a negative integer (i.e. **new KapuaEid(BigInteger.valueOf(-1))**) and the database will not complain. Searching the database with such ID is also successful.
This is somewhat counter-intuitive, as the field definition seems to imply that IDs with negative values should be rejected by the database.

This bug doesn't allow to specify a different listening/raising address for the services contained in the same module.

title: Wrong Error Messages When user Does Not Have Proper Permissions
body:
This was originally planned to be part of solution for issue #1796 and PR that will fix it, but for fixing and testing reasons has been split to a new issue.
For now, Kapua's error messages when permissions are not sufficient is for example: "Device edit failed: User does not have permissions to perfrom this action. Missing permissions: device:write:xxxx:xxxxx".
The issue here is the first part, "Device edit failed", which is unnecessary, as user can persume that edit has failed, due to the error shown. 
Bellow there is list of scenarios where this happens. 

1. If user has no more Device:Delete permissions and tries to delete a device (Screenshot No. 1)
2. If user no longer has Device:Write permissions and tries to edit a device (Screenshot No. 2)
3. if user no longer has Device_management:Execute permission and tries to execute a command or start/stop a bundle (Screenshot No. 3)
4. If user no longer has Device_management:Write permission and tries to upload a Snapshot (Screenshot No. 4)
5. If user no longer has Device_Management:Write permission and tries to change device's configuration; For now, Kapua reacts as new changes are saved/discarded (flash, loading screen, refresh), but changes are not actually saved. It should be done as in Assets: if user does not have permissions any more and clicks anything, everything disables. (Screenshot No. 5)
6. If user no longer has Job:Delete permission and tries to delete a job Step (Screenshot No. 6)
7. If user no longer has Job:Delete permission and tries to delete a job (Screenshot No. 7)
8. If user no longer has Job:Execute permission and tries to start or restart a job (Screenshot No. 8)
9. If user no longer has Job:Delete permissions and tries to delete a Target (Screenshot No. 9)
10. If user no longer has Schedule:Delete permission and tries to delete a Schedule (Screenshot No. 10)
11. if user no longer has Tag:Delete permission and wants to delete a tag. Also here are two identical errors - this should be fixed also (Screenshot No. 11)
12. If user no longer has Credential:Delete permission and wants to delete a credential (Screenshot No. 12)
13. If user no longer has Credential:Write permission and wants to edit a credential (Screenshot No. 13)
14. If user no longer has Credential:Write permission and wants to unlock a credential (Screenshot No. 4)
15. If user no longer has Access_info:delete permission and wants to delete a role in users (Screenshot No. 15)
16. If user no longer has Access_info:write permission and wants to add a role to users (Screenshot No. 16)
17. If user no longer has Access_info:delete permission and wants to delete a permission in Users (Screenshot No. 17)
18. If user no longer has Access_info:write permission and wants to add a permission - here Kapua  returns wrong error ("Role assigning failed"), although we are assigning a permission in Users (Screenshot No. 18)
19. If user no longer has Domain:read permission and wants to add a permission in Users (Screenshot No. 19)
20. if user no longer has Domain:read permission and wants to add a permission to a Role - here Kapua returns wrong error ("Role assigning failed"), although we are assigning a permission to a Role (Screenshot No. 20)
21. If user no longer has Role:Delete permission and wants to delete a permission from a role(Screenshot No. 21)
22. If user no longer has Role:Write permission and wants to add a permission to a role - here Kapua returns wrong error ("Role assigning failed"), although we are assigning a permission to a Role (Screenshot No. 22)
23. If user no longer has Group:Delete pemission and wants to delete a group - also the problem here is that Kapua returns two identical errors - this should be fixed also (Screenshot No. 23)
24. If user no longer has User:Delete permission and tries to delete a user from account (Screenshot No. 24)
25. If user no longer has Account:Delete permission and tries to delete an account, Kapua reports that "its children have to be deleted first" (Screenshot No. 25)
26. Kapua reports that user does not have "Device_management_registry:read premission if user wants to see Device -> Packages tab if user fist has this permission and is then revoked. This should not happen, since this permission is not needed to see this tab (Screenshot No. 26).
27. If user no longer has Job:Write permission and wants to add Targets (Screenshot No. 27)
28. Is user no longer has Device:Read permissions and wants to refresh main Tag grid - Kapua should not return permission error for devices, if user is in Description tab (Screenshot No. 28)
29. If user no longer has User:Delete permission and wants to delete a Kapua User (Screenshot No. 29)
30. if user no longer has Group:Read permission and wants to add a permission (in Users or in Roles - Screenshot No. 30).
31.  Is user no longer has Device:Read permissions and wants to refresh main Group grid - Kapua should not return permission error for devices, if user is in Description tab (Screenshot No. 31)

**Testflow:**
1. Login as kapua-sys or any other user that has proper permissions
2. Go to Users, create a user (e.g. user0) and add all the necessary permissions to him (e.g. device:read and device:write)
3. From another browser login as user0, go to Devices tab and try to add/edit a device after the device:write permission has been revoked from first browser.

**Expected behavior**
First part of these error messages should be removed as it is logical that operation has failed, if Kapua returns error message.

title: Telemetry message published through Streams Api has a wrong clientId stored
body:
**Describe the bug**
Telemetry message published through Streams Api has a wrong clientId stored.
The clientId stored is coming from the internal Mqtt connection pool.  

**To Reproduce**
Publish message using Streams Api

**Expected behavior**
curl http://127.0.0.1:9200/index/message/_search?pretty should return:

"sent_on" : "2018-06-08T15:16:15.515Z",
"body" : null,
"captured_on" : "2018-06-08T15:16:15.515Z",
"client_id" : "client-id-set",
"timestamp" : "2018-06-08T15:16:15.515Z"
...

instead of

title: Add permission forward-ability
body:
Hi all,

we need to implement the feature of "forward-ability" of the permissions. 
This means that an account A with a child account B must be able to manage resources of the account B.

The logic would be that a user A of the account A that has per permission A has the same permission on the account B, as if user A has both A and B permission. 

To allow restriction of this behaviour a new flag on the permission will tell if the permission is forward-able or not. 

The current situation is that `kapua-sys` account can manage child account because it has `*:*:*:*` permission. But if a child account A of `kapua-sys` has another child account B, the A account will only be able to delete the account and not to create users/roles/etc on the account B.

Regards, 

_Alberto_

title: Liquibase script refactoring
body:
Hi all, 

while working on #583 I discovered something odd on Liquibase.
By default it uses absolute path name as a key to know if a file has been executed already or not. 
This means that If the same script is executed from a different directory Liquibase wouldn't be able to recognize that is has already been executed and try to execute it again.

There is a property to override this called `logicalFilePath`, which value is used as a key instead of the absolute path. This property must be added to all file with changeset to execute. 
I was not able to add it to the plan SQL file and I suspect that we have to convert them to XML|YAML|JSON format to be able to specify that property. 

BTW the current layout works fine for tests and demo deployment. It could be a problem in case of more complex usage.

Regards,

_Alberto_


EDIT: 
Documentation page of this property: http://www.liquibase.org/documentation/databasechangelog.html

title: Random QA tests failures
body:
Hi all,

after merging #583 some random test failures started to appear more frequently. We had already some random failures on qa tests but they were occasional.

After digging a bit I discovered that is a problem related to how Liquibase script are loaded and the fact that the Kapua Liquibase Client  is run from many different places concurrently. 

The KapuaLiquibaseClient was implemented to copy resources from the jar to a tmp directory and then execute it immediately. With the improvement contained on #583  all scripts gets copied and then executed. 

For the fact that KapuaLiquibaseClient is run from different places it can happen that the copied resources gets overwritten by another KapuaLiquibaseClient is executing them, with even more chance that now that apply of Liquibase scripts takes a bit longer.

I'll fix this making execution of Liquibase script `synchronized` as a simple patch.

Regards,

_Alberto_

title: Find another way to represent allowSelfEdit for service configuration
body: Currently services configuration uses the OSGi Metatype  `<Option>` to specify whether an account can modify a specified attribute or not. However such tag should be used to specify allowed options for a given attribute, more and less like the HTML `<option>` inside a `<select>`. We should find another way to specify `allowSelfEdit` and other properties we  could introduce in the future.

title: [Net] PPP password is not a (MetaType) Password
body:
Found in Kura 2.0.2. Not verified in Kura 2.1.0.

Typically passwords have ``Password`` type and they are base64 encoded in the dowloaded snapshot.
For example (password is "admin"):

```
<esf:configuration pid="org.eclipse.kura.web.Console">
    <esf:properties>
        <esf:property type="Password" name="console.password.value" encrypted="true" array="false">
            <esf:value>YWRtaW4=</esf:value>
        </esf:property>
    </esf:properties>
</esf:configuration>
```

The PPP password is different. It's a ``String`` (not a Password) and not base64 encoded.

```
<esf:property type="String" name="net.interface.ppp0.config.password" encrypted="false" array="false">
    <esf:value>password</esf:value>
</esf:property>
```

Not a big deal since the password is likely stored in clean in the ppp pap/chap scripts...

title: [Wires] Asset configuration is not updated after a ChannelDescriptor change.
body:
If a BaseAsset instance is attached to a driver, and the channel descriptor of a driver is changed by adding new properties (for example by installing a new version of the driver with a different channel descriptor), the configuration of the existing Asset will not be updated.

The expected behaviour would be that the old configuration of the Asset gets merged with the default values of the new properties (if any) obtained from the channel descriptor.

body:
Setting the `connect.retry-interval` to 0 seems to work until reboot.
After a reboot, the DataService component starts continuously to try to activate, determining the impossibility to use the default cloud service and all the related stack.

title: [Artemis] MQTT clients fail to reconnect after the broker is restarted
body:
Stopping and restarting embedded Artemis broker instances might cause a previously connected client to fail to reconnect.
Steps to reproduce:
1. Enable the **Simple Artemis MQTT Broker** or the **ActiveMQ Artemis Broker**.
2. Connect a Kura Cloud Service instance to the broker.
3. Stop and restart the broker.
4. Try to reconnect the client.

After repeating steps 3 and 4 a couple of times the cloud service might fail to reconnect.
The Kura log reports this exception:
```
org.eclipse.kura.KuraConnectException: "Connection failed. Cannot connect"
	at org.eclipse.kura.core.data.transport.mqtt.MqttDataTransport.connect(MqttDataTransport.java:333)
	at org.eclipse.kura.core.data.DataServiceImpl$2.run(DataServiceImpl.java:609)
	at java.util.concurrent.Executors$RunnableAdapter.call(Executors.java:511)
	at java.util.concurrent.FutureTask.runAndReset(FutureTask.java:308)
	at java.util.concurrent.ScheduledThreadPoolExecutor$ScheduledFutureTask.access$301(ScheduledThreadPoolExecutor.java:180)
	at java.util.concurrent.ScheduledThreadPoolExecutor$ScheduledFutureTask.run(ScheduledThreadPoolExecutor.java:294)
	at java.util.concurrent.ThreadPoolExecutor.runWorker(ThreadPoolExecutor.java:1142)
	at java.util.concurrent.ThreadPoolExecutor$Worker.run(ThreadPoolExecutor.java:617)
	at java.lang.Thread.run(Thread.java:745)
Caused by: Invalid client ID (2)
	at org.eclipse.paho.client.mqttv3.internal.ExceptionHelper.createMqttException(ExceptionHelper.java:31)
	at org.eclipse.paho.client.mqttv3.internal.ClientState.notifyReceivedAck(ClientState.java:990)
	at org.eclipse.paho.client.mqttv3.internal.CommsReceiver.run(CommsReceiver.java:118)
	... 1 more
```
The client Id of the CloudService is valid since it has been previously accepted by the broker.
This seems to be caused by the fact that in the [MQTTConnectionManager](https://github.com/apache/activemq-artemis/blob/c8982d775b55849836ae20739a9e82f7eaf1d650/artemis-protocols/artemis-mqtt-protocol/src/main/java/org/apache/activemq/artemis/core/protocol/mqtt/MQTTConnectionManager.java#L43) class there is a static set that contains a list of the connected client ids, a new connection is not accepted by the broker if the client ID is already present in this set.
It seems like this set is not properly cleared, during my tests it always contains the client id of the CloudService that fails to connect even after that the broker is disabled.

The fact that the broker does not accept a connection if there is a client already connected with the same clientId violates the MQTT spec, according to [MQTT-3.1.4-2](http://docs.oasis-open.org/mqtt/mqtt/v3.1.1/csprd02/mqtt-v3.1.1-csprd02.html#_Toc385349768) the broker should disconnect the existing client and accept the new connection.

The existence of this static set also introduces some coupling between the **Simple Artemis MQTT Broker** and **ActiveMQ Artemis Broker** services: it is not possible to connect to one of the two instances if there is a client already connected to the other with the same clientId.

title: NetworkAdminServiceImpl: submitFirewallConfiguration blocks for 30 seconds
body:
Setting the firewall configuration through `setFirewallXxx` methods of `NetworkAdminServiceImpl` always takes 30 seconds.
The `submitFirewallConfiguration` methods waits for an `org/eclipse/kura/net/admin/event/FIREWALL_EVENT_CONFIG_CHANGE_TOPIC` OSGi event but neither `NetworkAdminServiceImpl` subscribes to that event nor the event is raised in that code path.
Eventually the wait timeouts and the method returns.

This bug has been present since KURA 2.0.0 release.

title: GSM modems not correctly detected after a reset
body: A GSM modem that provides also net interfaces (i.e. usb0) are not correctly detected after a reset. This is due to the fact that the NetworkServiceImpl is able to detect only tty and block resources. When a net resource added event triggers the NetworkServiceImpl, the resource is added to the block list and the modem is not recognized.

title: SystemAdminService.getUptime() returns SystemAdminService#UNKNOWN on MacOS when locale is not English
body:
Since the code to figure out the uptime on Mac uses string pattern matching to parse the result of uptime (which contains "days", "hours", and things like that), it doesn't work when the local is not 'en'.

The implementation should be replaced to use the kernel boottime as a reference and compute the uptime from there (see `sysctl kern.boottime`)

title: [DbDataStore] Stale messages not purged with timezone other than UTC
body:
Kura uses a HouseKeeper thread to purge messages from the internal data store once they have been published. The query to find these messages (QoS == 0) is of the form:

`DELETE FROM <table_name> WHERE qos = 0 AND publishedOn <= DATEADD('ss', 5, NOW()) AND publishedOn IS NOT NULL;"`

The NOW() function returns the current time from the underlying OS. However, when updating the "publishedOn" column once a message is published, the Java code uses Date().getTime(), which always returns UTC. Because of this, systems with a timezone set to anything west of UTC will never clear messages from the datastore.

Kura should be able to handle systems with a timezone set to something other than UTC.

- Textual description of the issue:

Currently Kura generates the `/etc/bind/named.conf` configuration file using two different templates, depending (at least) on the value of the configuration parameter **Pass DNS Servers through DHCP** in the **DHCP and NAT** section of the web UI.

Both of these configuration file variants specify a custom logging configuration for `named`:

1. If the parameter is set to `false`, `named` is configured for logging on `data/named.run`.
2. If the parameter is set to `true`, `named` is configured for logging on `/var/log/named.log`.

In the scenarios above I've found the following issues:

1. In the first scenario, if the daemon is invoked using `/etc/init.d/bind9 start`, it will fail to start printing the following messages on `/var/log/syslog`:

```
Mar 27 06:02:38 raspberrypi named[7768]: automatic empty zone: EMPTY.AS112.ARPA
Mar 27 06:02:38 raspberrypi named[7768]: configuring command channel from '/etc/bind/rndc.key'
Mar 27 06:02:38 raspberrypi named[7768]: command channel listening on 127.0.0.1#953
Mar 27 06:02:38 raspberrypi named[7768]: configuring command channel from '/etc/bind/rndc.key'
Mar 27 06:02:38 raspberrypi named[7768]: couldn't add command channel ::1#953: address not available
Mar 27 06:02:38 raspberrypi named[7768]: isc_stdio_open 'data/named.run' failed: file not found
Mar 27 06:02:38 raspberrypi named[7768]: configuring logging: file not found
Mar 27 06:02:38 raspberrypi named[7768]: loading configuration: file not found
Mar 27 06:02:38 raspberrypi named[7768]: exiting (due to fatal error)
```

The daemon start correctly if the following log-related section of `/etc/bind/named.conf` is removed:

```
logging {
	channel default_debug {
		file "data/named.run";
		severity dynamic;
	};
};
```

If the section above is removed bind will use the default logging configuration and forward log messages to the `syslog` daemon.

2. In the second scenario, `bind` is configured to log on `/var/log/named.log`, and to keep 3 backup versions of the file. When the daemon starts it will try to rename `/var/log/named.log` into 
`/var/log/named.log.0`, but it will fail because it does not have the permissions for modifying the `/var/log/ `directory, as it runs as the `bind` user

```
Mar 27 06:15:45 raspberrypi named[9026]: generating session key for dynamic DNS
Mar 27 06:15:45 raspberrypi named[9026]: sizing zone task pool based on 6 zones
Mar 27 06:15:45 raspberrypi named[9026]: set up managed keys zone for view _default, file 'managed-keys.bind'
Mar 27 06:15:45 raspberrypi named[9026]: configuring command channel from '/etc/bind/rndc.key'
Mar 27 06:15:45 raspberrypi named[9026]: command channel listening on 127.0.0.1#953
Mar 27 06:15:45 raspberrypi named[9026]: configuring command channel from '/etc/bind/rndc.key'
Mar 27 06:15:45 raspberrypi named[9026]: couldn't add command channel ::1#953: address not available
Mar 27 06:15:45 raspberrypi named[9026]: unable to rename log file '/var/log/named.log' to '/var/log/named.log.0': permission denied
```

This can be fixed as well by removing the logging related section of `/etc/bind/named.conf`. The `/var/log/named.log` is created by Kura installer script, which also changes the ownership of the file to the `bind` user. If the file is removed, `bind` will not be able to recreate it and it will fail to start.

title: [NetAdmin] Fix AT escape sequence timings in TelitModem
body:
The GPS disable logic for Telit Modems currently does not perform a 1 second pause after sending the `+++` escape sequence for switching serial port from GPS to AT mode.
This can cause the ModemMonitorService code to miss the `NO_CARRIER` modem response at the `+++` command and can cause the GPS disable process to fail.

title: [NetAdmin] Race condition between NetAdmin and PositionService after modem reset
body:
During the reset of a USB modem with GPS enabled that uses the same port for AT and GPS data, a race condition can occur between 2 threads that contend access to modem serial port.

The process is initiated by the ModemMonitor thread, that resets the modem and immediately enables GPS and posts ModemGpsReadyEvent.
The following threads are involved in the race condition:

1 - the PositionSerivce that handles ModemGpsReadyEvent and opens GPS serial port
2 - the ModemMonitorService.trackModem() method, that runs on an “anonymous” executor, that tries to identify the modem using at commands on the same port.

Thread 2 is the one responsible for tracking modems, it is triggered due the USB events that occur during modem reset.
The race condition can cause PortInUseExceptions in any of the two threads, and further modem resets.

title: [NetAdmin] Some state of the logic that manages modems persists across resets
body:
A part of the logic that manages modems is provided by the `CellularModem` subclasses, that are instantiated by a `CellularModemFactory` and are cached.
Currently a `CellularModemFactory` always returns the same `CellularModem` instance for a given modem, even if the managed modem has been reset.
This behaviour can cause problems because some of the `CellularModem` implementations keep internal state.

For example, the `TelitModem` class defines a boolean flag that specifies if the GPS is enabled or not, if the modem is reset with GPS enabled and the `NetAdmin` fails to disable GPS, the value of this flag will be retained. This can cause the NetAdmin to incorrectly assume that the GPS is still enabled after the reset even if it is not.

The state of the `CellularModem` instances should be cleared after a modem reset.

title: emitAllReadChannels method doesn't handle Runtime exceptions
body:
The `emitAllReadChannels` method in `WireAsset` class doesn't handle the unchecked exceptions, but only `KuraException`. So, if an unchecked exception as `RuntimeException` is thrown, it is simply passed to the upper layer and this can stop the current thread.

For example, if a Driver doesn't support readings, the `emitChannelRecords` throws an `IllegalArgumentException` that is not caught by the `emitAllReadChannels` method. The results is that the current thread on Wires is closed.

**Describe the bug**

2. Enable and set Major to > 65535
3. Apply

**Expected behavior**

title: [Modbus] Implement the MBAP header for TCP/IP communication

title: [BLE] BluetoothGattImpl.getCharacteristics(String startHandle, String endHandle) and getServices() methods return empty list
body:
It seems that ANSI Escape sequences send by gatttool (according to https://git.kernel.org/cgit/bluetooth/bluez.git/tree/attrib/interactive.c) remain in strings treated by BluetoothGattImpl.

Response data filter corresponding to `getCharacteristics` is `startsWith("handle:")`  but received string begin by `[Khandle:` (with [K from the erase line escape sequence). So the method returns an empty list.

Likewise for `getServices`.

Kura version : 2.0.0
Bluez version : 5.23
Plateform : Raspberry Pi 3 with Linux raspberrypi 4.4.11-v7+

The failure is caused by the following item in the list:

title: Kura makes use of system properties when filtering for native code libraries which is not supported
body:
At several locations Kura filters for native code libraries using system properties (kura.arch), however that is not supported by OSGi, still it works with Equinox 3.8.1. It is only possible to filter for "launching properties".

However other OSGi implementations more recent Equinox version don't support this anymore and fail to load the native libraries.

title: [Net] Modem monitor concurrency issue with multiple modems
[Net] PppFactory is not a factory and its design is wrong
body:
`PppFactory` is used by `ModemMonitorServiceImpl` to both create new instances and return already created instances. There are several defects:
1. It's not a factory. It's more similar to the [Multiton Pattern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multiton_pattern).
2. `obtainPppService(String iface, String port)` is misleading and error prone. Internally only the interface name, for example `ppp0` is used as the key.

The above can lead to the following scenario:
- Initially `obtainPppService(ppp0, /dev/ttyACM0)` creates a new `IModemLinkService` instance for the interface `ppp0` running on the modem serial port `/dev/ttyACM0`. This instance is tracked internally by PppFactory by the interface name `ppp0`. The monitor will spawn `pppd` on `/dev/ttyACM0`
- The modem gets reset/unplugged (for any reason). On Linux is entirely possible that the serial port device name changes for example to `/dev/ttyACM1`.
- In the next loop iteration the monitor will call `obtainPppService(ppp0, /dev/ttyACM1)` again but this will return the previous instance since the serial port name does not matter. The monitor will spawn `pppd` on `/dev/ttyACM0` which is clearly wrong.

Replace all calls to ConfigurationAdmin.getConfiguration(String)
body:
All calls to `org.osgi.service.cm.ConfigurationAdmin.getConfiguration(String)` should be replaced to calls of `org.osgi.service.cm.ConfigurationAdmin.getConfiguration(String, String)` providing `null` as the location parameter.

Most calls in Kura already are already migrated to that call, but not all. Using Apache Felix ConfigAdmin actually enforces the default binding which is generated otherwise and will not configure some components. Also see OSGi spec for `getConfiguration(String)`:

> Bind its location to the calling bundle's location.

That effectively binds the configuration to the Kura configuration bundle which is wrong. It should instead be bound to the bundle containing the service. Leaving the argument `null` would do that automatically once the service is registered.

title: [Modem] NoClassDefFoundError: Could not initialize class org.eclipse.kura.linux.net.modem.SupportedUsbModems
body:
This issue is caused by commit 9f5870537e36afa6641dc6d3d237686e82407f02 
Everything works right if the device has no internal modem, while, if the modem is available, the execution will stop at boot due to a `NoClassDefFoundError` on class `org.eclipse.kura.linux.net.modem.SupportedUsbModems`.

The issue is triggered by `SupportedUsbModemsInfo.isSupported` that tries to call `SupportedUsbModems.isSupported`. Before executing the `isSupported` method, the `SupportedUsbModems` static block will invoke `getLsusbInfo` that will call `LinuxProcessUtil.startWithStats`. 
The static block in `LinuxProcessUtil` modified by 9f5870537e36afa6641dc6d3d237686e82407f02 tries to get a service reference of the `SystemService`, but the result of this invocation is a null value. This is due to the fact that the `SystemService` component definition has a dependency on the `NetworkService`, but the network service needs the `SystemService` to execute: an indirect dependency loop is generated in this way, preventing the code to execute properly.

@ctron Could you take a look at this?

title: [DbDataStore] defrag and checkpoint are not per-table operations
body:
DbDataStore exposes two methods ``defrag`` and ``checkpoint`` that act on the entire DB and not on the DB table associated with the DbDataStore.
When multiple ``DbDataStore`` instances exists (since the introduction of the multiple cloud connections feature), each ``HouseKeeperTask`` instance will periodically call ``defrag``, potentially concurrently.

title: [DbDataStore] repair is very slow on big tables
body:
The ``repair`` operation contains a DB query to detect duplicates of the primary key (which should not occur).
The operation was added due to this [bug](https://sourceforge.net/p/hsqldb/discussion/73674/thread/a08046eb/).

The query has shown to take a very long time (in the order of minutes) on relatively large **file** databases (for example enabling the "almost persistent" configuration in kura.properties).

The bug is only known to happen on certain gateways using a raw flash storage configuration.

Since these gateways are no longer supported, the ``repair`` could be executed only once on startup maybe subjected to a configuration parameter.

We never saw this problem before but now that we installed Kura on a powerfull device (core i7 / 16 Gb ram / SSD / ...) we have the problem.

Thanks in advance for your job !

Hello,

It is hard to comment on this without knowing your application. I believe the synchronization block is necessary when attempting to install the deployment package. A couple of questions:
1. When you see this issue, are you also getting error in the log files (/var/log/kura.log and /var/log/kura-console.log)?
2. Do you have any potential long running processes in your bundle activate methods? This can often cause issues when activating bundles. 

Thanks,
--Dave

title: Improved type conversions in OPCUA driver
body:
This PR adds an additional property in OPCUA driver channel configuration, named `opcua.type`.
This property is considered only in case of a write and is ignored otherwise, it allows to specify the type of the OPCUA variable to be written.
The driver will attempt to convert the Java value to be written to the specified type. The allowed values for this property are the following:

* DEFINED_BY_JAVA_TYPE
* BOOLEAN
* SBYTE
* INT16
* INT32
* INT64
* BYTE
* UINT16
* UINT32
* UINT64
* FLOAT
* DOUBLE
* STRING
* BYTE_STRING
* BYTE_ARRAY
* SBYTE_ARRAY

This PR should extend the set of types that can be written using the driver to the list above, types not included in the list are still unsupported.

The default value for this parameter is DEFINED_BY_JAVA_TYPE, if this value is selected, the driver will perform the conversion automatically as in the current implementation, as follows:

Java -> OPCUA
BOOLEAN -> Boolean
DOUBLE -> Double
FLOAT -> Float
INTEGER -> Int32
LONG -> Int64
STRING -> String
BYTE_ARRAY -> SByte[]

Backwards compatibility is preserved by the fact that DEFINED_BY_JAVA_TYPE is the default.

This PR also changes the way in which BYTE_ARRAY Java type is handled, now the driver should support reading and writing the following OPCUA types using the BYTE_ARRAY Java type:

ByteString,
Byte[] (array of unsigned bytes)
SByte[] (array of signed bytes)

This PR also includes some tests for type conversions.

Closes #1840

title: Wrong approach for handling the bundles providing automation resources - host and fragments
body:
We use "bundle.getEntry" to check if a bundle is a provider of automation resources. This method searches only the contents of this bundle for the entry. Then we check if this bundle is a fragment, and if it is, we do not process it. So, if the host does not contain automation resources then it will not be processed; the fragment will not be processed either - as a result these resources will never be loaded.
Also if the host is processed before all it's fragments have been installed, some fragment bundles that are providers will not be processed.

title: Hue: Initial state fetch
body:
This is a Bug in the Hue binding: The initial state of a Lamp is not fetched after adding it.

Reproduce:
1. Remove Hue Bulb Things.
2. Bulbs are re-discovered, appear in inbox
4. Call /rest/inbox/(hue-bulb-thinguid)/approve
5. Call /rest/items/(hue-bulb-itemname)

Then the state is NULL, after pollinterval (default 10s) there should be a non-NULL state, but thats not the case. I guess, that there is no handler queued after ItemAddedEvent.
