title: POST request for thing addition gives 500 if same UID exists already
body:
If a thing is already added and if we try to add the same thing again by sending the POST request to `/things`, it gives a 500 error. If we try again then the response is 200 and the thing is added.

What is happening here is, if we try to add the same thing again the old thing is removed first (according to the method `addThingSafely` in `ThingSetupManager` class) but before it adds the new thing, it is sending back 500 error somehow.

When we retry the request, it creates the thing because the old thing has been removed in the previous step.

I am trying to figure out what is wrong there. Anyone has a clue?

body:

I'm using openHAB2 and while testing the new rule engine via REST API I have tracked down an issue described in the title. When I delete rule_42, rule_41 fires reliable.

title: "Integers" sent in configuration now include scale
body:
If I send a configuration value of -2, it is now received as a BigDecimal of -2.0, which is not equal to -2.  This seems to have changed recently (in the last week or two) - prior to this it was received without the scale setting and the change broke a load of comparisons in ZWave.

Given that comparisons of BigDecimal checks the scale, it's annoying that integer config types are not marshalled without the scale.

Maybe this is unavoidable, in which case feel free to close, but I thought I'd raise it in case others also experience problems with this change.

title: When enabling an advanced channel, the Paper UI hides all advanced channels
body: As the title say: When I enable/link an advanced channel, the Paper UI suddenly only shows non-advanced channels, but the button still says "show less". All channels should be kept on the page.

title: ChannelItemProvider depends on bundle start order
body:
#1288  introduced the ChannelItemProvider

If I understand the mechanism correctly, the "virtual" items are now created (createItemForLink) if a Thing or a ItemChannelLink has been added.

It seems to me that (at least) on startup it is possible that "createItemForLink" is called before all the bundle XMLs are completely parsed (see: https://github.com/eclipse/smarthome/pull/1519#issuecomment-221020452).

I can reproduce the error here in a Karaf container where the most ESH bundles are using the same start-level (I am using the our karaf and karaf-tp features).
I can workaround that startup behavior if I increase the start-level of the core.thing bundle.

title: Integer config parameter is stored as decimal
body:
If a service is configured through the Paper UI (and therefore through the REST API), numbers are sent in JSON always as double, i.e. an integer 1 becomes 1.0.
The REST API then stores this value as a BigDecimal with 1 decimal digit, so that it is not regarded as an integer anymore.

A concrete problem with this behavior is described here: https://community.openhab.org/t/change-homekit-setting-in-paperui/11407

title: RawType base64-encoded value is written to log file every time state changes
body:
Hi,

whenever an item changes, the ItemStateChangedEvent is logged (on info level), containing the old and the new state of an item:
`itemName + " changed from " + oldItemState.toString() + " to " + itemState.toString();`

If a RawType item has changed, the toString method of the RawType outputs its Base64-encoded value:
`PortableBase64.getEncoder().encode(bytes);`

This is not really nice as I don't need the binary file in my log file and this can increase the size of the log file quite fast.

title: Hue binding: things remaining in INITIALIZING state
body:
When starting OH, I noticed that my hue bridge thing is ONLINE (as expected) but my hue light things remain in INITIALIZING state.

HueLightHandler:initialize looks really weird to me. If run when the bridge is in state INITIALIZING, it will apparently set the thing state to INITIALIZING ! At my knowledge, a binding should only set state to ONLINE or OFFLINE.
And there is probably rare cases while state is not set at all in this method.
And finally just a remark, this binding does not implement bridgeStatusChanged.

title: ThingHandler.channelLinked() not called for all channels after handler initialization
body:
The [documentation](https://www.eclipse.org/smarthome/documentation/development/bindings/thing-handler.html#channel-links) reads:

> The channelLinked method is called, even if the link existed before the handler was initialized. It will be called only after the initialized method has been executed successfully

According to https://github.com/openhab/openhab2-addons/issues/1125, this does not seem to be the case anymore.

Related to this, the JavaDoc of 'ThingHandler.channelLinked()' is not very helpful and it should imho contain the same information as the documentation.

body:
Trying to create a new item through the Paper UI (e.g. when creating a link in advanced mode), I get a 400 Bad request now and find this in my log:

```
12:18:56.119 [WARN ] [thome.io.rest.core.item.ItemResource] - Received HTTP PUT request at 'items/XXX' with an invalid item type 'DateTimeItem'.
```

I assume that we missed a place where "Item" needs to be removed.

title: 404 when accessing Configuration->System
body:
Using the latest OH2 build, the Paper UI shows an "ERROR 404 - Not found" when accessing the System configuration and it seems that it stops rendering the page (at least it leaves an empty box with no configuration parameters at the end).

Looking at the javascript console, I see

```
catcher.js:197 GET http://localhost:8080/rest/config-descriptions/system:persistence 404 (Not Found)
```

This probably occurs when no configuration has been set yet. I think the Paper UI should silently ignore such a situation and still make it possible to submit a configuration for it.

P.S.: I see another 404 for http://localhost:8080/ui/fonts/Roboto-LightItalic.woff. This is probably unrelated, but should be fixed as well.

title: Prevent hidden files from being parsed
body:
When using Mac OS X to edit Openhab files through an SMB share, files with a leading ._ are created by Mac OS X to store file information about the actual file in.

**Example:**
Create/edit a file called "test.item" using OS X finder application  and Mac OS X also creates a file called "._test.item".

Although these ._ files do not contain any valid information for Openhab, they are being parsed causing problems in mainly the Openhab rule engine.
This leads to errors in the Openhab log like:

2016-09-02 09:54:45.764 [ERROR] [.script.engine.ScriptExecutionThread] - Rule 'Pantry light motion': Script interpreter couldn't be obtain

2016-09-01 15:47:55.026 [WARN ] [pse.smarthome.core.items.GenericItem] - failed notifying listener '[org.eclipse.smarthome.model.rule.runtime.internal.engine.RuleEngineImpl@1ec05f5, Home_State, null]' about state update of item java.lang.NullPointerException: {}

Perhaps preventing the ._ files to be parsed would help in preventing issues caused by these files?

Since configuration options can be optional, it would be nice to be able to unset or at least send a blank entry for values.

title: ThingManager should adapt state updates to linked item type
body:
I have a hue light defined like this in hue.things:

```
Bridge hue:bridge:xxx "Philips Hue Bridge" [ ipAddress="192.168.1.3", userName="xxx" ] {
    0210 1 "Hue White and Color - Living Room Ceiling" @ "Living Room" [ lightId="1" ]
```

I want to have an on/off switch on my sitemap, so I defined an item for it as

```
Switch living_light_ceiling_switch "Living Room Ceiling Switch" <light> (gLights) { channel="hue:0210:xxx:1:color" }
```

I read in the documentation that I need to use the :color channel instead of :switch to make it work. So now I have a sitemap definition as

```
Switch living_light_ceiling_switch "Living Room Ceiling Switch" <light> (gLights) { channel="hue:0210:xxx:1:color" }
```

It works nicely as far as turning the light on and off from the UI but if I try to turn the light on/off from the real Hue app the state doesn't get updated in the classic UI or HABdroid. I see in the basic UI that it gets updated with its HSB value (68,88,0) instead of an ON/OFF state.

This is problematic because in openHAB 1.x I had quite a few rules depending on the ON/OFF state of the item, for example if conditions like (living_light_command is another switch item):

```
if (living_light_ceiling_switch.state != living_light_command.state) { ... }
```

 and now those are not working at all. Can this be fixed in the binding? Either create/enable the :switch channel for the thing, or make the :color channel converted to ON/OFF states when the items is a simple switch.

Issue #866 might be related, but I thought I better open a new issue for this, as that one is not really about this switch state problem. I understand that rewriting my rules to somehow check for the brightness value might work, but it's far from ideal and probably I'm not the only one who will be hit by this during transition to openHAB2.

Oh, and I'm using beta4.

title: Duplicate channels on Thing
body:
A thing's channels are stored as a List<Channel> , see 

https://github.com/eclipse/smarthome/blob/e0985e90d389350580e59bfbcd7e0adaaccf7519/bundles/core/org.eclipse.smarthome.core.thing/src/main/java/org/eclipse/smarthome/core/thing/internal/ThingImpl.java#L49

Because this is a list, its possible for a Thing to have duplicate channels with the same ID. This also means that calling "getChannel(String id)" will only return the first instance of the duplicate channel. My assumption would be that a thing can only have a single instance of a channel.

title: Basic UI does not update icons of read only switches
body:
I've done some more testing with the functionality provided by #2030 and it seems that icons of read only switches in the Basic UI are not properly updated. I typically use these for representing the state of motion/smoke/CO sensors.

You can easily reproduce this in the demo by replacing the `Group demo` in `demo.sitemap` with

```
        Text label="Group Demo" icon="firstfloor" {
            Switch item=Lights mappings=[OFF="All Off"]
            Group item=Heating
            Group item=Windows
            Text item=Temperature
            Switch item=Light_C_Corridor_Ceiling
            Text item=Light_C_Corridor_Ceiling
        }
```

and replacing the definition of `Light_C_Corridor_Ceiling` in `demo.items` with:

```
Switch Light_C_Corridor_Ceiling     "Ceiling [%s]" <switch> (gC, Lights)
```

When you then switch `Light_C_Corridor_Ceiling` or `Lights mappings`, the icon of `Switch item=Light_C_Corridor_Ceiling` is properly updated. 

However the icon of `Text item=Light_C_Corridor_Ceiling` is not.

Only after reloading the page it will again represent the right state.

Another way to reproduce it is to open `Group Demo > Open windows`. And issue the following commands in the console:

```
smarthome:update Window_GF_Frontdoor OPEN
smarthome:update Window_GF_Kitchen OPEN
smarthome:update Window_GF_Living OPEN
smarthome:update Window_GF_Toilet OPEN
smarthome:update Window_FF_Bath OPEN
smarthome:update Window_FF_Bed OPEN
smarthome:update Window_FF_Office_Window OPEN
smarthome:update Window_FF_Office_Door OPEN
smarthome:update Garage_Door OPEN
```

Now all window icons should be open. But they only are after reloading the page. The same way windows should be closed after issuing:

```
smarthome:update Window_GF_Frontdoor CLOSED
smarthome:update Window_GF_Kitchen CLOSED
smarthome:update Window_GF_Living CLOSED
smarthome:update Window_GF_Toilet CLOSED
smarthome:update Window_FF_Bath CLOSED
smarthome:update Window_FF_Bed CLOSED
smarthome:update Window_FF_Office_Window CLOSED

```

        <description>Servers online status.</description>

title: NTP Tests bug, when time is changed
body:
In the NTP Binding Tests the "Europe/Helsinki" time zone is used. But recently there has been a time change in this time zone and that broke two of the tests:

1) 'if no time zone is set in the configuration, the string channel is updated with the default one'

The message is:
The string channel was not updated with the right timezone
Expected: is "EEST"
     but: was "EET"

Aparently the abbreviation EEST(Eastern European Summer Time) is used only in summer and now that the time is changed the abbreviation, that is returned is EET(Eastern European Time) - https://www.timeanddate.com/time/zones/eest

2) 'if no time zone is set in the configuration, the dateTime channel is updated with the default one'

The message is:
The dateTime channel was not updated with the right timezone
Expected: is "+0300"
     but: was "+0200"

Now that the time is changed, the current offset is +0200, not +0300

I have made a PR with a fix for this: https://github.com/eclipse/smarthome/pull/2377

title: BaseThingHandler:channelLinked() called frequently / too much
body:
In a simple setup with a single Item -> Channel definition in the DSL, the above method is called three times (for the given channel) at startup of the runtime, twice triggered by ThingManager.added() and once by ItemRegistry.allItemsChanged(). 

Expected behaviour would be that the method is called once for each time an Item definition is parsed, taking into account the fact that "temporary" items are created. 

In my use case the channelLinked() triggers a read request on a bus (e.g. KNX), which is not designed to be flooded in this way, especially when reading out the same value multiple times.

title: ThingHandlers stay UNINITIALIZED of registration runs into timeout
body:
The method `ThingManager.registerChildHandlers()` has the following code:

```
                        registerHandler(child);
                        initializeHandler(child);
```
Within `registerHandler` the handler registration is done in a "Safe" call, i.e. it might return after 5 seconds without having successfully registered the handler by that time.
As a result, `initializeHandler` will simply do nothing, since it checks whether the handler is correctly registered already.

The outcome is that the Thing stays in UNINITIALIZED state indefinitely.

[This seems to be like a report](https://community.openhab.org/t/binding-handler-registration-issues/17422) of exactly that situation.

title: Hue brightness conversion is not bijective
body:
The brightness conversion of a percent value to a hue value and then back to percent should be the same value. E.g. 67% => 170 => 67%
Currently the conversion done in LightStateConverter will end in 66% cause the value cast to int instead of being rounded.

title: CRON rule triggered multiple times if in same file as an invalid/unresolved rule
body:
See discussion at https://github.com/eclipse/smarthome/issues/2545:

There are situations where the same rule is scheduled multiple times. It appears to happen if rule files are refreshed and contain rules that weren't correctly parsed before (due to syntax errors or potentially unresolved item or action names).

Under Configuration->Items click (+) to add an item. 
Fill in all required fields, but in the "Name" field supply a name containing a space, such as "Office Lights" 
Click (+) to add the item.   

Results: You are returned to the Items list without an error and without the item being added.   

Expected results:  
If spaces are not allowed in item names,  a message to that effect should be given, and/or the user not allowed to continue.

title: Multiple time cron expressions in rule not working
body:
As requested ( https://github.com/openhab/openhab-distro/issues/355 ) I'm opening a new issue.

Works (fires every five seconds):
```
rule "cron test"
when
	// Time cron "0 0 0 * * ?" or
	Time cron "0/5 * * * * ?"
then
	logInfo("cron", "test")
end
```

Doesn't work as expected (second cron doesn't fire):
```
rule "cron test"
when
	Time cron "0 0 0 * * ?" or
	Time cron "0/5 * * * * ?"
then
	logInfo("cron", "test")
end
```

I'm using the current apt version of openhab:
```
openhab2-offline/testing,now 2.0.0~b4 all  [installiert]
  openHAB Offline Distribution
```

title: Config parameters normalisation not working for thing parameters
body:
I'm seeing some parameters being stored in the jsondb as a STRING when they are defined as INTEGER.

My guess is that this is happening in the normalisation code. The parameters in question are in the thing config descriptions - not the thing-type.

This is more obvious when using HABmin since HABmin only sends updates to parameters that have changed - if I don't change these parameters, then nothing is sent in the REST interface, but these parameters are being changed to STRING. PaperUI is sending the parameter as a number, and it's getting stored as 12.0 in json which is still wrong, but it does at least work in this instance.

I assume that whatever code does the normalisation is using the config descriptor for the thing-type, and not the thing itself. Possibly [here](https://github.com/eclipse/smarthome/blob/48e405fb3f1e60b56333e26bd42021bd5cfc1bc8/bundles/io/org.eclipse.smarthome.io.rest.core/src/main/java/org/eclipse/smarthome/io/rest/core/thing/ThingResource.java#L671).

Having updated the zwave binding to allow [textual thing definitions](https://github.com/openhab/org.openhab.binding.zwave/issues/153), the binding no longer functions if parameters are updated with the UI.

title: PaperUI, text entry and annoying shifting
body:
In the PaperUI->Control - if you have a channel that is a simple string and start typing letters, eventually you'll enter the 8th character and the whole field shifts down a line.

The problem with the shift down is that the field loses focus.  Especially annoying is if you click it again and backspace once (so we have 7 characters) - it shifts back up and loses focus again. This behavior makes it very difficult to enter something in.

I'd rather it either get's focus (and the carot position is after the last character) or the field simply scrolls

title: [BasicUI] Slider knob not showing in BasicUI on Microsoft Edge
body:
Hi everybody,

I know this isn't a major issue, but I noticed that the slider knob is missing when using the BasicUI in Microsoft Edge. This makes adjusting the slider a bit tricky.
**Edge:**
![snip_slider](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/25036470/22208950/09581e36-e185-11e6-9086-532c825785bc.png)
**IE:**
![snip_slider12](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/25036470/22209454/d047fe98-e186-11e6-9b47-054dac78873d.png)

Using the F12 DOM Explorer and comparing the CSS styling between Edge and Internet Explorer, I discovered that the height of `.mdl-slider.is-upgraded `is set to 2px in Edge and due to an override from `_:-ms-input-placeholder, :root .mdl-slider.mdl-slider.is-upgraded` it is set to 32px in IE. As this override doesn't happen in Edge, the height stays at 2px and the knob isn't showing.

**Edge:**
![snip_slider2](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/25036470/22208958/130dc250-e185-11e6-8898-0420ef0b0612.png)

**IE:**
![snip_slider23](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/25036470/22208962/1692ab84-e185-11e6-85df-6a4c2830b981.png)
![snip_slider4](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/25036470/22208975/1f652c14-e185-11e6-87b8-46db9a4f2b58.png)

Setting the height to 32px in Edge fixes the problem.

I don't know if this is an issue inherent to Google Material Design or if there is a simple fix. But it would be nice to see the slider working in Edge to, as I use it as my primary browser on all my devices.

Thanks!

title: Switch Groups changing to UNDEF
body:
With OH2 GA (might also occur with other versions) I do face an issue with Group:Switch:OR going to "UNDEF" instead of ON or OFF.

I do own some motion sensors (Homematic HM-Sen-MDIR-O-2) and "itemized" them as follows:

```
Group:Switch:OR(ON,OFF) gMotion "Motion detected"
Switch M1 "Motion Sensor #1" <motion> (gMotion) { channel="homematic:..." }
Switch M2 "Motion Sensor #2 " <motion> (gMotion)  { channel="homematic:..." }
```
However, the group's state only is ON or OFF if both sensors have the same state. If their state's differ, the group reports itself as UNDEF.

On motion, the event.log prints

```
[GroupItemStateChangedEvent] - gMotion changed from OFF to UNDEF through M1
[ItemStateChangedEvent     ] - M1 changed from OFF to ON
```
later:

```
[ItemStateChangedEvent     ] - M1 changed from ON to OFF
[GroupItemStateChangedEvent] - gMotion changed from UNDEF to OFF through M1
Source of Issue (issue reported by m0wlheldChristoph Dahlen):
https://community.openhab.org/t/issue-with-group-switch-or-going-to-undef/21403
```

My findings:
If all switches are OFF, the group is OFF
If only one or several are ON, then the group is UNDEF
If all are ON, the group is ON

###################
I checked another group of 30 switches. All have changed from NULL to OFF after starting OH. The group then switches from NULL to OFF too, when the last item of the group switches to OFF.
`gStickyUnreach changed from NULL to OFF through Win_Kind1_StickyUnreach`

So far so good.

But when I change one switch to ON, the group goes UNDEF for some reason.

title: PaperUI | DecimalType is parsed to Integer
body:
I noticed that the Paper UI no longer displays decimals places.
This bug was introduced in #2628:

title: Installing Rules Engine Crashes Event Source
body:
It seems that when I install the Rules engine (either through PaperUI or by hitting the endpoint `http://{ip_addr}/rest/extensions/misc-ruleengine/install`) the event stream crashes, hence why the loading spinner never completes in PaperUI.

Steps to reproduce:
- `curl http://{ip_addr}/rest/events` to listen to the event stream.
- Install the rules engine in PaperUI > Add-ons > Misc > Install Rules Engine (Experimental)
- *curl process gets terminated and loading spinner never completes*

Our app depends on the Rules engine, so it needs to be able to listen for the install completed event. I've tried installing other extensions and I can see them being logged when they're installed/uninstalled. This seems to only happen when installing the Rules engine.

title: itemAdded called multiple times on RegistryChangeListener at boot
Group Item Does Not Have Valid Defaults For Group:Dimmer and Group:Switch
body:
The Item syntax in `Items.xtext` clearly indicates that the `ModelGroupFunction` is optional, even if the `ModelItemType` is specified. However, at least with `Group:Dimmer` and `Group:Switch` (without a `ModelGroupFunction`), declarations like
```
Group:Dimmer   bedroom_dimmers
Group:Switch   bedroom_switches
```
result in an error 
```
[ERROR] [arthome.core.items.dto.ItemDTOMapper] - Group function 'AND' requires two arguments. Using Equality instead.
```
This is in conflict with the openHAB documentation at http://docs.openhab.org/configuration/items.html#groups

> By default, if no function is provided to the group, the Group uses OR.

Pretty clearly, that's wrong, between the error message, and it not working.

Expected Behavior:

An appropriate default would be implemented for the impacted `ModelItemTypes`

---

The reason to support a group qualified by `ModelItemType` is at least three-fold:
* Clarify what can and what shouldn't be added to the group
* Provide at least Designer, if not run-time protection of adding the "wrong" kind of items to the group
* Narrow choices within Designer's pickers

I'm not terribly concerned as to _what_ the default is. I can always specify it if I'm using the group for more than just collecting it's elements for ease of management or for iterating over them.

See further https://community.openhab.org/t/items-bug-group-function-and-requires-two-arguments-using-equality-instead/25268

title: NPE in Configuration.toString()
body: In the ThingHandlerFactory of my binding I log a Thing's configuration when I process a Thing in createHandler(). The thing types are initialized with static XMLs, and I have several configuration properties which do not have a default value. The current Configuration.toString() method fails with a NPE, since it attempts to read the class of a property's value, and such value is not set.

title: JSON Field Type Mismatch in `/rules` Endpoint.
body:
Hi,

It seems like there might be a JSON field type mismatch when hitting the `/rules` endpoint. 

When fetching the rules from `GET /rules`, sometimes the JSON response for a rule contains the field `"required": "false"` which I believe is meant to actually be a `boolean` (inside `Rule->Actions->Inputs`).

Steps:
- I created a new rule (containing just one trigger) with `POST /rules`. 
- Next, I updated that rule so that it would have a second trigger by calling the `PUT /rules/{ruleUID}` endpoint.
- After refreshing the list of rules by calling `GET /rules`, the newly updated rule JSON now contains the field `"required": "false"`. That field wasn't there prior to adding a second trigger.

Here's what the final JSON response looked like (scrapping out all of the unnecessary stuff).
`
{
...
	"actions": [{
		"inputs": {
			"required": "false"
		},
		"id": "2",
		"configuration": {},
		"type": "script.ScriptAction"
	}],
...
}
`

Is this intended, or a bug? The `/module-types` endpoint also uses the `Inputs` JSON schema, but that one actually sets the `"required"` field to a `boolean` instead of a `String`.

title: Change to DayLigth saving Time causes stop in timerelated persistence strategies
body:
As reported in the OH community ( [Link](https://community.openhab.org/t/openhab-not-saving-mesaurements-after-daylight-saving-time-change/25647)) the change to DayLigth Saving Time caused persistence schedules that are only using a time based strategy (everyMinute etc.) to stop at the time-switch.

Checks done on my side:
Actual values continued to be displayed.
The check of the database (rrd4j with a "everyMinute" strategy) showed the last value to be stored at the time-switch.
Several users confirmed that after restart of the OH-instance the time-scheduled persistence was working again. 
There is also an report on a cron based rule that stopped working, can't say if it is really related to the above.

title: [REST/Persistence] API request for persistence items returns empty list
body:
I installed two persistence extensions: rrd4j and InfluxDB.

A GET request to "/rest/persistence" returns the following result:

`[
  {
    "id": "rrd4j",
    "label": "rrd4j",
    "type": "Queryable"
  },
  {
    "id": "influxdb",
    "label": "influxdb",
    "type": "Queryable"
  }
]`

A GET request to "/rest/persistence/items?serviceId=rrd4j" and "/rest/persistence/items?serviceId=influxdb" returns an empty list with status code 200:

`[]`

Expected result: A list of all available items as defined in the *.rules file.

The data for a specific item is available at "/rest/persistence/items/{ITEMID}?serviceId=influxdb".

The behaviour can be reproduced with a clean install of openHAB 2.0.0.

title: BasicUI: Images and Charts not updating according to Configuration
body:
There's been a discussion in the community about images and charts not updating as expected:
https://community.openhab.org/t/basic-ui-image-refresh-rate-in-seconds-instead-miliseconds/27152

Some tests suggest that the refresh parameter is interpreted differently:
* ClassicUI: milli sec
* BasicUI: sec

**Fix**: Use same time base for all UIs

Also, in my own setup the update works only on images not on charts.
The chart initially loads in BasicUI but then instead of updating it shows a broken image symbol.

title: thingUpdated() gets called during initialize()
body: As observed in https://github.com/openhab/openhab2-addons/pull/2019#issuecomment-298440882 and https://www.eclipse.org/forums/index.php/t/1085852/ it seems that `ThingHandler.thingUpdated()` gets called while the handler is still in `ThingHandler.initialize()`. This puts the unnecessary burden of handling synchronization on bindings and is not intended.

```
rule "Tide Dash button pressed"
when
    Channel "amazondashbutton:dashbutton:Tide:press" triggered
then
    sendNotification("some@email.com", "Amazon button pressed!")
    sendCommand(Vacuum_Dock, ON)
end

```

 when
     Channel "mihome:sensor_switch:<ID>:button" triggered
 then
     var actionName = receivedEvent.getEvent()
     switch(actionName) {
         case "CLICK": {
             <ACTION>
         }
         case "DOUBLE_CLICK": {
             <ACTION>
         }
         case "LONG_CLICK_PRESS": {
             <ACTION>
         }
         case "LONG_CLICK_RELEASE": {
             <ACTION>
         }

 end
```
2. Try to trigger the events and see the results

Expected result: The rule is triggered and performed actions should be logged in the console.

Actual result: The rule doesn't trigger, nothing is being logged.

title: [Paper UI] Sliders for Dimmer items have lost % sign
[Paper UI] Brightness slider must not send HSB commands
body:
Using the brightness slider (the middle one) for color channels in the Paper UI results in HSB commands being sent. Instead, it should send PercentTypes only, because otherwise it is not possible to adjust the brightness if the hue&saturations settings might not be correct in the UI (e.g. because the color has been adjusted using a color temperature control).

As far as I remember, this used to be the case in the past. Has anything changed here?

title: [BasicUI] Image not resized properly
PaperUI: Rules loads Extensions
body:
If you don't use an extension service but open the rule category in the PaperUI (http://127.0.0.1:8080/paperui/index.html#/rules) it complains about a non available service using a notification:
ERROR 503 - Service not available

The service that is not available is the extension one.
I don't think we need to warn every time the rules category is opened that the extension service is not available but accept the missing service silently.

This may or may not be a bug - seems to work differently then channel advanced settings.  For a transport that I've been working on - I have a configuration descriptor (below).  When you go to Configuration->Services->Press the Configure button on my transport - I expected the advanced group to be hidden behind a 'Advanced' or 'Show More' type of button - but it was simply displayed as is (see the screen shot below).

        <parameter-group name="advancedSettings">

title: io.rest uses gson 2.5.0, although we so far only support gson 2.3.1
body:
I found this in my logs:

```
Exception in thread "Thread-65" java.lang.IllegalAccessError: tried to access method com.google.gson.Gson.newJsonWriter(Ljava/io/Writer;)Lcom/google/gson/stream/JsonWriter; from class org.eclipse.smarthome.io.rest.JSONResponse
        at org.eclipse.smarthome.io.rest.JSONResponse.lambda$0(JSONResponse.java:162)
        at java.lang.Thread.run(Thread.java:745)
```
A closer analysis shows that this method is only publicly available in gson 2.5, while my setup only has gson 2.3.1 available.

Interestingly, our smarthome.target resolves 2.2.4 AND 2.5.0, so the IDE picks up 2.5.0 and compiles against it.

As far as I remember, we wanted to be compatible with gson 2.3.1, but it all seems to be a bit messed up right now...

body:
The Paper UI uses incorrect descriptions for boolean group functions. Just two examples:

AND(OFF,ON) shows
```
One OFF → OFF else ON
```
while it should be
```
All OFF → OFF else ON
```
and OR(OFF,ON) shows
```
All OFF → OFF else ON
```
while it should be
```
One OFF → OFF else ON
```

I didn't check the others - if we are lucky, these are the only ones that got mixed up.

title: Remove separate altitude parameter from Astro binding
body:
When approving my auto-discovered Sun thing, I got this in my log:

```
15:52:30.491 [INFO ] [smarthome.event.ThingAddedEvent     ] - Thing 'astro:sun:local' has been added.
15:52:30.493 [INFO ] [me.event.ThingStatusInfoChangedEvent] - 'astro:sun:local' changed from UNINITIALIZED to INITIALIZING
15:52:30.500 [ERROR] [ding.astro.handler.AstroThingHandler] - Astro parameters geolocation could not be split into latitude and longitude, disabling thing 'astro:sun:local'
15:52:30.501 [INFO ] [me.event.ThingStatusInfoChangedEvent] - 'astro:sun:local' changed from INITIALIZING to OFFLINE
```
The issue is that the discovery now adds "<lat>,<long>,<alt>" in the geoLocation config parameter of the Thing, while it expects the altitude to be filled into the dedicated "altitude" parameter instead.

As we will soon have a [location context](https://github.com/eclipse/smarthome/issues/3709), which also includes altitude information, I think it would make most sense to remove the "altitude" parameter of Astro things and rather mark the geoLocation parameter to be of context "location", which implicitly can hold an optional altitude value.

title: RULES: Error aborting execution rule with return
body:
Hi @all,
referencing to this discussion here:
[https://community.openhab.org/t/exit-rule-with-return-false/26913/6](https://community.openhab.org/t/exit-rule-with-return-false/26913/6)

I put this case to the issues.
Maybe not a big deal. Main problem is, to be able to break a rule execution.
This works with
`if (something) return false`
but it causes an error in the designer and during loading the rule file.

If you use instead this one:
`if (something) return`
then, there is no error in the designer and no error during loading the file, but the execution of the rule is not longer possible.

Thx for solving.

title: Astro binding :  Peculiarities of the Sun phase channel
body:
I am using the Astro binding in my openHAB system, using the Sun / Phase channel as a way to check the "state of daylight" in my rules. 

While testing this I was looking at the log files for a "full cycle" (i.e. a 24 hour period) and I noticed a couple of strange things. 

Here is a snip of my log file:

2017-08-14 03:55:00.003 [ItemStateChangedEvent     ] - AstroSunHome_sPhase_Name changed from UNDEF to NAUTIC_DAWN
2017-08-14 05:02:00.003 [ItemStateChangedEvent     ] - AstroSunHome_sPhase_Name changed from NAUTIC_DAWN to CIVIL_DAWN
2017-08-14 05:50:00.004 [ItemStateChangedEvent     ] - AstroSunHome_sPhase_Name changed from CIVIL_DAWN to SUN_RISE
2017-08-14 05:54:00.002 [ItemStateChangedEvent     ] - AstroSunHome_sPhase_Name changed from SUN_RISE to DAYLIGHT
2017-08-14 13:34:00.002 [ItemStateChangedEvent     ] - AstroSunHome_sPhase_Name changed from DAYLIGHT to NOON
2017-08-14 21:14:00.003 [ItemStateChangedEvent     ] - AstroSunHome_sPhase_Name changed from NOON to SUN_SET
2017-08-14 21:18:00.003 [ItemStateChangedEvent     ] - AstroSunHome_sPhase_Name changed from SUN_SET to CIVIL_DUSK
2017-08-14 22:06:00.007 [ItemStateChangedEvent     ] - AstroSunHome_sPhase_Name changed from CIVIL_DUSK to NAUTIC_DUSK
2017-08-14 23:13:00.003 [ItemStateChangedEvent     ] - AstroSunHome_sPhase_Name changed from NAUTIC_DUSK to ASTRO_DUSK
2017-08-15 00:00:00.023 [ItemStateChangedEvent     ] - AstroSunHome_sPhase_Name changed from ASTRO_DUSK to UNDEF

The first thing I notice is that apparently the Sun / Phase channel will never report NIGHT as a state (contrary to what the documentation states) but instead goes back to UNDEF. 

The next thing is that the Sun / Phase channel can report a stated called NOON (and this is as stated in the documentation). As can been seen in the log this is reported as the phase from 13:34 until SUN_SET. 

As far as I know, however, NOON is a specific point in time (12:00 / midday) and not a period of time, thus (IMO) NOON should not really be reported on the Sun / Phase channel.

When adding e.g. a hue bridge manually, its result is automatically set to IGNORED in the inbox as expected. When removing the bridge, the IGNORED entry in the inbox must be automatically deleted so a new discovery can find it again. It turns out, that this is not happening most of the time.

The reason is, that we do not have such a thing as a Pre-Delete-Hook, where we could easily check and remove possible ignored entries.Listening to ThingStatusChangedEvents as currently implemented does not help, because a REMOVED event indicates that a thing is already removed and REMOVING is not always fired and sometimes directly followed by a REMOVED. In most cases we are accessing the ThingRegistry too late to get informations about the thing being removed (it just returns null).

title: JSONPATH returning NULL on item not found can lead to problems with openhab REST API
body:
NOTE: Reported here as per request of @kaikreuzer in https://github.com/openhab/openhab2-addons/issues/2767

System: Ubuntu server 16.04 LTS on Xeon 1240L V3. Openhab stable from ppa

I recently included Sonoff B1 lightbulbs with Tasmota fw in my system. Here is an example item config:

```
Switch B1_1_Sw          "B1-1-Switch"           (gALL, gLIGHTS)         { mqtt="<[broker:b1-1/stat/RESULT:state:JSONPATH($.POWER)],  >[broker:b1-1/cmnd/POWER:command:*:${command}]" }
Number B1_1_Dim         "B1-1-Dimmer"                                   { mqtt="<[broker:b1-1/stat/RESULT:state:JSONPATH($.Dimmer)], >[broker:b1-1/cmnd/Dimmer:command:*:default]" }
Number B1_1_CT          "B1-1-ColorTemp"                                { mqtt="<[broker:b1-1/stat/RESULT:state:JSONPATH($.CT)],     >[broker:b1-1/cmnd/CT:command:*:default], >[broker:b1-1/cmnd/CT:command:*: ]" }
String B1_1_Col         "B1-1-Color"                                    { mqtt="<[broker:b1-1/stat/RESULT:state:JSONPATH($.Color)],  >[broker:b1-1/cmnd/Color:command:*:default]" }
```

The B1 with tasmota software answers to all commands with

> stat/RESULT {“POWER”:“ON”, “Dimmer”:100, “Color”:“FFFFFFFFFF”}

(of course with appropriate values). It also answers with this to the cmnd/CT command which sets the color temperature. If you want the color temperature in a reply, you have to send an empty cmnd/CT and you will get something like this.

> stat/RESULT {“CT”:500}

Now, JSONPATH returns NULL if it can’t find the path item you are asking for, and as both the standard as well as the CT reply use the RESULT path, there’s always something going to be NULL. If you send a regular command, CT will be NULL and if you ask for CT, POWER, Dimmer and Color will be NULL.

That lead to this messages in the log:

> 2017-10-03 20:12:50.277 [WARN ] [b.core.events.EventPublisherDelegate] - given new state is NULL, couldn’t post update for 'B1_1_CT’
> 2017-10-03 20:12:50.282 [WARN ] [b.core.events.EventPublisherDelegate] - given new state is NULL, couldn’t post update for 'B1_1_CT’

> 2017-10-03 20:12:50.325 [WARN ] [b.core.events.EventPublisherDelegate] - given new state is NULL, couldn’t post update for ‘B1_1_Dim’

And after a short while the openhab REST API would reply to an items request with a 500 java.lang.NullPointerException.

title: ConfigDispatcher: Config file processing order-dependent if exclusivePIDs are used
body:
### Context
The `org.eclipse.smarthome.config.dispatch.internal.ConfigDispatcher` processes configuration files in the `processConfigFile` method. How a config file is processed depends on whether it has a so-called _exclusive PID_ or not: A config file has an exclusive PID if its first line starts with a PID marker _pid:_ followed by a PID.

### The Issue
Consider the following two config files:

a.cfg:
```
pid:some_pid
A=some value
```

b.cfg:
```
some_pid:B=some other value
```

Then the processing of these two files in the ConfigDispatcher depends on the order in which the two files are processed:
* If `a.cfg` is processed first, then the resulting configuration contains both properties `A` and `B` for PID `some_pid`.
* If `b.cfg` is processed first, then the resulting configuration only contains property `A` for PID `some_pid`.

Frankly, I do not know which result is the correct one, but I think that it is not correct that it depends on the order in which the files are processed. 

One result of this 'order dependency' is that the test `ConfigDispatcherOSGiTest#theSameLocalAndGlobalPIDsInDifferentFilesAreConsideredOnePID` sometimes fails on my machine (it uses two config files with the same structure as in the example above) - depending on the order in which the two config files used by this test are processed (the config files are processed sorted by lastModified date, which is the same on my machine for both used config files). 

### Expected behavior?
As stated above, I do not know what the expected behavior is. However, from looking at the code of the method `ConfigDispatcher#processConfigFile` I see that there is some logic that tries to skip config properties for a PID if this PID is used as exclusive PID in another config file. Currently, this logic works only if the file with the exclusive PID is processed last. So I guess that the expected behavior could be that config properties for a PID are ignored if there is another config file which has this PID as exclusive PID. However, from looking at the unit test referenced above, skipping properties in files without exclusive PID is not expected. But of course this unit test might simply be buggy...

To conclude: Does anyone here know what is the intended behaviour here regarding parsing of config files with and without exclusive PIDs?

title: Configuration normalisation not performed on channel configuration
body:
When saving channel configuration, normalisation is not performed on the channel configuration. Additionally, it looks like the defaults may not be of the correct type - defaults are specified as a ```String``` (ie in ConfigDescriptionParameterBuilder) and should be normalised before being passed to the binding.

For example, the following -:

```
            options = new ArrayList<ParameterOption>();
            options.add(new ParameterOption("65535", "Use On/Off transition time"));
            parameters.add(ConfigDescriptionParameterBuilder.create(CONFIG_ONTRANSITIONTIME, Type.INTEGER)
                    .withLabel("On Transition Time")
                    .withDescription("Time in 10ms intervals to transition from OFF to ON").withDefault("65535")
                    .withMinimum(new BigDecimal(0)).withMaximum(new BigDecimal(60000)).withOptions(options)
                    .withLimitToOptions(false).build());
```

will provide a String when the configuration is read from the channel.

(This is a continuation of the discussion on this OpenHab issue: https://community.openhab.org/t/sitemap-causing-oom/38936/10)

**Summary**:
It looks like there's no restriction on how many objects [SitemapResource::eventOutputs](https://github.com/eclipse/smarthome/blob/dcef6131b70c231a604b4beec5dc9e1769fbb88f/bundles/io/org.eclipse.smarthome.io.rest.sitemap/src/main/java/org/eclipse/smarthome/io/rest/sitemap/internal/SitemapResource.java#L130)  can contain and this can easily lead to an OOM.

title: Statechangelistener prevents GroupItem to be disposed
body:
When a GroupItem registers a StateChangeListener in form of another GroupItem, the deletion of the latter won't remove the StateChangeListener, because the toElement method in ManagedItemProvider creates a new instance of the GroupItem to perform the tidy up task on. Later the removeStateChangeListener of the newly created GroupItem will be called, but this will fail since there are none. The Java GarbageCollector will remove the GroupItem from the ItemRegistryImpl but stops at the old GroupItem, since it's still referenced from the GroupItem which holds the reference on it's listeners. When creating a new GroupItem with the same uid the GroupItem won't add the new GroupItem as a listener, since the overriden equals method of a GenericItem will state them the same, because the comparison isn't done by object id. Thus the listener of the old GroupItem will be used and the new GroupItem won't get updates.
If questions arise i'll be happy to provide additional informations.

Greetings,
maw

title: Bridge nested syntax does not support different thingHandlerFactory for thing
body:
This issue is a follow up from #5301 and refers to a somewhat experimental technology at the moment.

Given are two bundles that share the same binding id. Reasons for this are described in #5301 A prototype for this is the [blukii support](https://github.com/eclipse/smarthome/tree/master/extensions/binding/org.eclipse.smarthome.binding.bluetooth.blukii) or the modbus based [sunspec support](https://github.com/mrbig/openhab2-addons/tree/3216-binding-sunspec-modbus/addons/binding/org.openhab.binding.modbus.sunspec)

The issue arises when the bridge and the connected thing are from different bundles, and the nested syntax is used:

```
Bridge modbus:tcp:se4000 [ ... ] {
    inverter-single-phase myinverter [ ... ]
}
```

Currently these items are silently ignored, because the GenericThingProvider checks the proposed thing with the bridge's ThingHandlerFactory only. [See here](https://github.com/eclipse/smarthome/blob/5528ad5e460e2d8b6412bc34610530c0f2f06a28/bundles/model/org.eclipse.smarthome.model.thing/src/org/eclipse/smarthome/model/thing/internal/GenericThingProvider.xtend#L232)

I propose, that we should rescan every thingHandlerFactory each time the code is recursing into nested bridges/things. To avoid incorrect connection between different bindings may the binding id could been checked and if they don't match then ignore the thingHandlerFactory.


Note: a workaround for this is to ignore the nested syntax in such cases and use flat list with references, so the above could be rewritten as:

title: [astro] Time drift on positional job
body:
The sun elevation is supposed to be calculated at a regular frequency (default is every 300s). However, due to the use of `scheduleWithFixedDelay` for the positional job, which schedules the job starting from the termination of the previous job to the commencement of the next job, there is a small time drift introduced. This time drift can be anywhere from a few milliseconds to 35-40 milliseconds per execution, depending on the CPU speed.

Example of drift:
```
2018-04-30 17:36:52.955 [vent.ItemStateChangedEvent] - SunAzimuth changed from 262.15 to 263.18
2018-04-30 17:41:53.000 [vent.ItemStateChangedEvent] - SunAzimuth changed from 263.18 to 264.20
2018-04-30 17:46:53.042 [vent.ItemStateChangedEvent] - SunAzimuth changed from 264.20 to 265.21
2018-04-30 17:51:53.060 [vent.ItemStateChangedEvent] - SunAzimuth changed from 265.21 to 266.22
2018-04-30 17:56:53.093 [vent.ItemStateChangedEvent] - SunAzimuth changed from 266.22 to 267.21
2018-04-30 18:01:53.090 [vent.ItemStateChangedEvent] - SunAzimuth changed from 267.21 to 268.21
2018-04-30 18:06:53.113 [vent.ItemStateChangedEvent] - SunAzimuth changed from 268.21 to 269.19
2018-04-30 18:11:53.211 [vent.ItemStateChangedEvent] - SunAzimuth changed from 269.19 to 270.18
2018-04-30 18:16:53.241 [vent.ItemStateChangedEvent] - SunAzimuth changed from 270.18 to 271.15
2018-04-30 18:21:53.338 [vent.ItemStateChangedEvent] - SunAzimuth changed from 271.15 to 272.13
2018-04-30 18:26:53.378 [vent.ItemStateChangedEvent] - SunAzimuth changed from 272.13 to 273.10
2018-04-30 18:31:53.422 [vent.ItemStateChangedEvent] - SunAzimuth changed from 273.10 to 274.06
2018-04-30 18:36:53.458 [vent.ItemStateChangedEvent] - SunAzimuth changed from 274.06 to 275.03
```

This drift could be eliminated (or greatly reduced) by the use of `scheduleAtFixedRate` instead of `scheduleWithFixedDelay`.

The guidelines indicate `scheduleWithFixedDelay` is preferred. However, as the astro binding performs accurate calculations, it can be argued that the frequency with which those calculations are performed also should be accurate. Therefore a deviation from the guidelines is warranted.

Reference this forum discussion [here](https://community.openhab.org/t/astro-binding-event-drift/44328)

title: Sitemap updates the wrong widgets after reordering
body:
Let's assume we have a sitemap like this:

```xtend
sitemap test label="Test Sitemap" {
    Frame label="Test Items" {
        Text item=testNumber
        Text item=testDimmer
    }
}
```

It's going to look like this in Basic UI:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2592443/39534945-00250fec-4e33-11e8-8622-adb1cd3f3af6.png)

Now I have a rule that increments the testNumber item's state on a regular basis. 

When I now change the order of the two widgets in the sitemap file like this:

```xtend
sitemap test label="Test Sitemap" {
    Frame label="Test Items" {
        Text item=testDimmer
        Text item=testNumber
    }
}
```

then the Basic UI refreshes automatically and correctly looks like this:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2592443/39535106-5fff5b3e-4e33-11e8-914f-2ca106433536.png)

However, as soon as the numberItem state changes for the next time, it is going to look like this:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2592443/39535153-7f644f5c-4e33-11e8-81d6-36b87fe95990.png)

As you can see, the wrong widget gets updated.

After a quick analysis it looks like the `PageChangeListener` keeps operating with a stale collection of widgets and therefore calculates the widgetIDs wrong. 

This in fact is a regression introduced by #3846. I will push a fix which partially reverts #3846 in a few moments.

body:
As mentioned [here](https://community.openhab.org/t/openhab-2-3-release-candidate-available/45318/29, closures don't work properly anymore. 

The reason is that the terminal rule which was introduced in #4818 had precedence over any other rule and thereby accidentally also "grabbed" the closures.  The `XClosure` also uses the same square-bracket syntax but not on terminal level.

Having looked into this, I don't see a way of fixing it unambiguously. The decision to use square brackets also in the context of quantities simply does not work.

title: [Tradfri] MemoryLeak on connection resume
body:
Whenever the Tradfri binding re-establishes a broken connection to the gateway, it leaks quite some memory to the heap. This is particularly painful when using an unstable link (e.g. via power-line communication). The fact that each instance of the `InMemoryConnectionStore` puts a towel onto 500000 seats (~2MB) by default adds a very painful trait to this:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2592443/40488351-e0d20894-5f66-11e8-91d0-8c98faad06d6.png)

In this case, ~200 MB were aggregated over the time of only 3 days. 

On a first quick glance it looks like the `CoapObserveRelation`s keep themselves entertained by re-trying to connect all the time and thereby re-scheduling themselves. They need to be cancelled explicitly. Not sure yet if there is anything else left to cleanup, especially the restart of the `DTLSConnection` might be dodgy too...

title: ClassCastExceptions when updating SmartHome bundles
body:
migrated from Bugzilla [#478783](https://bugs.eclipse.org/bugs/show_bug.cgi?id=478783)
status NEW severity _normal_ in component _Core_ for _---_
Reported in version _0.8.0_ on platform _PC_
Assigned to: Project Inbox

On 2015-10-01 03:48:27 -0400, Jochen Hiller wrote:

> We are using Eclipse SmartHome running on an OSGi framework where we make on a regular base updates of bundles.
> It happened in rare cases (especially when a bundle does not stop correct) that during the update class loaders can not be cleaned up by the framework. This lead to the situation that after the update some bundles did use object instances from an old class loader.
> This happened for bundles where object instances are shared between bundles, the packages are exported by an Export-Package directive, but NOT imported in bundle via an Import-Package. We changed that in according bundles which did solve this issue.
> 
> There is blog post from Peter Kriens about concepts of Export/Import package since OSGi R4:
> http://blog.osgi.org/2007/04/importance-of-exporting-nd-importing.html
> 
> Peter recommends as a best practice that in standard case all Export-package should be reflected also as an Import-Package. 
> 
> We recommend to apply this best practice to all ESH bundles. We will provide a PullRequest where we change all MANIFEST that every Export-Package will have a corresponding Import-Package.
> 
> Any comments on that? Especially from people running ESH on other frameworks, like Equinox, Felix, Karaf.

On 2015-10-01 04:09:24 -0400, Markus Rathgeb wrote:

> I already stumbled over this topic after starting with OSGi.
> I don't know why this is not done. Perhaps because the Eclipse IDE does not generate that stuff in the Manifest.
> 
> For myself I am using the maven-bundle-plugin for OSGi bundles and delegate the Manifest generation (sometimes with some additional instructions in the pom) to that plugin.
> But the Eclipse IDE does support all that "non Eclipse stuff" (in a comfortable way).

title: Add GroupItemStateChangeEvent
body:
migrated from Bugzilla [#481716](https://bugs.eclipse.org/bugs/show_bug.cgi?id=481716)
status NEW severity _normal_ in component _Core_ for _---_
Reported in version _unspecified_ on platform _PC_
Assigned to: Project Inbox

On 2015-11-09 09:17:54 -0500, Kai Kreuzer wrote:

> The GroupItem itself listens on state changes of its members (in GroupItem.stateChanged()) and recalculates its own state. It does NOT send a a change event for itself though, but only informs all StateChangeListener about it. The old (current) rule engine actually registers as such a StateChangeListener and thus is able to react on Group items even though there is no event.
> 
> It would be nicer if the Group Item publishes a change event as well - it then actually also has the chance to name the item that caused the state change of the group (which is a very regular feature request).

title: postUpdate/sendCommand not synchronous in Rules
body:
migrated from Bugzilla [#478435](https://bugs.eclipse.org/bugs/show_bug.cgi?id=478435)
status UNCONFIRMED severity _normal_ in component _DSL_ for _---_
Reported in version _0.8.0_ on platform _PC_
Assigned to: Project Inbox

On 2015-09-25 12:47:15 -0400, karel goderis wrote:

> With the following simple rule, and with the Item TeslaScheduledDeparture holding a valid value (e.g. not NULL or UNDEF):
> 
> rule "Tesla - initiate variables rule"
> when 
>   System started
> then
>   TeslaScheduledDeparture.postUpdate(UnDefType.UNDEF)
>   logInfo("org.openhab","System Started : TeslaScheduledDeparture "+TeslaScheduledDeparture.state)
> end
> 
> the following is written to the logs:
> 
> 2015-09-25 18:40:12 [DEBUG] [.m.r.r.i.engine.RuleEngineImpl:267  ] - Executing startup rule 'Tesla - initiate variables rule'
> 2015-09-25 18:40:14 [INFO ] [o.e.s.model.script.org.openhab:48   ] - System Started : TeslaScheduledDeparture 2015-09-26T08:30:00
> 
> Does this async behaviour stem from the introduction of the safeCall()s? 
> 
> This is imho undesired behaviour, and leads to adverse effects in Rules. The workaround is to copy over Item.state(s) to locally defined variables at the beginning of each, to do the necessary processing, and at the exit of a rule, write back/postUpdate() any values to the Item.state(s)
> 
> Therefore, should lock()s be introduced on the ItemRegistry?

On 2015-09-26 03:40:32 -0400, Dennis Nobel wrote:

> > Does this async behaviour stem from the introduction of the safeCall()s? 
> 
> No, the safeCalls are executed synchronously. Only if a call takes longer than 10 seconds, the thread will continue to work.
> 
> ItÂ´s because a postUpdate is by definition asynchronously. The whole eventing system only allows asynchronous events.

On 2015-09-26 04:34:11 -0400, karel goderis wrote:

> mhh... do you think this would not lead to problems then? like, you are never sure to have the latest value of an Item when you call .state 
> 
> Is there a recommended approach then for Rules?
> 
> Karel

On 2015-09-26 05:52:39 -0400, Dennis Nobel wrote:

> It depends. Do you really want to query the state of an item directly after you have updated it in a rule? If you sent a command you either donÂ´t know how long it will take before the binding changes the state. The behavior - independent from the eventing system - is just asynchronously.
> 
> What is your concrete use case?
> 
> If you want to get informed that a value was changed you can use the newly introduced ItemStateChangedEvent. This event is sent AFTER an item state was updated.

On 2015-09-26 05:59:06 -0400, karel goderis wrote:

> I understand, but in this case the binding is not the limiting factor. it also happens with Items that are not bound to a binding.
> 
> ItemStateChangedEvent is not yet exposed to the ScriptEngine right?
> 
> K

On 2015-09-26 06:08:40 -0400, Dennis Nobel wrote:

> No itÂ´s not. But I think we donÂ´t need it there, as the Rule engine already has something like "Item MyItem changed" as a trigger. Even if the state of an Item might not be changed at this time, I think usually there is no problem, because you just work with the value from the update event inside the rule.

On 2015-09-26 07:19:08 -0400, karel goderis wrote:

> Ah - that I am afraid does not hold true. At least in my case - you do not only need the value that has effectively changed, but also the latest value of all the there Items, either in or out "Item changed" clauses.
> 
> You either have to build very long complex Rules, with a trigger for every possible variable/Item you need in the rule, or you make a bunch of rules that are less complex, acting on a single Item. In such a constellation, if you update the value of an Item in Rule A, you do need that exact value maybe in Rule B. 
> 
> I can tell you from the use case I have here (automatic charging and pre-heating rules for my Tesla), that these "glitches" are very annoying and troublesome. And that is only relatively simple use case imho
> 
> Karel

> 
> a check should be added to check whether a Job with the same identity exists in the scheduler, and if so, remove the existing job before trying to schedule the new job
>

title: [mqtt-things] Homie device doesn't update its read-only channel
body:
Hi @davidgraeff!

Sorry for bothering you again, but I think that I have found a bug in the mqtt-things binding. As you know, I'm using this script to test my "virtual" Homie 3.0 devices:

```python
import random
import time
import paho.mqtt.client as mqtt

mqtt_broker_host = "localhost"
mqtt_broker_port = 1883
mqtt_client_id = "homie_3.0_temperature_sensor"
mqtt_client_keepalive = 60

homie_prefix = "homie"
homie_version = "3.0.0"
homie_device_id = "homie-3-temperature-sensor"
homie_device_name = "Homie 3.0 Temperature sensor"
homie_device_ip = "192.168.1.150"
homie_device_mac = "DE:AD:BE:EF:FE:ED"
homie_device_nodes = ["temperature"]
homie_device_state = None

def publish_homie_version(client):
    topic = "{}/{}/{}".format(homie_prefix, homie_device_id, "$homie")
    client.publish(topic, homie_version, 1, True)

def advertize_device():
    client.publish("homie/homie-3-temperature-sensor/$state", "init", 1, True)
    publish_device_info()
    publish_node_info()
    client.publish("homie/homie-3-temperature-sensor/$state", "ready", 1, True)

def publish_device_info():
    client.publish("homie/homie-3-temperature-sensor/$homie", homie_version, 1, True)
    client.publish("homie/homie-3-temperature-sensor/$name", homie_device_name, 1, True)
    client.publish("homie/homie-3-temperature-sensor/$localip", homie_device_ip, 1, True)
    client.publish("homie/homie-3-temperature-sensor/$mac", homie_device_mac, 1, True)
    client.publish("homie/homie-3-temperature-sensor/$fw/name", "sensor-firmware", 1, True)
    client.publish("homie/homie-3-temperature-sensor/$fw/version", "1.0.0", 1, True)
    client.publish("homie/homie-3-temperature-sensor/$nodes", "temperature", 1, True)
    client.publish("homie/homie-3-temperature-sensor/$implementation", "homie-python", 1, True)
    client.publish("homie/homie-3-temperature-sensor/$stats/interval", "60", 1, True)

def publish_node_info():
    client.publish("homie/homie-3-temperature-sensor/temperature/$name", "Indoor temperature", 1, True)
    client.publish("homie/homie-3-temperature-sensor/temperature/$type", "Temperature", 1, True)
    client.publish("homie/homie-3-temperature-sensor/temperature/$properties", "temperature", 1, True)

    client.publish("homie/homie-3-temperature-sensor/temperature/temperature", 23, 1, True)
    client.publish("homie/homie-3-temperature-sensor/temperature/temperature/$name", "Indoor temperature", 1, True)
    client.publish("homie/homie-3-temperature-sensor/temperature/temperature/$settable", "false", 1, True)
    client.publish("homie/homie-3-temperature-sensor/temperature/temperature/$unit", "ºC", 1, True)
    client.publish("homie/homie-3-temperature-sensor/temperature/temperature/$datatype", "float", 1, True)
    client.publish("homie/homie-3-temperature-sensor/temperature/temperature/$format", "-20:120", 1, True)

def on_connect(client, userdata, flags, rc):
    print("Connected with result code {}".format(rc))
    advertize_device()


def on_message(client, userdata, msg):
    print("{} -> {}".format(msg.topic, msg.payload))


def loop():
    last_temperature_time = 0
    while True:
        if (time.time() - last_temperature_time) > 5:
            temperature_value = random.uniform(20,25)
            print("Sending tempertaure value: {0:.2f}ºC".format(temperature_value))
            client.publish("homie/homie-3-temperature-sensor/temperature/temperature", "{0:.2f}".format(temperature_value), 1, True)
            last_temperature_time = time.time()
        time.sleep(1)


client = mqtt.Client(mqtt_client_id)
client.on_connect = on_connect
client.on_message = on_message

client.will_set("homie/homie-3-temperature-sensor/$state", "lost", 1, True)

client.connect(mqtt_broker_host, mqtt_broker_port, mqtt_client_keepalive)

client.loop_start()

try:
    loop()
except KeyboardInterrupt:
    print("Stopping client")
    client.publish("homie/homie-3-temperature-sensor/$state", "disconnected", 1, True)
    client.disconnect()
    client.loop_stop()
```
The device is discovery perfectly and the thing is imported flawlessly, with its "Indoor temperature" channel. The problem is that, although the script is configured to send a new temperature value each 5 seconds (a random value between 20 and 25), the item is never updated and I can see the following message in the karaf console:

```
13:48:38.718 [WARN ] [ng.mqtt.generic.internal.ChannelState] - Received MQTT data on homie/homie-3-temperature-sensor/temperature/temperature. This channel is read only!
```
If the Homie property is read-only (not settable), the binding should not subscribe to the "/set" topic, but in this case the binding is blocking the "common" state topic. Are you aware of this problem? Otherwise, I haven't encountered any problem, awesome work!

Best regards and keep up with the good job,

Aitor

title: [MQTT] brokerId must be a configuration parameter of a broker
body:
In ESH, EVERY thing/bridge must have at least one configuration parameter. The instance must NOT be determined by the ThingUID.

The MQTT Broker type is incorrectly modelled. `AbstractBrokerHandler` does a
```
this.brokerID = thing.getUID().getId();
```
Instead, this id must be taken from the Thing configuration (and thus must be declared in the config descriptions).

body: Server responds with a 500 Request failed error when we try to update a rule by adding a new trigger of type 'GenericEventTrigger' or 'TimerTrigger' (trigger configuration not specified). The new triggers is however added to the server.

title: BaseThingHandler.editThing() does not preserver State
body:
When calling this method somewhere in the Handler, then a new Thing is created, and assigned to handler.thing, but in the process the State of the original Thing is not preserved or copied over (but is set to the default UNINITIALIZED). Moreover, the Thing assigned to handler.thing is not the same object instance as the one that is tracked by the ThingManager. That means that for example in the osgi console, the Thing can be "ONLINE", but the Thing referenced by the handler will be UNINITIALIZED
(See also https://www.eclipse.org/forums/index.php/t/1072808/)

title: Synchronous Execution of Astro Startup Jobs and minor fixes
body:
The scheduling operations schedules few jobs and executes 2 specific jobs immediately. These two jobs are executed in a different thread to prevent blocking the thread that spawns it. 

In addition, during handler initialize, channel linking and unlinking, we reschedule the jobs. And every time, before we reschedule the jobs, we remove the jobs from the ESH Core scheduler that are associated with the current thing.

As the jobs that execute immediately are handled by different threads, it is sometime noticed that while rescheduling, removal of jobs did occur after the jobs got rescheduled. This created unexpected issues in ESH Core scheduler. In this PR, we have rendered the asynchronous operations of executing immediate jobs in different threads to synchronous execution so that we can make sure the removal always happens before rescheduling.

Another note is that previously we required `equals` and `hashcode` to be overriden by `AbstractJob` but currently it is not used anymore. These `equals` and `hashcode` affected normal executions of scheduled jobs as well. Hence, the methods have been removed.

title: [Core] Added support for quoted strings in rule triggers
body:
According to #2826, the following works

```xtext
rule "Test Rule 1"
when
    Item test changed to world
then
    // This is IS working
end
```

while the following is NOT working:

```xtext
rule "Test Rule 2"
when
    Item test changed to "world"
then
    // This is NOT working
end
```

With this PR, I so far have only added a test-case for this. And indeed it fails and results as expected in 

```
testChangedEventTrigger_withoutQuotes(org.eclipse.smarthome.model.rule.runtime.internal.engine.RuleTest)  Time elapsed: 0.639 sec
testChangedEventTrigger_withQuotes(org.eclipse.smarthome.model.rule.runtime.internal.engine.RuleTest)  Time elapsed: 0.034 sec  <<< FAILURE!
org.junit.ComparisonFailure: expected:<[world]> but was:<["world"]>
	at org.junit.Assert.assertEquals(Assert.java:115)
	at org.junit.Assert.assertEquals(Assert.java:144)
	at org.eclipse.smarthome.model.rule.runtime.internal.engine.RuleTest.assertUpdateTriggerWithNewState(RuleTest.java:82)
	at org.eclipse.smarthome.model.rule.runtime.internal.engine.RuleTest.testChangedEventTrigger_withQuotes(RuleTest.java:66)
```

So the quotes somehow end up inside the string! 

It looks like this behavior gets better when defining the trigger in [Rules.xtext](https://github.com/eclipse/smarthome/blob/09d8095efe9933216874e488b379cd9a10aa85e2/bundles/model/org.eclipse.smarthome.model.rule/src/org/eclipse/smarthome/model/rule/Rules.xtext) instead as

```xtext
ChangedEventTrigger:
	'Item' item=ItemName 'changed' ('from' oldState=ValidState)? ('to' newState=ValidState)?
;		
ValidState:
	ID | Number | STRING
;
```

directly like this:

```xtext
ChangedEventTrigger:
	'Item' item=ItemName 'changed' ('from' oldState=(ID|Number|STRING)? ('to' newState=(ID|Number|STRING))?
;		
```

However, we then would lose the nice way of integrating the content proposal in [RulesProposalProvider.java](https://github.com/eclipse/smarthome/blob/3ae5d7b1b284f2bde6199bfe8dad950fd38cae39/bundles/model/org.eclipse.smarthome.model.rule.ui/src/org/eclipse/smarthome/model/rule/ui/contentassist/RulesProposalProvider.xtend). So there must be a better way to "trick" xtext into behaving well. Any suggestions? @chriskn or @cdietrich maybe?

relates to #2826

title: [Core] Fixed daylight saving time (DST) bug in scheduled jobs
body:
While searching for possible future execution candidates there is a
problem if a change from standard time to daylight saving time occurs.

This time jump forward leads to a duplicate of a date. For example in
Europe, Germany SUN 2018 Mar 25 3:00:00 exists TWICE because the time was
shifted from 2am to 3am.

While pruning the execution candidates we only kept the next 2 whereas the
first usually is the current time, which leaves the 2nd candidate to be
the final one. If the time change occurs we only have 2 same dates which
both are the current time and thus both are discarded.

With this PR I have changed the implementation to keep 3 candidates, so
there will be a future execution date left.

Fixes #5294
Fixes #3185

title: Do not use invalid filenames on Windows for JSON storage
body:
Windows has a rather long list of forbidden characters in filenames, see

https://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/aa365247(VS.85).aspx

Linux-like systems only disallow / and the null-byte.

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filename#Reserved_characters_and_words

By URLencoding the string, all of these characters are safely transformed
into %<HexValue> and % is an allowed character. This encoding is even
reversible.

Given that we will not run on RT-11 systems we should be safe.

I use a maximum length of 127 to be safe even on android systems:
https://stackoverflow.com/questions/13204807/max-file-name-length-in-android

The down-side is that even spaces are now converted into %20, but I chose
to use URLencoder.encode instead of implementing the conversion by myself.

For existing storages I check whether a file exists and keep using it.

Fixes #5687

title: Internal ISRs should not be exposed to the user
body:
Several drivers use internal ISRs that are installed when the constructor or a start-type method is called. These sensors do not offer the the possibility of installing any other ISR; don’t have any insatallISR()-type methods like other sensors do. 
In conclusion, the access level should be set to private.

These are:
beatISR() from GrooveEHR
flowISR() from GroveWFS
signalAISR() from RotaryEncoder

title: Mpr121 configAN3944 CDT register has invalid value
body:
in  [configAN3944](https://github.com/intel-iot-devkit/upm/blob/master/src/mpr121/mpr121.cxx#L150) the CDT register is set to 0x04 which is an invalid value. Consequences are:
- lock-in of the sensor to "touched" state when touched for long periods of time ( > 10 seconds)
- lock-in sensor  to "touched" state when left alone for more than an hour
  
  The CDT part of register 0x5D (Highest 3 bits) should at least be set to 001 as indicated in the Application Note AN3889 , as you can see from the below screenshot of the application note:

![screen shot 2016-05-19 at 1 12 48 pm](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/3643758/15403179/bcae4340-1dc5-11e6-9662-0a5e1c138e76.png)

in the current [configAN3944](https://github.com/intel-iot-devkit/upm/blob/master/src/mpr121/mpr121.cxx#L150) the highest 3 bits of 0x5D are set to 000 which is invalid.

![screen shot 2016-05-19 at 1 12 55 pm](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/3643758/15403213/f103d54c-1dc5-11e6-9eb4-10b94cd2154a.png)

Shouldn't this be declared as **_'int_**'?

title: Rules timer bug.
body:
I think I have found another minor bug in the rules engine.  When you have a timer running and want to cancel it for whatever reason the command is is to set the timer to 0.  (timerset,1,0)
What happens is the command is recognized but the result in the log is Event: Rules#timer=1.  This does not cancel the rule.  It has the effect of just shortening it because what ever is supposed to happen when the timer expires still does.  

In short, the timer is not actually cancelled. Whatever logic is defined to occur when it expires naturally is still executed.

title: turn off log2ram
body:
log2ram maps 50M of ram.  Logs are rotated weekly and stay uncompressed in the /var/log directory.  When this happens, the /var/log directory will eventually explode, and no log can be written. (ever).   And we lost 50megs of memory

To fix this problem, 
solution 1:
Tune /var/log  such that log2ram maps to a directory that max can ever be is less than few megabytes.  And logrotate to somewhere else.

solution 2:
stop using log2ram and use what ever it is there.

# Bug

- **TOOLCHAIN**
    ARC GNU 2017.03.

- **BOARD**
    EMSK 2.3

- **ARC CORE**
    EM7D.

## Bug Description
   Take secret_secure under example/baremetal/secureshield as example, other examples share the same issue.
   When build the example using command:
make BOARD=emsk BD_VER=23 CUR_CORE=arcem7d TOOLCHAIN=gnu OLEVEL=O0

In console, any command invoke main cause a exception:

COM1>main -h
soft interrupt 1 interrupt handler
../../../../library/secureshield/core/src/v2/secureshield_sjli.c: Line 121: halt reason:interface @253c0 not found in container 1

But build without OLEVEL=O0 works fine.

The problem is caused by sjli instruction: when invoke sjli instruction, the registers for parameters are set before a call to arc_lock_save (in secureshield_secure_call_exports.h line 103-118), when build with O0, the call to function arc_lock_save is a function call and destroyed r0 and r2, that are the parameters for sjli. When build is O2, gcc optimize the function call out and only generated a clri instruction like this:
     81a:       272f 013f               clri    r4

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Enhancement
   To make the code independent of optimization level, either move the function call before set of parameter registers or use clri and seti instruction directly.

title: Bug in interrupt handling without storing DSP/FPU registers
body:
# Issue Summary
- **Type**: *Bug* 
- **Category**: *BSP* 
- **Release Version**: Specified version such as 2016.05 or All

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Bug

## Development Environment
- **HOST OS**: Windows 10, 64bit

- **TOOLCHAIN**: MWDT L-2017.06

- **BOARD**: EMSK 2.3

- **ARC CORE**: Any

## Bug Description
   FPU and DSP registers are not saved during handling of interrupts and exceptions, This may lead to undefined behavior.
For my case: I have a thread that has a division operation, and there is a **vKernelTick** which is the ISR of tick timer of freertos port. This interrupt has also a division operation in calling of **board_timer_update**. **MW** is optimizing the local variables in case of division and use the **accl** and **acch** registers, so if the tick interrupt happens  after performing the division operation and before using **accl** or **acch** register, there will be a corrupted values in those registers when returning from the ISR where an exception happened and the arc_reset is called.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Enhancement
   Adding the following code to INTERRUPT_PROLOGUE and EXCEPTION_PROLOGUE at **arc_asm_common.h**
```
#if ARC_FEATURE_FPU_DSP_CONTEXT
	SAVE_R58_R59
	SAVE_FPU_REGS
	SAVE_DSP_REGS
#endif
```
and the following to INTERRUPT_EPILOGUE and EXCEPTION_EPILOGUE
```
#if ARC_FEATURE_FPU_DSP_CONTEXT
	RESTORE_DSP_REGS
	RESTORE_FPU_REGS
	RESTORE_R58_R59
#endif
```
same as SAVE_CALLEE_REGS and RESTORE_CALLEE_REGS.

title: Setting color values individually
body:
### Where are you using pytradfri (eg stand-alone, Home Assistant etc)
Stand-alone

### Version of pytradfri
5.2.1

### Expected behaviour
```
lamp.light_control.set_hsb(1000, 1000, None)
```
Above code should update hue and saturation, but leave brightness unchanged. This is the behaviour of 5.2.0

### Actual behaviour
Program crashes with the following (partial) traceback:

```
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.6/site-packages/pytradfri/device.py", line 224, in set_hsb
    self._value_validate(brightness, RANGE_BRIGHTNESS, "Brightness")
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.6/site-packages/pytradfri/device.py", line 266, in _value_validate
    if value < rnge[0] or value > rnge[1]:
TypeError: '<' not supported between instances of 'NoneType' and 'int'
```

In other words. The value validation I wrote blocks this type of use.

### Solution
The easiest solution is changing the value validation to allow `None` as a value. 

See PR #139

title: vscpl1_usb2candrv.dll not able to open more than one interface
body:
System: Windows 7-64, latest release of vscpd/works, USB2CAN interface with firmware 1.5 (latest)

Neither the usb2can.dll provided by 8devices nor the vscpl1_usb2candrv.dll provided in:
https://github.com/grodansparadis/vscp_software/tree/master/src/vscp/drivers/level1/usb2can

is able to open more than one CAN interface at any one time. This seems to be known problem, as in file
https://github.com/grodansparadis/vscp_software/blob/master/src/vscp/drivers/level1/usb2can/usb2can/common/dlldrvobj.h
line 41 the maximum number of opened drivers is limited to 1. Changing this constant from 1 to 256 does not change the behaviour - still only one channel can be opened, further calls to CanalOpen() will not do anything but return an error.

Furthermore the handle returned by CanalOpen() is always 1681 for any number of usb2can-interfaces on the same machine.

That said, it seems that in file
https://github.com/grodansparadis/vscp_software/blob/master/src/vscp/drivers/level1/usb2can/usb2can/common/dlldrvobj.cpp
in line 178 we get always 1681 as handle. This may be the case because the break in line 179 always breaks the for-loop counting through all interfaces.

Sadly even with removing the break (which seems to be obvious) the dll is still not able to open multiple interfaces - but the returned handle now changes, at least sometimes, to values of 1681, 1682, 1683 and 1684 (and probably more) - but still only one usb2can is delivering data.

Reproduction:
1. have two usb2can-interfaces with different serial numbers,

install_dependencies:

title: Setting single node property re-uses range from previous set
body:
This defect is against 2.0 (master)

If you set a node property using a range, like this:

```
Homie
  .setNodeProperty(valvesNode, PROPERTY_TIME)
  .setRange(valve)
  .send(String(time));
```

and then later set a single (non-range) property, like this:

```
Homie
  .setNodeProperty(batteryNode, PROPERTY_VOLTAGE)
  .send(String(voltageCoefficientSetting.get() * ESP.getVcc()));
```

The second set re-uses the left-over range value from the previous set.  In my case, the first set, above uses topic `devices/sprinklers/valves/time_6` and then the second set incorrectly sends `devices/sprinklers/powerUSB/voltage_6` when it should be just `devices/sprinklers/powerUSB/voltage`.  This is because HomieClass::setNodeProperty() doesn't clear the range when generating and returning the SendingPromise.

setNodeProperty() should clear the range in the sendingPromise before returning it.

I have a pull request for your consideration, coming shortly.

title: Bug when using getMqttClient() feature.
body:
Hi,
When using the `Homie.getMqttClient();` feature the OnMessage callback is called but topic argument is not complete.

This is due to the BootNormal.cpp OnMessage callback that suppress '/' and remplace those by '\0' vithin the topic buffer variable(which will be then given to our custom OnMessage callback).
Topic is shorten until node, property and  set field are behind the end_of_string.

I agree that this bug appears depending on in which order OnMessage callback are registered, but this seems a bit dirty when processing message to not check device-id while subscription are possible for any MQTT topic.

I made a fix to BootNormal.cpp, the fix consist in verifying that arriving message are destinated to current device-id (after processing for Broadcast messages)

title: FYI : Don't use lengthy string for HomieNode name
body:
Don't use big strings in (eg;relay012345544444)

**HomieNode lightNode1("relay012345544444", "switch");** 

it will keep crashing your ESP8266.

_If you ESP is crashing without any message (at boot time) then this is the cause._

NOTE : I am on develop branch and this is the same issue on Master branch too.

-Venkat

title: Not following the OTA protocol causes the board to panic
