title: [gen 3] [bootloader] External flash sleep refactoring
body:
### Problem

We've introduced an incompatibility in the bootloader with older versions of system firmware in the releases containing https://github.com/particle-iot/device-os/pull/1725.

When you have a bootloader that has this feature on your device, before we jump into the system-part1 the QSPI flash is put into low power mode and requires a special command to wake it up. So, when you have a system-part1 that doesn't send that special command, the QSPI flash is left in low power mode and anything dealing with it fails, e.g. filesystem.

### Solution

This PR does a couple of things:

1. External QSPI flash is no longer implicitly being put into lower power mode when executing `hal_exflash_uninit()`. This call only disables the QSPI peripheral on nRF52840. 
2. External flash sleep functionality has been decoupled into `hal_exflash_special_command()` with `HAL_EXFLASH_COMMAND_SLEEP` and `HAL_EXFLASH_COMMAND_WAKEUP` commands.
3. `core_hal` sleep functions no explicitly call `hal_exflash_special_command()` to put the external flash into sleep mode.
4. `hal_exflash_init()` still implicitly wakes up the external flash, but now through a call to `hal_exflash_special_command()`

### Steps to Test

1. 0.9.0 + bootloader from this branch shouldn't cause a panic mode
2. bootlader and system-part1 from this branch shouldn't case a panic mode
3. Deep sleep and STOP mode sleep tests should pass as previously

title: [Electron/LTE] devices drop Cloud connection every time user firmware opens and closes a TCP socket [ch34976]
body:
### Problem

LTE E-series R410 devices drop Cloud connection every time user firmware opens and closes a TCP socket.  This does not appear to affect U260/U201/G350 devices.

### Root cause
The timeout for the socket close command USOCL times out after 10s (has been this way since the first electron release).  Sara R410M timeout of this command is 120 seconds, but that is likely only for TCP sockets since UDP sockets can be closed immediately.  Sara U201/260/G350 timeout of this command is 1 second.  If the TCP socket took more than 10 seconds to close, the USOCL command would timeout and allow the AT interface to be accessed by the next command, but it would not ready because it's still waiting for the socket close command to finish or timeout.  If a following command happens to be a Particle Publish, Keep Alive Ping or Vitals Publish, these commands are blocked by the TCP socket closing and subsequently forces a teardown of the Cloud connection.  

### Solution
Timeouts will are adjusted so that if the socket is a TCP socket, the full 120 second timeout is respected.  If it's a UDP socket, we will continue to optimize this value down to 10 seconds.

### Steps to Test

Requires a TCP connection to a server that defaults to the `Connection: keep-alive\r\n` state, and closes slowly when `TCPClient::stop()` is called.  This is not a common case, and at this time of writing only one customer server is known to behave this way and will be tested internally.  If other public servers are noted with this issue, this PR will be updated with a test app that demonstrates this behavior and this test app will be added to the internal on-device tests.

### Workaround for slowly closing TCP sockets
Add `Connection: close\r\n` to your request header.  This should cause an immediate remote close of the socket from the server when all data has been sent by the server.

[electron, gen3] Temporarily increase IDLE task priority whenever a thread exits (calls vTaskDelete)
body:
### Problem

Due to the busy-loop nature of the application thread and higher priority (2) FreeRTOS IDLE thread responsible for thread resources cleanup (stack) is not being given CPU time, causing memory leaks, unless the application thread goes into a blocked state (waiting on a synchronization primitive or delaying).  This could cause the device to be stuck "blinking green" until reset.

### Solution

Temporarily increase IDLE thread priority to `configMAX_PRIORITIES - 1` (maximum) whenever `vTaskDelete(NULL)` is called using `portPRE_TASK_DELETE_HOOK` to clean up the stack as soon as possible and restore it back to `tskIDLE_PRIORITY` once IDLE thread runs using idle hook.

### Steps to Test

Set a breakpoint to `vApplicationIdleHook`, make some thread exit, it should get executed.

title: Fix/reload dct functions
body:
### Problem

Particle Update fails to update a Photon/P1 from Device OS <1.2.1-rc.3 to 1.2.1 via DFU mode. This is caused by that after updating the system parts, the address of DCT functions that resided in system parts aren't consistent, so when bootloader tries accessing the DCT after that, it then crashes.

### Solution

Dirty a flag after every DFU write operation to the internal flash, so that after updating the system parts, next time when bootloader calls DCT functions, it will reload the DCT functions to make sure that the address of the DCT functions in new system parts are valid.

### Steps to Test

1. Build and flash the new bootloader
2. Flash older DeviceOS e.g. 1.0.0 onto the device
3. Reset and go into DFU
4. Write into DCT
5. Write system-part1 and system-part2 of DeviceOS release v1.2.1 without resetting
6. Write into DCT again, this should succeed and not crash the device

### Problem

The reset pin (RST) on the side of the Argon is unable to reset the board by another board using a GPIO (e.g. a Xenon).

We saw two kinds of symptoms of this issue:
1. Argon cannot be reset
2. Argon can be reset, but the reset pin on Argon goes from 3.3V to 1.6V and wait for around 500ms, then it goes to 0V.

### Solution
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/7424522/62269137-adf8be00-b464-11e9-8b93-3a8ba34368ee.png)

As we can see from the picture, if we configure WIFI_EN(ESPEN) pin to OUTPUT high, the voltage decline a little after the D2 diode, given there is a pull-up resistor R30 100k, we should configuration WIFI_EN(ESPEN) pin to open drain.


### Steps to Test
#### failed case
1. Configure WIFI_EN(ESPEN) as output mode
1. Download below application to two Argon, connect Argon-A's D8 pin to Argon-B's reset pin
1. Observe the symptoms

#### Successful case
1. Configure WIFI_EN(ESPEN) as the open-drain mode
1. Repeat the above steps

    pinMode(D8, OUTPUT);
    digitalWrite(D8, 0);

- Due to a regression introduced in 1.1.0, the system layer always sends its handshake messages, even if the session was resumed. This causes increased data usage.

- User module isn't initialized in monolithic builds.

title: [nrf52840] platform: disable clock driver in Reset_System() before jumping into system firmware
body:
### Problem

Originally reported in https://community.particle.io/t/workbench-local-flash-occasionally-requires-hard-reset/52744

The main issue is that `POWER_CLOCK_IRQn` interrupt comes in immediately after we jump from bootloader into the system part and before we initialize all the necessary power/clock related things in the Nordic SDK which causes a jump to `0x00000000` because the clock event handler has not been registered.

The problem comes from the fact that we are not stopping the clocks or disabling interrupts (all or at least `POWER_CLOCK_IRQn` specifically) before jumping into the system part.

I have no explanation on why we haven't seen this previously, perhaps a compiler started optimizing things slightly differently due to the Nordic SDK update in 1.2.1.

Surprisingly the event that causes the interrupt is `EVENTS_LFCLKSTARTED`, despite the fact that we have a busy loop waiting for LFCLK to start in `Set_System()`

#### Stack trace

```
#0  nrfx_clock_irq_handler () at nrf5_sdk/modules/nrfx/drivers/src/nrfx_clock.c:335
#1  <signal handler called>
#2  Set_System () at MCU/nRF52840/src/hw_config.c:75
#3  0x00048778 in HAL_Core_Config () at src/nRF52840/core_hal.c:301
#4  0x000302aa in Reset_Handler () at ../../../build/arm/startup/spark_init.S:3
```

#### Affected versions

Bootloaders in DeviceOS 1.2.1 - 1.4.1.

### Solution

Mask `POWER_CLOCK_IRQn` interrupt in `Reset_System()` before jumping into system firmware. It will get re-enabled again once clock driver is initialized.

### Steps to Test

I was able to reproduce this issue so far only in some cases on Borons only either:

1. Flashing a bootloader binary 1.2.1+ over serial repeatedly (at least with 1.4.1 DeviceOS on device)
2. Quickly clicking reset button once the device boots into system firmware

Building Boron bootloader out of this branch (or using [boron-bootloader-1948.zip](https://github.com/particle-iot/device-os/files/3740722/boron-bootloader-1948.zip)) and flashing onto the device should resolve the issue.

### Binaries

[boron-bootloader-1948.zip](https://github.com/particle-iot/device-os/files/3740722/boron-bootloader-1948.zip)

Boron 2G/3G devices are having a hard time connecting to the cellular tower due to a few issues:

title: [Gen 3] Workaround for QSPI/XIP nRF52840 hardware anomaly 215
body:
### Problem

See #1832 

https://infocenter.nordicsemi.com/index.jsp?topic=%2Ferrata_nRF52840_Rev2%2FERR%2FnRF52840%2FRev2%2Flatest%2Fanomaly_840_215.html&anchor=anomaly_840_215

The gist of the problem is that we concurrently access the external QSPI flash through two different mechanisms: QSPI peripheral and XIP (maps the external flash into the microcontroller memory space). As outlined in the anomaly description, the access to certain QSPI registers after the access to XIP region may lead to a complete CPU lockup. In our testing it showed also that under some circumstances it's not a complete lockup, but a failure to communicate with the QSPI flash.

### Solution

The original plan was to any and all usage of XIP (currently used for OTA and module info retreival e.g. when sending a describe, validating modules, doing a particle serial inspect).

However, instead we've figured out an alternative approach in using the workarounds suggested by Nordic in conjunction with RTOS critical sections in particular pieces of external flash HAL to prevent other threads from accessing the XIP region while we are performing the operation on the QSPI peripheral.

There is a slight performance impact, however. I've added benchmarking to exflash_hal and the results while heavily writing into the filesystem are:

1. On average we'll be spending **~1.2ms** with RTOS scheduler disabled while performing certain QSPI operations (like write and erase). This should be pretty much insignificant, as the RTOS scheduler resolution is 1ms.
2. The maximum time I've seen RTOS scheduler disabled due to applied workaround was **5.7ms**, however such values were seen only during early initialization and there were no spikes seen after than with values stabilizing at **~1.2ms**

This PR also fixes issues with EC public key handling, which caused a DCT write on every boot.

title: [Gen 3] Fixes renegotiation of options and adds IPCP packet parsing
body:
### Problem

1. We sometimes see that the devices establish the PPP link, however remain stuck in blinking green. This is caused by the remote side changing offered DNS servers during the negotiation (i.e. it offers one set first and then after we accept if, for some reason offers another).
2. IPCP packets are not easy to debug and are dumped raw
3. [B5 SoM] For some reason we are not receiving CREG/CGREG/CEREG URCs on muxed AT channel and they only appear in the muxed data channel, which causes us to not notice loss of carrier.

### Solution

1. All default IPCP options (IP addresses, Primary/Secondary DNS) are now overridable by the remote side. Once the PPP link is established, we now also check whether we've agreed on a set of DNS servers, and if not, teardown the link.
2. IPCP packet parsing is added.
3. [B5 SoM] Adds `AT+QCFG="cmux/urcport",1` to receive URCs only on muxed AT channel.

This PR also disables IPV6CP.

### Steps to Test

1. Force the device (b5som) into a state where it'll throw `Peer NAK'd an option unknown to us`, it should connect succesfully
2. Build monolithic DeviceOS with `DEBUG_BUILD=y`, IPCP packet dumps should be visible in the logs

title: [Gen 2] Fixes socket leak in UDP.begin()
body:
### Problem

`UDP::begin()` can be called when already active with an open socket. It will unconditionally create open a new socket and discard its reference to the old socket while leaving it open.

If this sequence is repeated the system can run out of socket handles preventing new UDP sockets from being opened and even preventing cloud connection.

While users should call `UDP::end()` to close any open socket before a new `UDP::begin()` the implementation should defensively check for and close an open socket on `UDP::begin()`.

**NOTE: this bug only applies to Gen 2 devices**

### Solution

Call `stop()` in `begin()`.

This PR also frees up some flash space in `wiring/no_fixture` test suite for cellular platforms, as we started to overflow.

### Steps to Test

Run `wiring/no_fixture` tests on Gen 2 and Gen 3 platforms. All tests can be excluded (`E` command) except for `MDM_01_socket_writes_with_length_more_than_1023_work_correctly` on cellular platforms and `UDP_begin_does_not_leak_sockets_without_calling_stop` on all the platforms (`i` command to enable the tests selectively).

Thank you for contributing! ```
### Problem Signal strength on Gen2 is collected using CSQ command. 1. This command does not provide quality value on Gen2 2. This command is quite unreliable, meaning that is sometimes gives invalid signal strength value in an expectedly solid cell coverage location. u-blox recommends to use UCGED command, which is expected to work more reliably than the CSQ command. ### Solution Replace CSQ command with UCGED for R410M radio. UCGED gives RSRP/RSRQ in dBm/dB and CSQ gives in index values. RSRP/RSRQ from UCGED are converted from dBm/dB to CESQ-type index values and further processed. **Implementation:** - Hard-bounding values for RSRP in [-200,0] and assign error value otherwise(255) - Hard-bounding values for RSRQ in [-20,0] and assign error value otherwise(255) - Check that UCGED contains valid values for both RSRP and RSRQ string, else call it an error - No retry algorithm on the UCGED command - In a multiple-response UCGED command, uses the first set of values as the correct readings and ignore the rest ### Steps to Test Manual testing required here 1. Check that correct signal strength and quality are reported by comparing the values reported by the previous Device OS and the values reported by your code for the same device in the same location. 2. title: Fire Hazard, Wrong bitmask is provided for 4208
body:
In the Power Management, there is a function for setting the cut off voltage which takes an integer and converts it to the appropriate bit mask.

When sending in 4.208 volts (the upper bound on the LiPo battery provided with spark kits) it sets the voltage to 4.4 volts. This has caused units on our test bench to fail, and could cause fires if using any other standard LiPo battery that doesn't have a limit circuit installed in the battery.

I am not sure how to complete all of the required steps to get this through your processes, but see this bug as a danger, and would appreciate any help in getting it implemented. Or if someone else can do the unit testing required to get it passed I would not mind them taking over the issue.

title: Fixes issue #498 where `particle update` fails on Photon/P1
body:
## Problem

When updating system firmware with `particle update` with CLI 1.43.0 on Photon/P1, the device locks up at the last step where DCT is written to.

## Solution

**Short term solution:** Need to flash Bootloader and OTA Flag before system parts for Photon/P1 because as soon as the system parts are flashed they will change the location of DFU read/write functions which live in system firmware.

**Long term solution:** Add a dirty flag in Device OS that would cause the bootloader to reload DCT functions from system parts if their flash area has been modified.  Will be added to a future Device OS release.

## Reference

Fixes #498 
https://community.particle.io/t/device-os-1-2-1-and-particle-cli-1-43-fail-in-particle-update/51140

title: Improvement: Sensors/Zone Communication
body:
If your temperature sensor doesn't communicate or you have no temperature reading for a time:
during the night database clean-up removed old records, in result it get reading 0 and frost protection kicks in (it will probably keep going until the sensor starts working). Not good if you are on holidays.

**Suggestion:** Would be good if code could fault the zone if there is no temperature reading for a time or no comms with zone relay (so you don't turn on boiler when you can't communicate with zone controller), and then you have something in place to indicate zone fault on main screen.

For that one you probably need changes in boiler logic to mark zone fault, new column in zone table to mark it faulty for display on webpage and you need to force sending valid temperature reading from the sensor even if it didn't change from time to time.

title: Improvement: Stop Boiler if Gateway/RPI loss of communication
body:
if boiler is running, and your gateway goes down or pi is powered down/crashed. Your boiler relay will remain on as it won't get any new command. 
**Suggestion:** 
Fix would be easy, have a new variable, that is reset to 0 every time you receive a message (you should receive message roughly every minute).
In loop(){} have wait() and then increase the variable if the variable exceeds some set value turn off the boiler relay. That way if you don't get any command for a time it will knock off the relay.
Note: Same does not apply to zone relay for safety reason as it cause not problem if we leave zone open.

bug

**Details**

_Summary of bug_
ZmNinja uses an event summary pullup window accessed via the events side menu. In it's closed state it appears as a yellow coloured tab at the bottom of the screen. The event summary pull up window can be activated (pulled up) by either tapping the yellow tab or dragging the yellow tab up. Tapping the tab expands the window and shows the event summary data, however **if you drag the tab up** there is no summary information shown **initially** on first run.

_Sequence required in order to show bug_
To show this bug it is important to exit zmNinja and restart it and perform these steps in the following sequence. 
1. Select _events_ from side menu. Drag up yellow pullup tab **(Don't tap to pull up)** you will find that no event data is shown in the pull up footer, only the titles, "1 hour Summary", "1 day Summary", "1 week Summary", "1 month Summary". (At first I thought these titles were supposed to be buttons that didn't seem to work as I tend swipe up pull up tabs not tap pull up tabs).
2. Now tap the yellow tab. There may be a second or so delay but then the pullup window will be populated with event data.
3. If you now make-sure a number of additional events have occurred and drag up (not tap) the event window again. It's now populated with events but does not show the new events just the same number of events we saw earlier. Tapping the tab will update the window and show the additional events.

So in summary the pull up footer does not update event data when dragged/swiped up rather than tapped.

title: Portals that implement redirects don't work with web scrape (Wizard)

title: Image review via progress slider fails to navigate.
body:
**Platform & OS Version**

Android 8.0.0

**The version of zmNinja you are reporting:**

1.3.039

**The version of ZoneMinder you are using:**

1.32.3

**Device details:**

Samsung Galaxy 8 (more info on demand)

**What is the nature of your issue**

Bug

**Details**

When using zmNinja for Android, I cannot navigate through jpegs like I can on the electron version for linux. When I try to move via the progress bar, it goes back to 1x @ 0s and the "video" stops. Obviously I don't have this problem when I have x246 encoding turned on in zoneminder, but I wanted to save the processing power as my machine recording is low powered and the chickens alarm the thing all the time (it's not like my foscams have sound capabilities :P)  I suspect this is a touch vs click event thing... title: Fix: missing RegisterAPI.war file in linux setup
body: The comment mentioned after the `OS=linux` is removed. This comment was getting selected for the OS parameter, which is not needed.

title: Fix: Changed IP address of LDAP Docker for Linux
body:
https://github.com/moby/moby/issues/17305
Details of the fix can be found above

title: REST API /engine/start v1.9.0 breaks when starting a started tenant.
MongoDB calls fail when authentication is enabled
body: When using authenticated access to MongoDB, database calls fail due to authentication errors. The existing code assumes that user credentials are in the *sitewhere * database, which for most users is not the case. Add ability to specify authentication database when using credentials for MongoDB.

title: Every call to user management 'authenticate()' results in update
body: The user management authenticate() call always updates the last login date, which results in a database update. The authenticate call is used by Spring Security to verify permissions, so it is called for any authenticated object such as a REST method. Make the update to last login date optional via the APIs.

title: Users with access to REST services can list information for other users
body: If users are created with permissions for REST service access, they have the ability to list information for all other system users. This should only be available if the user has privileges for user administration.

title: Search providers not configurable via tenant configuration editor
body:
https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/sitewhere/lknGYbhcHqw

There is currently no method of configuring search providers via the web-based tenant configuration editor. Add search providers category as well as implementations (such as Solr) to the tenant configuration model so they show up as configurable.

title: MongoDB calls fail when authentication is enabled
body: When using authenticated access to MongoDB, database calls fail due to authentication errors. The existing code assumes that user credentials are in the *sitewhere * database, which for most users is not the case. Add ability to specify authentication database when using credentials for MongoDB.

title: Date parsing problems in data series queries
body:
See https://github.com/sitewhere/sitewhere/issues/85

REST methods such as the ones used for retrieving data series have problems parsing dates in shortened formats. You must currently pass everything up to the millisecond. The restrictions should be relaxed, and invalid dates should return a 400 response code rather than a 500 which indicates an internal error.

title: NullPointerException in GroovyRouteBuilder event processing
body:
See https://github.com/sitewhere/sitewhere/issues/86

Some of the updates to the Groovy configuration for 1.9.0 caused problems with GroovyRouteBuilder. Event processing now throws NPE when attempting to route an event.

title: Azure EventHub processor fails with errors in Apache Qpid
body:
See https://github.com/sitewhere/sitewhere/issues/84

Apache Qpid starts throwing exceptions after sending data for several minutes. Test the latest Qpid version to see if it will fix the problem.

title: Trim whitespace from hardware ids and add validation in UI
body: It is possible to add new devices with hardware ids that include spaces. This should be prevented by adding validation in the UI and REST services.

title: Events for non-assigned device should create unassociated assignment
body: If events are received for a device that has not been assigned, an error message is printed to the log. This is due to the fact that events are attached to the current device assignment and not the device itself. When events are received for a non-assigned device, create an unassociated assignment for the device on-the-fly and log events to it.

title: Metadata grid causes layout problems with large number of elements
body: When many items are added to the metadata for an object, the metadata grid causes the containing dialog to stretch. Properly handle scrolling to prevent dialog stretching.

title: Duplicate keys in REST services generate 500 rather then 409
body: The REST services currently return a 500 error code for duplicate keys due to exception handling in the API implementations. Instead, a 409 (conflict) error code should be returned to more clearly indicate what happened and be consistent with expected REST behaviors.

title: When using InfluxDB persistence, state change events cause exception
body: When using the hybrid MongoDB / InfluxDB event management, device state change events are not properly persisted and generate a NullPointerException. The method for storing the state change event currently returns null rather than persisting the event. Add support for state change events.

title: Tenant with no sites causes presence manager to fail
body: If all sites are removed from a tenant, the device presence manager is not able to start. The failure of the presence manager does not allow the tenant to start, so it effectively makes the tenant unusable.

title: Twilio command destination items missing in tenant configuration editor
body: When adding a Twilio command destination via the tenant configuration editor, it allows you to enter the basic information, but not the nested elements. The command encoder and parameter extractor options are not properly populated.

title: Sending registration request for existing device should update metadata
body: When processing a registration request for a device that is already registered in the system, the metadata for the existing device should be updated with the metadata in the request. In some cases, devices need to send information such as their current IP address even if they are already registered.

title: Using JSONP with large payloads results in incorrect content type
body: SiteWhere properly handles JSONP requests in most situations, but in cases where larger payloads are involved, the content type returns JSON rather than JavaScript. This causes clients to fail due to security checks. It appears that this only happens when chunked transfer encoding comes into play.

title: Assignment state not updated when using hybrid MongoDB/InfluxDB approach
body: When using the hybrid MongoDB/InfluxDB approach for storing device event data, assignment state is not updated even when the 'update state' flag is set.

title: MapQuest mapping provider for Leaflet no longer works
body: MapQuest no longer makes map tiles available via direct request, so any site using the MapQuest provider breaks. Update to the latest Leaflet libraries and add another default provider that works.

title: Unhandled exceptions in state processing can kill state manager thread
body: If an unhandled exception occurs in the state manager persistence thread, it can bubble and kill the thread. Since there is nothing to make sure the thread is alive, all state changes are ignored from the point on for the tenant. Add better exception handling to prevent uncaught exceptions from killing the thread.

title: Deleting user does not remove it from tenant auth users list
body: When removing a user from the system, the user id is not automatically removed from the list of authorized users for tenants. It could present a security risk if a new user is added with the same username, but is not intended to have access to the tenants.

title: Startup reports wrong name for SiteWhere home environment variable
body: When SiteWhere starts, it uses an environment variable to find the root folder in which the configuration is located. If not found, an error is reported indicating SITEWHERE_HOME is not set. The code is actually checking 'sitewhere.home'. Update code to check both variable names.

title: ActiveMQ event source missing KahaDB store jar
body: When using an ActiveMQ event source with SiteWhere 1.7.0, a ClassNotFoundException is thrown due to a missing jar file. Add KahaDB jar to fix problem.

title: SiteWhere client call for listing device commands not working
body: The REST call in SiteWhereClient is using the POST method rather than GET, so it fails.

title: Hazelcast should be configured for one group/cluster per tenant
body: The current Hazelcast configuration uses a single group for all tenants, effectively making all tenants part of the same cluster. This does not mesh with the goal of completely separating data between tenants and can lead to other problems. Update default configuration to use a different group per tenant id.

title: Arduino example uses outdated protocol buffers definition
body: Update protocol buffers definition in the Arduino example to use the latest specification. The specification as given is not compatible with recent versions of SiteWhere.

title: Refactor to remove CXF dependencies
body: The system currently uses CXF to make REST calls in some cases, which pulls in many transitive dependencies and bloats the product. Since Spring RestTemplate is already being used in the majority of cases and is part of the Spring Boot strategy, the modules that use CXF should be refactored to use it as well.

title: Accessing REST services for stopped tenant results in server error
body: If a tenant is in a stopped state and a client accesses the REST services using valid credentials and tenant auth token, the server generates an error. The tenant engine state should be checked as part of the auth token verification process. Rather than generating a 500 status code it should return a 503 indicating the service is not currently available.

title: Assets searches not returning correct results
body:
Some asset queries are not returning the correct results. Including:

* Location search by name
* Hardware search by name or description

The REST services are returning a 200 with no results.

title: Command invocation with no initiator id causes error on admin UI
body: The device management APIs allow command invocations to be created with no initiator id, but the admin UI errors when that is the case. Update admin UI to handle case where initiator id is not specified.

title: Unable to log in with multiple tenants active
body: If a user has access to multiple tenants and tries to log in to the system, choosing an available tenant results in an error page. Can be replicated by starting with a fresh system, adding a new tenant with the admin user as an authorized user, then logging out and attempting to log back in and choose a tenant.

title: Tenant REST APIs not properly restricting access
body: The tenant REST APIs are only using coarse-grained permissions to control access. Currently, this means that only tenant administrators can access many of the REST services even when users are marked with self-editing permissions. Also, tenant REST APIs should verify that the authenticated user is in the list of allowed users for a tenant before giving access to its data.

title: State not being returned on assignment lists for HBase
body: When listing device assignments, state information is not being returned when using the HBase provider. The MongoDB provider returns the state so HBase should be the same to be consistent. It's also needed to support presence calculations.

title: Do not allow specification to be deleted if devices are using it
body: The REST services currently allow device specifications to be deleted even if devices are using them. This causes problems since the devices are orphaned and have no frame of reference. Require any devices using the specification to be deleted before deleting the specification itself.

title: Deleting last tenant makes SiteWhere unusable
body: If all tenants are deleted from the system, there is no way to log back in to add tenants. The current approach brings up a page indicating that the user has no available tenants to log in with. If the user is a tenant administrator, they should be allowed to see the tenant management page.

title: Login page contains invalid script reference
body: As per https://github.com/sitewhere/sitewhere/issues/19, the Kendo library is incorrectly referenced in the login page. This does not currently cause problems since the components are not used there, but it might cause future problems.

title: Getters in MongoDB device management should return null if not found
body: The responses for calls in the MongoDB device management implementation are inconsistent. They should all return null if the object is not found by id. Many currently throw exceptions, which is not the expected behavior.

title: Plugging a device into a composite device generates an error
body: Plugging a device into a composite device generates an error because the URL for the POST request is invalid.

title: Attempting to delete assignment results in error message
body: When viewing a list of assignments, if you click on the 'x' to delete an assignment and ok it, an error message "Tenant not found for authentication token." appears. This is the result of the conversion to multitenancy and the tenant auth token not being passed in the URL.

title: When adding subgroups to a device group, validate element id
body: When adding a subgroup to a device group via the admin interface, it is possible to add an invalid element id without getting an error. This results in bad data in the database and exceptions around invalid references when listing the elements. Add validation when the subgroup is entered so that bad data can not be added.

title: Entering username with dot symbol breaks user edit functionality
body: When attempting to edit a user with a username that contains a dot character, the edit fails. This is due to a couple of problems with the Spring configuration. The path variable needs to allow the character (which is does not by default) and suffix handling needs to be turned off for Spring content negotiation.

title: Air traffic control example does not work with multitenancy
body: The air traffic control example was created before multitenancy was introduced, so it does not work on SiteWhere 1.2.0 and later. Update the example to work on multitenant systems.

title: Siddhi Groovy stream processor generates NPE at runtime
body: The addition on multitenancy introduced a bug that causes an NPE in the SIddhi Groovy stream processor. The lifecycle component is not having its associated tenant set, so the script makes an invalid reference.

title: Outbound processor for Azure EventHub fails with missing dependency
body: This was reported by a customer in GitHub issue (https://github.com/sitewhere/sitewhere/issues/13). It looks like the Qpid jar for AMQP is not being included in the SiteWhere build.

title: Stopping and restarting a tenant with an MQTT command destination does not release resources
body: If a tenant that uses an MQTT command destination is shut down, reconfigured, and restarted, exceptions occur indicating that the resources have not been released.

title: Executing batch command invocation with no site chosen returns no results
body: Executing a batch command invocation from the administrative application without choosing a site causes the result set to be empty. Choosing a site fixes the problem but should not be required.

title: Icon for viewing command invocation details missing
body: The icon that was previously shown at the right of each command invocation in the assignment detail page is no longer shown. This does not allow details about the command invocation to be viewed.

title: XML schema can not be resolved when server started without internet connection
body: If the server is started without an internet connection present, the Spring initialization fails due problems resolving the SiteWhere schemas. Spring has built-in handlers for loading schemas from jars rather than the network, but they are not being used. It appears that the addition of request parameters to the end of the schema URLs is causing the Spring logic not to properly match. Update the default configuration files so that they can work offline.

title: If lat/long values are not entered for location asset, list page does not load
body:
When adding new location assets, the UI allows latitude and longitude not to be entered, but leaving them blank causes the asset list page not to load. 

Reported in https://groups.google.com/forum/?hl=en#!topic/sitewhere/lvZYd0H40uY

title: Clicking on Specifications tab with no asset data throws exception
body: If starting a system with model initializers disabled, clicking on the device specifications tab results in an exception (as reported by https://groups.google.com/forum/?hl=en#!topic/sitewhere/r3BtN-mIpDQ)

title: On upgrade, new permissions not automatically added
body: When upgrading to a new SiteWhere version, new user model granted authorities are not automatically added. The new permissions should be merged on startup so they show up in the hierarchy when editing users.

title: Java client not passing date fields for listDevices()
body: The Java client method for listing devices takes date range search criteria, but does not pass the parameters through to the web service.

title: In device emulator, MQTT port is not persisted across sessions.
body: When using the device emulator, if the MQTT port and other values are changed, they are not persisted across sessions. If users have SiteWhere configured differently than the default, this results in having to re-enter the data every time the page is reloaded. Use cookies to persist the data across sessions.

title: Fix annotations on paging parameters to show correctly in Swagger
body: When using the Swagger interface, paging parameters on list methods appear as required fields. Example URLs always include the page number and size even though they are not required. Update annotations so that Swagger correctly interprets the usage.

title: Titles missing on many pages in admin UI
body: The internationalization code changes the way titles are specified and many pages are no longer displaying a title.

title: Adding/removing assets in admin UI does not change system runtime
body: When assets are added/deleted/changed in the new admin UI panel, the changes are not reflected in the runtime system until the system is restarted or the asset management REST service refresh method is called. As side-effect of edits, auto-flush the cache on the corresponding asset module. Also, when adding or removing categories, reflect changes in the runtime asset module manager.

title: Protobuf encoded command invocations throw exception
body: Invoking commands that are sent with the default protobuf encoding scheme results in a stack trace and command not sent.

title: Adding asset with no image causes error in admin console
body: When entering an asset in the admin console, if you do not add an image, the dialog does not prevent you from submitting and the REST call saves the data, but the list screen no longer works. Require that an image URL be associated with every asset.

title: Deleting devices does not remove them from cache
body: When devices are deleted, they are not being removed from the cache. The result is that the device APIs still return the device for queries by hardware id.

title: Asset management REST APIs can be ambiguous
body: The asset management REST APIs that interact with a single asset module should be prefixed by the 'modules' path element. For example /assets/my-module/asset should be /assets/modules/my-module/asset. This makes it clearer what the URL delivers since the old format would infer an asset reference rather than an asset relative to a module.

title: Java client gets error unmarshaling result from asset search REST call
body: Executing the SiteWhereClient.getAssetsByModuleId() method results in an exception due to new fields that have been added to the asset base class in version 1.0.5. The "assetCategoryId" field should be ignored if null.

title: MongoDB port number can not use property placeholder due to schema restriction
body: When using Spring property placeholders, the schema parser complains about using the ${portNumber} syntax because the attribute is defined as an xsd:int. Update schema with a new type that allows an integer or a string value that matches a regular expression for a property placeholder.

title: Server hangs on startup if MQTT broker is not available
body: If SiteWhere is configured with an MQTT event source and the broker is not available, the server hangs until the broker is available. There should be a configurable timeout after which the event source will fail, but the rest of the server still functions.

title: Misssing internationalized value in header on device detail page
body: When internationalization was added, the title bar value at the top of the device detail page was not added properly, resulting in it not being shown.

title: MongoDB device managment implementation does not support passing credentials
body: The MongoDB device management implementation does not currently support passing credentials for authenticated servers. Generally, MongoDB is only used for local installations, but some users need to run on hosted MongoDB instances. Add ability to specify username and password for MongoDB implementation and add attributes to Spring configuration to make it easy to configure.

title: If connection to MongoDB is lost, exception bubbles rather than being handled gracefully
body: If SiteWhere is using a MongoDB instance for persistence and communication with the instance is interrupted, an uncaught exception bubbles out to the REST servlet. The loss of connectivity should be handled gracefully with proper error reporting.

title: Internationalization value not available for 'device search' dialog
body: The 'device search' dialog shown when choosing a device to add to a composite device does not display properly. The i18n value is not found and causes the other elements not to display properly.

title: Internationalization value not available for hardware id in 'assign device' dialog
body: The i18n value for English on the 'hardware id' label in the 'assign device' dialog is not present so the label does not display properly.

title: Leaving final slash off admin interface URL causes 404 error
body: If the user enters http://localhost:8080/sitewhere/admin (with no trailing slash), the admin interface generates a 404 error. Quite a few users have run into the problem, so the application needs to be updated to cover that URL as well.

title: Logic for updating model objects forces passing of existing metadata
body:
The logic used for updating model objects does not preserve existing metadata values. The base class for create/update requests is MetadataProvider and it starts with an empty map. The common update logic treats an empty map as a request to remove all metadata (SITEWHERE-146). Instead of inheriting from MetadataProvider, the requests should have a getMetadata() method which starts with a null value. 
* If a null is passed, the existing metadata is left unchanged. 
* If an empty map is passed, all values are removed. 
* If a populated map is passed, the existing values are replaced with the provided values.

title: Authentication token is hard-coded for Swagger UI requests
body: It appears that, while updating to the latest version of Swagger, the default credentials were hard-coded in the headers being sent to the SiteWhere APIs. If a different username or password is entered at the top of the page, they are not used. If the default account password is changed, all calls fail. Credentials need to be generated dynamically with each REST call.

title: There is no way to remove all metadata from most objects
body: Although the REST APIs and admin console user interface are supposed to allow removing metadata fields, the case where all metadata is removed does not work. If an empty array of metadata is passed to the REST services, the existing metadata is not removed.

title: HBase performance is slow for device events
body: HBase performance for device events is slower than it should be. The event table is set up for autoFlush, so each put is causing the pipe to be flushed. The implementation should be improved to allow device event puts to be batched for greatly increased performance. Also assignment state was being updated by default for events. The default should be not to update the state unless the inbound event source is configured to update it.

title: Spring libraries cause problems with Java 8
body: The version of Spring used in SiteWhere 1.0.1 (3.2.1-RELEASE) is not compatible with Java 8 and causes exceptions on server startup. Upgrade Spring libraries to a newer version that is compatible with Java 8.

title: Metadata names with invalid characters can be submitted via REST services
body: The system does not currently validate metadata field names to make sure that they do not contain special characters. Metadata names should only contain alphanumeric characters plus underscores or periods.

title: References to CATALINA_BASE fail to resolve on some systems
body: On some systems, system startup fails due to the CATALINA_BASE environment variable not being resolved at runtime. Investigate using CATALINA_HOME instead.

title: Commands sent to nested devices are sent to the wrong hardware id
body: When sending a command to a nested device, the command should be addressed to the parent hardware id. This was working in previous versions, so introduction of new routing constructs may have introduced a regression.

title: Shutdown of socket inbound datasource shows error in logs
body: When the server shuts down, the socket event source generates an exception on closing the socket even though the condition is expected. The error should be ignored if the event source is shutting down.

title: Admin application should display error page if server not started
body: The admin console application fails with an exception if the server does not start cleanly. Instead, it should display an error page and point the user to the logs to find the error.

title: Event source and receiver APIs can result in message loss
body: The current APIs for inbound event sources use queues in the receivers and threads in the event sources for processing them. The events should only be queued in the inbound processing strategy since, if the system goes down before the receiver queue is empty, events may be lost. If the inbound processing strategy uses persistent queues or something similar (as in the enterprise edition), the events should never be lost.

title: REST calls fail after login expires in admin app, but app does not redirect to login page
body: When using the administrative console application, the user login expires after a few minutes of inactivity. At that point, clicking on most links causes the application to redirect to the login page. However, AJAX REST calls do not result in the same behavior and instead show an error message indicating the call was unauthorized. The AJAX calls should result in a redirect to the login page as well.

title: Default configuration assumes sitewhere.properties file exists even if not used
body: The default sitewhere-server.xml file assumes that the default Spring property placeholder file (sitewhere.properties) exists and throws an exception if not. Since the default configuration does not have any property placeholders used, if the file is missing, it should be ignored.

title: HBase performance is slow on simple calls
body: On simple calls that should not take long to execute, the HBase device management implementation is lagging. Investigate performance bottleneck.

title: Registration manager requires protocol-specific code
body: The current registration manager implementation requires protocol-specific code because there are no SPI classes to allow things to be generic. The implementation-specific code should be pushed into the encoder in the command destination so that the registration manager is protocol agnostic.

title: MQTT topics in command delivery provider require hardware id as last portion of topic
body: The existing MQTT command delivery provider only allows topics that have the hardware id as the last element in the topic. The values should use a format string to allow the hardware id to be placed anywhere in the topic.

title: Not including trailing slash in SiteWhere API causes failures in Mule Studio plugin
body: When entering the SiteWhere API URL in the SiteWhere global element properties in the Mule Studio connector, subsequent REST calls fail. The plugin should automatically detect whether the trailing slash is missing and add it if necessary.

title: User account credentials are not being used in Mule Studio connector
body: If credentials other than the defaults are entered in the Mule Studio connector, the values are ignored. In the case where the password for the default account has been changed, calls to the remote SiteWhere instance will always fail.

title: Creating specification command parameter of type boolean fails
body: When adding a new specification command from the admin UI, adding a boolean parameter causes the operation to fail. The problem appears to be a discrepancy between the type list in the UI and the type list in the backend API.

title: Button for 'Edit Specification' on specification detail screen not working
body: Clicking the 'Edit Specification' button at the top of the specification detail page does nothing. It should bring up the corresponding dialog.

title: Command links on specification detail page do not work
body: Links for commands on the specification detail page underline with a hand cursor when moused over, but nothing happens when they are clicked. Clicking should open the 'edit command' dialog for the command.

title: Support "administer own tenant" permission in REST services and web interface
body: Though there is already a permission for "administer own tenant" in the list available for users, the REST services and web interface do not use the permission. The permission should be checked when querying for a single tenant by id, updating a tenant, listing existing tenants, and deleting a tenant via the REST services. It should also apply to the administration dropdown to determine whether the "Manage Tenants" entry is made available.

title: Tenant template dropdown does not select correct template on updates
body: When attempting to update the list of authorized users for a tenant, the error message "Can not change the template of an existing tenant." is shown.

title: Querying for site with invalid token returns 400 response code rather than 404
body: When querying for a site by a non-existent token, the response code is 400, but should be 404.

title: Invalid asset reference in device specification causes exception that prevents rendering
body: If the asset referenced by a device specification is deleted, an exception is thrown that prevents the user interface from rendering. The error should be recorded, but the REST call should be allowed to return along with an indication that the asset is not found so a "broken link" can be indicated in the user interface.

title: Sending measurements event with 'update state' flag set generates exception
body:
See https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/sitewhere/r3DnE_PB5H8

When sending a measurements event with the 'update state' flag set, an exception is thrown because the event id is a UUID and MongoDB expects it to be an ObjectId. This is related to #130 where we introduced the ability to update metadata on existing events.

title: Hazelcast cache causing issues for datastore asset modules
body: It appears that there are cases where the Hazelcast cache used to store assets for datastore asset modules is cleared, causing problems with looking up assets at runtime. Remove Hazelcast caching for now and wait for refactoring of asset management subsystem before adding caching back in.

title: Groovy socket interaction handler not initialized properly
body: When running a Groovy script as a socket interaction handler, the processing fails with a NullPointerException due to the tenant not having been initialized when the event receiver starts. Use the standard "startNestedComponent" call to make sure the handler is properly initialized.

title: Updating existing asset category causes broken links
body: Updating an existing asset category (with or without changes) causes broken links due to the asset module manager not reloading properly. This shows up in the user interface like assignments are pointing to non-existent assets, even though they are still in the database.

title: Deleting active assignment from device UI does not delete assignment token from device document.
body:
While in the Web UI, under devices and within a specific device, if an active assignment is deleted, the assignment token does not get removed from the device doc and will still show "assigned" when looking at the full list of devices. Clicking "Release assignment" from there, gets the error that "device assignment token not found." This prevents the device from being reassigned, or deleted.

Of note, while in this state, from the API, you can successfully `get` the previously deleted assignment via `/assignments/{assignment token}`, but when attempting to delete the assignment with the corresponding delete call, the API responds with same error above.

With further investigating via mongo shell, I noticed the assignment does not exist in the Assignments collection, which was odd since I was able to get the Assignment from the API.  I also verified that the device doc was still was referencing the assignment token in the Devices collection. 

I was able to fix this by removing the device from the Devices collection via mongo shell and was then able to re-create and re-assign the device from the UI.

title: Device status not saved when creating a new device
body: The device status field is not persisted when a new device is created.

title: Memory leak in Groovy script runtime
body: When running a lot of traffic through Groovy scripts, the memory usage eventually creeps up until the VM runs out of memory. This is due to Groovy generating Java class metadata as part of its script execution. Update Groovy version and settings to remove memory leak.

title: InfluxDB command response 'respEvent' tag should be a field
body: When storing command responses in InfluxDB, the response event information is being stored as a tag rather than a field. This effectively creates a new series for each event, which is extremely inefficient.

title: System exceptions not properly relayed via gRPC pipes
body: When server-side logic throws a SiteWhereSystemException, the detail for the exception is lost because the content is not properly converted to pass across the gRPC pipes. Update error handling logic to properly pass and rethrow errors.

title: Metadata tab missing in tenant create/update dialog
body: The tab content is not rendering properly in the tenant create/update dialog, so the metadata panel is not being displayed.  This is due to updates in the Vuetify APIs. Update content to properly show tabs and metadata content.

title: Adding commands via user interface fails with server error
body: When adding a new device command via the user interface, a server error occurs. The error indicates that the device command token is required, but the underlying APIs allow it to be null. The gRPC definitions should mark the token as optional.

title: Command invocation button missing from device assignment user interface
body: When viewing command invocations in the administrative user interface, the button for invoking a new command is missing. This is due to updates in the Vuetify APIs. Use the updated APIs to enable the button.

title: Device group create fails when adding via the admin user interface
body: Adding a new device group fails due to a token field marked as required on the gRPC APIs when it is actually optional.

title: Component attributes in administrative interface sometimes not reset
body: When adding new components via the administrative user interface, attribute values from previously added components are sometimes not cleared, resulting in invalid component values. When the attributes dialog is reset, the previously entered values should be cleared.

title: Empty attributes in administrative component editor passed as empty strings
body: When configuring system components via the administrative user interface, leaving a field blank passes a blank string as the value for the attribute. The default behavior should be to not pass the attribute so that the Spring XML configuration does not try to use the value. This is a problem for numeric fields because they will fail validation. Instead, components should have standard default values for fields that are not passed (or they should be marked as required).

title: Port value ignored for CoAP server event source
body: When configuring the CoAP server event source, the port value is ignored. The schema allows for the port value to be specified and the configuration editor shows the field, but it is not being injected when Spring configures the underlying implementation.

title: Admin UI tenant creation passes token with wrong JSON field name
body: This is the result of swapping to internal ids + tokens rather than a single tenant id. The user interface should be passing the requested token field, but still uses the old tenant id format.

title: Initialization errors do not properly bubble for lifecycle components
body: When errors occur in lifecycle component initialization, they are not properly bubbled.. even when marked as required components. This can give the impression that certain aspects of the system are working when they have failed to initialize.

title: Deleting a user also deletes metadata from user tenants
body: If a user is deleted, the tenants that reference the user are updated to remove the user from the authorized user list. A side-effect is that tenant metadata is deleted.

title: User interface no longer displays permissions tree when creating a user
body: After the last Vuetify upgrade, the user permissions tree is no longer visible when creating a new user. The tabs component needs to be updated to use the newer Vuetify syntax.

title: Users with usernames that end in ".au" can not be accessed via REST
body: While users with username that end in ".au" may be added via the administrative UI, the corresponding GET request returns a 406 status indicating a problem with media type.

title: Concurrent tenant updates via API may generate an exception
body: When updating tenant information via the REST/internal APIs, a ConcurrentModificationException may be thrown.

title: API error when adding a site without a empty 'map' object
body:
Though optional, when doing a POST to /sites the body must contain property assignment `map: {}`, or unhandled exception is logged along with a 500 response. Confirmed via Swagger browser.

title: Loading invocation by unique id in InfluxDB can overload RAM
body:
Due to the way that command invocations are indexed in InfluxDB, getting one by unique id can result in loading all event data in RAM. From the original report:

> I can see in Influx logs that this API does the following iflux request:

> ```SELECT * FROM "DATABASE".autogen.events WHERE eid = 'invoc_id'```

> We noticed that this request overloaded the RAM of our influx instances if the database contains a lot of eid and it may lead to a crash of this machine. The reason to this RAM overload is that performing a filter on a field loads all the data in RAM until the  expected eid is found (fields re not indexed).

body: When persisting device data using MongoDB device management APIs, device status is not stored. All of the APIs support the field, but there is no corresponding entry in the MongoDB model.

title: Default values for MQTT outbound connector cause error
body: If no values are entered for the MQTT outbound connector an error is thrown indicating no topic, mulitcaster, or route builder are configured. The fallback should be to use a MQTT topic based on tenant id and connector id rather than failing.

title: Version of QRCode library is no longer available on Maven Central
body: Build processes are failing because the library for QR code support is no longer found on Maven Central. Update to later version.

title: Device registration microservice API channel / Consul errors
body: In cases such as backup/restore where services are scaled to 0 and back up, the device registration microservice reports error getting an API channel to other services and also is not able to register with Consul.

title: Service discovery causing connections to drop between microservices
body: There are cases where Consul marks a service as `critical` when systems are overloaded and the current connectivity monitor will drop connections due to unhealthy connections. Instead, do not drop connections, but rather report a warning about the connected service.

title: MongoDB server selection timeout exceeded
body: If the microservices start before a MongoDB replica set has time to initialize, there are cases where the server selection timeout (30s) is exceeded. Change the default to -1 to allow an indefinite wait since the server components can that make the requests can not start without the database present.

title: State change updates sending after shutdown and throwing exceptions
body: When shutting down an instance, state updates are still being sent after the heartbeat service is terminated. Cleanly handle shutdown by terminating the updates thread.

title: Allow clients to choose between cached/uncached data for remote APIs
body: Microservices are currently limited to either using the cached or uncached versions of remote APIs due to the way API channels are implemented. Separate the caching mechanism and allow both cached and uncached called from the same microservice depending on whether stale data may be tolerated.

title: Batch element processed date always displays as null
body: When viewing elements for a batch operation, the "processed date" always displays as null. The correct value is stored in the database.

title: Do not put artificial limits on event date ranges if not entered
body: Currently for event searches, if no date range is entered it is defaulted to a window which is set in the server-side logic. This is counter-intuitive for the user because they have not limited the query. Leave the date range query open-ended if no dates are specified. Open-ended date ranges will need to be properly handled in the event management implementations.

title: Useless code in KNX plugin
body:
I think I've found some useless or even wrong code in KNX plugin:

1. `self._lock = threading.Lock()` on [line 105](https://github.com/smarthomeNG/plugins/blob/00f151b23aea74ea299134c5e19b7a074cc54a58/knx/__init__.py#L105)  
If I didn't miss something, this property is never used.
Afterwards the `import threading` on [line 37](https://github.com/smarthomeNG/plugins/blob/00f151b23aea74ea299134c5e19b7a074cc54a58/knx/__init__.py#L37) can be removed also.

1. `self.handle_close()` on [line 388](https://github.com/smarthomeNG/plugins/blob/00f151b23aea74ea299134c5e19b7a074cc54a58/knx/__init__.py#L388)
I think this should be `self.close()` as `self.handle_close()` does nothing.  
`handle_close` is a method which can be implemented in objects which inherit from lib.connections.Stream. This is called in `Stream.close()` before the socket gets closed.
But in the KNX plugin `self.handle_close` is not implemented.

1. `if self.connected:` on lines [234](https://github.com/smarthomeNG/plugins/blob/00f151b23aea74ea299134c5e19b7a074cc54a58/knx/__init__.py#L234) and [250](https://github.com/smarthomeNG/plugins/blob/00f151b23aea74ea299134c5e19b7a074cc54a58/knx/__init__.py#L250)
The surrounding method `handle_connect` is called in lib.connection.Stream right one line below setting self.connected to true, so at the beginning of the method self.connected is always true.
If an exception happens in between we have a bigger problem and should not just ignore a closed connection but leave the method immediately.

title: Cycle between calculation of sun position is too long
body:
The cyclus between two calculations of the suns position is too long. Right now it is calculated every 30 minutes. That means e.g. an azimuth change of more than 10° which is too much. 
[env_loc]
    filename = location.py
    crontab = init | sunrise+1m | sunset+1m | sunrise-5 | sunset-7
    cycle = 1800
I would suggest to decouple the sunrise/sunset functions into one script which will be executed just around sunrise/sunset times and shortly afterwards. And then put two further scripts into the game, one for azimuth and one for elevation. The one for azimuth should update the azimuth every two minutes, this way we can keep the angle deviation below 1°. The one for elevation should update the elevation every five minutes so to keep the angle deviation below 1°. And furthermore which might be even more important: The script uses the smarthome sun object to do the calculations. When modifying the UZSU plugin I needed to create a new sun object since sharing it with the rest of SmartHomeNG can yield very strange and unexpected results.

title: Configuration values are not correctly retrieved
body: Configuration values are not retrieved correctly when asked via configuration topics. The problem is not detected in the tests, as a test validating the publishing format is also missing.

title: Attribute alias don't work along with timestamp
body: Currently, the timestamp conversion mechanism do not work properly with aliased attributes. Tests should ensure that an attribute that is aliased to be a timestamp, will properly trigger timestamping mechanisms.

title: Change C1 attribute name to P1
body: Change the name of the attribute generated in the device entity for a C1 device attribute to P1.

title: When there is a disconnection in the Mosquitto broker the Agent doesn't notice
body: When the Mosquitto shuts down or disconnects for whatever reason, once the mosquitto is up again, the subscriptions of the IOTA have been lost. It should, instead, try to recreate them when the connection is reacquired.

title: Provisioning API allows two devices with the same ID
body: With the MQTT IoT Agent this shouldn't be allowed, as two devices with the same ID and the same APIKey would use the same topics for its communications (and could not be distinguished by the IOTA).

title: Getting the information of a provisioned device returns an spurious 'id' attribute in attribute descriptions
body: A little back this year, the name of the attribute's attribute, 'id' was changed to 'object_id'. It seems part of the code remains as it was in the past, so the 'id' attribute is coming in the get provisioned device operation. It should be removed.

title: Mandatory resource should be equal to the default resource in the IOTAM
body: When the IoT Agent registers to the IoT Agent Manager, it declares a default resource, that will be used in every group provisioning to that agent. The IOTA should enforce that default resource in the group provisioning requests, instead of enforcing the empty string.

title: P1 and C1 Thinking Thing modules do not work in single attribute mode
body: P1 and C1 module translation was tested sending information through the multiattribute topic, but errors have been reported when the same values are sent using the single attribute one. Tests should be implemented to cover this functionality and, in case the error is reproducible, fix it.

title: Date in dt configuration attribute is given in PM format
body: It should be fixed to be in 24h format

title: Extra comma in Thinking Things B module
body: An extra comma in the tests of the B module made the module to require one parameter more than those needed. Both tests and code should be fixed.

title: Information of an error response from the Context Broker is not propagated
body: When a function of the library is executed and the Context Broker answers with a non-200 statusCode, a BAD_REQUEST error is returned, always with code 400 and a standard text. It should return the code indicated in the Orion error and the details returned by the CB.

title: No information is provided in the error object for transport errors connecting to the CB
body: When an operation relating CB Content is executed and fails with a transport error (HTTP status code != 200 and not known to be a common error), an empty details object is returned. At least information about the status code or the returned error should be provided.

title: Missing attributes in device provisioning API.
body: Some devices are not being read in the device provisioning API: internalAttributes, timezone, static_attributes.

title: Entity Not Found should have a 404 code
body: Current behavior is to return a 500 code in presence of an ENTITY_NOT_FOUND error. It should b echanged to 404.

title: Change the Identification of the Devices.
body: Early in the development of the IoT Agent, the library API was thought to use the combination of deviceId and deviceType as a key to distinguish different devices. This assumption doesn't hold anymore, so it's time to change it.

title: Use Express methods to check the content type
body: The content type is being currently tested checking the literal value of the headers. The `is()` method of the Express request should be used instead.

title: ListDevices doesn't work with just one parameter
body: The current listDevices implementation for both device registries (in-memory and MongoDB) works only in the four parameters form, and is should work with just the callback (to return the complete collection of devices). The in-memory registry has an additional problem, as it forces the existence of the service and subservice parameters (that should be optional).

title: Configuration API pagination is not working
body: Currently, the offset and limit parameters are ignored when a request for listing the configuration groups comes to the IoTA. Those parameters should be honored.

title: Data filtering plugins should apply to metadata as well
body: Current data filtering plugins (timestamp compression) do not apply to metadata, but they should process the metadata attributes in the same way as the regular ones.

title: Asking for the list of configurations of a subservice return results for all services
body: If the subservice `/*` is used to retrieve all the configurations for a given service, all the subservices of all the services are retrieved instead. This behavior should be changed to ensure only subservices for the given service are retrieved.

title: Query middlewares won't work
body: Due to the last changes in the data transformation plugins, the `ngsi.query` callback received an extra parameter, making queries with query middlewares fail.

title: Attribute id in alias should be named 'object_id'
body: In the current implementation of the attribute alias mechanisms, the id of the device attribute is named "id", but it should be named "object_id".

title: Library errors make HTTP Response invalid
body: When a library returns an error object with a .code attribute, the contained value is returned, even if its not a valid HTTP code.

title: Both object_id and id in attributes are stored, but only the id displayed
body: When the object_id was introduced (as the external name for the attribute id), id was kept as the internal name for the id. This caused a duplication of the attribute in the database that cause some visualization problems. The best option may be to change the internal code to use object_id for everyting.

title: Entity retrieval on incoming notifications or queries uses the entity name without the type
body:
When a request comes to the IOTA Northbound interface, the IOTA uses the entity name alone to retrieve the information of the device that generated the entity. This is an error, as multiple entities with the same name but different type may coexist for a single service. The identification should be changed to take this into account.

A similar problem may exist for entities with the same name in different services.

title: Documentation problems: JS Object vs JSON
body: Most of the examples of the documentation are caught from live JS Objects read from a debugging session, and may be easily misunderstood as JSON. There is not quite a big difference, but it may be causing some errors on people reading the documentation (and changing from one to the other consists, basically in adding lots of `"` characters around). They all should be changed to plain JSON.

title: Initial entity provisioning does not take configurations into account
body: When a new device is provisioned, its representing entity is created in the Context Broker with initial values, to allow all the updateContext operations to use the UPDATE action type (that requires the presence of the attribute that is going to be modified). In the case where the attributes are defined at Configuration level (not device level), this creation fails, as it uses just the attributes defined in the provisioned device (instead of using the merge of both). Similar problems may be found for different scenarios for the same causes: the multiplicity of sources of definition for the devices configuration. We should think carefully about how to solve this problem as we may solve future bugs if we treat it carefully (maybe moving around an object that is a merge of both the device information and the configuration one, making the former override the latter).

title: Change timestamp type to 'ISO8601'
body: Current timestamp's attribute type is "timestamp". It should be changed to "ISO8601".

title: Update provisioned device fails when no lazy attributes or commands are given
body: When a device update request arrives to the northbound API, if the body does not contain a `lazy` attributes array or a `commands` array, the request fails with a syntax error in the library.

title: Use the mechanisms for logData customization
body: The mechanisms to insert service and subservice information into the logs were laid down in a previous request, but those mechanisms must be used in the actual code, using the intoTrans() function.

title: Add support for MongoDB Replica Sets
body:
The mongodb driver should be able to connect to a MongoDB replicaset. In order to configure the replicaset:
- The `host` attribute of the mongodb configuration will accept multiple IPs sepparated by comma.
- A new attribute `replicaSet` will appear to give the driver the name of the replica set.

title: Command updates not implemented
body: Currently, the device provisioning update do not accept commands, and silently ignore it. Commands should be modifiable in updates, creating the appropriate registrations and collateral attributes.

title: When a query comes to the IOTA the Static Attributes should not be returned
body: The current behavior of the IOTA is to return the set of static attributes in every NGSI request, including queries; but this behavior only makes sense in updates. The static attributes should be removed from queries.

title: Type attribute in configurations not used
body:
When a new device is provisioned, the `type` attribute is currently set as mandatory, so the default device type of the configuration can't be used in that scenario. To avoid this problem:
- Type attribute in provisioning should be marked optional.
- If a type is not provided for a device and there is a type in the configuration, that will be used as the type.
- If no type is found in any place, the default type from the configuration is used.

title: Configuration API Should allow to modify API Key
body: The API Key was originally conceived to be part of the Key for Configurations, but that criteria has changed, and now it should be allowed to change.

title: Configurations should allow adding static attributes
body: Static attributes are currently just added from the device, and not from the configuration. This should be changed to allow static attributes from the configurations.

title: Timestamp and level missing in logs
body: At some point during the development of the current version, timestamp and log level ceased to be printed.

title: 'Mongodb' module not found when using the --production
body: The mongodb module is not automatically imported by Mongoose, so executing mongoose raises a not found error. The module should be added to the formal dependencies in the `package.json`
