title: Domain objects not working properly
body: The information stored in the domain for logging purposes is not working properly when accessed via Northbound API, so the service and subservice is not appearing in the log entries.

title: Timestamp addition for static attributes generate multiple identical timestamp attributes
body: When a device defines static_attributes, and those attributes are sent to the Context Broker, the Timestamp is also added to the attributes. But when a single device request generates multiple NGSI updateContext, the Timestamp attribute in the metadatas is multiplied times the number of requests. This seems to be a problem with metadata addition in the DB (the same object retrieved once from the database is modified instead of creating a new one, and the timestamp is added instead of modified).

title: Command line client raises a 404 when listing groups
body: Listing groups with the command line clients always result in a 404, as the request is not being done properly, following the Provisioning API. This should be addressed by adding the appropriate fiware-servicepath header: '/*'.

title: When persistence is defined for stats but not for the registries, the IOTA crashes
body: When the stats service is configured with the peristence option on, and the mongodb data is configured, if the deviceRegistry options is not configured with MongoDB persistence as well, the agent doesn't initialize the db and crashes.

title: No response from the IoTa when creating a new device
If a device is registered using the library methods it must contain a service and a subservice
body: Currently, the library checks the presence of the service and subservice headers for incoming requests in the provisioning API, but not for internal calls through the library methods. Checks should be applied for both systems.

title: Different device groups with the same type name can't be created
body: Currently, the entity type name is an internal key so if a new device group arrives with the same device type it will overwrite de older one. This behavior is wrong, but there is no clear idea about what to use as the universal ID of a device group (service/subservice tuple may be a candidate, but multiple types should appear for a single tuple).

title: Update the documentation to reflect the changes in function signatures
body: With the last refactor, most of the IOTA function signatures where changed to add the service and subservice parameters to the call, but this change was not reflected in the documentation.

title: Allow the getDevicesByAttribute() function of the In-Memory repository to search through all the services
body: Current implementation of the getDevicesByAttribute() forces the `service` attribute to be non-null, or it will raise an error (that should be controlled, as pointed out in other issue). This behavior should be changed, to match the one in the MongoDB Registry: if a service is specified, the result should match the service; if none is specified, all the devices matching the condition should be returned (regardless of their service).

title: Pass service and subservice as arguments in command handlers
body: Current command handlers receive just the type and id of the entity as parameters, but it should also pass service and subservice to be able to retrieve information about the device.

title: Command handler doesn't work if no update handler is defined
body: Current implementation fails when a updateContext requests comes from the Context Broker if there is a Command Handler but no Update Handler (for lazy attributes). An empty handler works to overcome this issue. This behavior should be fixed, so any of the handlers is optional.

title: Add a prefix for all the environment variables
body: Automatic environment variable generation in Docker makes some of the variable using too common names collide with the ones in other containers. To avoid this problem, a environment variable prefix should be added to all the variables.

title: Use the attributes defined in the Configuration as default alias values
body: Mappings from object_id to name in configurations should be used as default values in the alias plugins, whenever there are no correspondent mappings provisioned in the device.

title: Expose the singleConfigurationMode attribute using environment variables
body: Single Configuration mode should be configurable using environment variables, and not only using the config.js file.

title: Devices provisioned with no configuration are not found in HTTP measure reporting
body:
Relates to an issue in the UL IoT Agent:

https://github.com/telefonicaid/iotagent-ul/issues/124

It seems to be a problem with Mongo 3.2 as used in the Docker images.

title: In MongoDB32 no group is found if undefined resource is passed
body: In MongoDB32, passing undefined values for attributes make queries fail (instead of ignore those attributes).

title: IoTAgent returns non-NGSI error as a response to an error in the Context Providers
body: When a error is produced in the Context Provider operations, the IoT Agent returns an IoTAgent-specific type of error, that is not the expected response to an NGSI message.

title: Static attributes not shown in device group updates
body: Device group updates don't manage well certain parts of the payloads, due to the different names of the fields in the DB model and the payload.

title: IOTAM Registrations won't send static attributes in group information
body: Current registrations for the IoTManager send only information about active attributes, missing both commands and static ones. This behavior should be fixed to make the registrations reflect all the information in the device groups.

title: Update device operation ignores static attributes
body: Cloned from [an issue in the UL IoTA](Update device operation ignores static attributes #137).

title: Logger modules not being singleton cause logging inconsistencies
body: Logops library is used both in the IoTAgent library, and in the IoTAgent code, but, by some mysterious reason, sometimes the modules are treated as a singleton (and changing the log level in one of them changes both) and sometimes they aren't and it just changes one of them. This should be changed, to avoid problems  in the IoTA Logs.

title: Remove Device ID Index
body: Up until now, the IoTAgent library supposed that the DeviceID was going to be unique globally accross the system. In a multitenant environment, though, that claim doesn't hold anymore, so the Unique index in the ID field of the Device model should be removed.

title: Device provisioning list ignores service and servicepath headers
body: Device listings ignore the service and servicepath constraints

title: Device group updates won't save attributes and static attributes
body: Device groups updates don't seem to be storing updates in the staticAttributes and attributes collections.

title: Missing context in logger entries
body: There are multiple logger entries along the code that do not include the `context` object. Those should be fixed to include it.

title: Adding a conversion for TimeInstant causes duplicate attributes
body: If a device is provisioned with an active attribute mapping with an attribute name of TimeInstant, instead of using that value as the TimeInstant global value, the value is duplicated. This is strange as projects like GDL relied on this mechanism and it's working in older versions of the Agent so we must have broke it in some update. A specific test for this case should be created to ensure this doesn't happen again.

title: Service and servicepath should not be mandatory in device provisioning
body:
Service and servicepath attributes of the device provisioning request are mandatory, even now that they are taken from the service headers. 

The 'commands' attribute is also mandatory, and it shouldn't.

title: It is not possible to create two devices with the same ID
body: This behavior comes from the times when the Device ID was unique for all the IoTAgent. Those times are over. Each Service should have its own space of Device IDs, independent from the rest of the services.

title: New plugins don't check existence of attribute arrays
body: The new plugin for multientity attributes doesn't check for the existence of the active attributes array, and fails if the device is provisioned with no active attributes.

title: Bidirectional plugin doesn't apply to active attributes defined in a Configuration Group
body: Definition of bidirectional values should be allowed for both devices and Configuration Groups. Current behavior of the plugin is to provision the appropriate subscriptions just in the case when the reverse expressions are declared directly for a device.

title: Should raise an error if a device is provisioned with the same name
body: Provisioning the same device twice currently makes the second definition override the first. This should be changed to ensure that, once a pair (DeviceID, Service) has been provisioned, no other can be provisioned with the same IDs

title: Notifications return 404 instead of a 200 OK
body: Lack of a result handler in notification handling makes every notification end up in a 404 Not Found error.

title: Entities in multientity scenarios cannot be defined as expressions
body: With the current implementation of the multientity plugin, entities associated to particular attributes must be statically defined in the attribute during provisioning.  This values should be configurable as expressions, so the name of the entities can be created based on information from the incoming measure.

title: Pool command expired but CB not updated
body: When a poll command is expired (the device has not requested the command within the valid period) the CB is not updated accordingly. Iotagent should update CB with command_status ERROR and command_info with a descriptive error message.

title: Lazy attributes obscurely mandatory in Device Provisioning API
body: Due to a bug in the provisioning API, requests without the lazy attribute raised a TYPE_NOT_FOUND error.

title: Timeout errors catched by the domain handler
body:
When there is a connection error to Mongo caused by a Timeout, the error is not catched in the MongoDB connection nor in the function making the call, but in the domain error handler. Some work should be done here to:
- Ensure the connection error is given as near to the calling method as possible.
- Ensure the alarms are raised for MongoDB connection
- Those cases where the domain handler is needed anyway are documented.

title: Alarm raises with null error
body: When a function intercepted by the alarm management interceptor calls its callback with a null error, the interceptor raises an alarm (without need).

title: Shouldn't allow two device configurations with the same resource
body: The resource is a unique identifier that may be used for listening in URLs either in the Northbound or the Southbound, so it should be forced to be unique.

title: Unify alarm release and raise log levels
body: With the current version of the library, whenever an alarm is raised, a ERROR log is logged to the output, while the release of the alarm causes an INFO level log. Both should be unified either to ERROR or to LOG levels.

title: Fix JSON Schemas
body:
There are some issues with the JSON Schema used to validate API input:

* There are some fields that should be allowed in the Devide Modification schema that are not, e.g.: endpoint.

* Some JSON Schemas have the `additionalProperties` field set for the top level of the schema, where there is only one element: the array of devices or groups. The property is not set for the devices themselves or the groups, so the validation is practically useless.

title: MongoDB driver bug (NODE-818)
body:
MongoDB driver for Node.js shows a bug related to replica set discovery process. In more details, if some node on the replica set time outs before the discovery finishes, the driver returns "no primary found". Please check the issue [NODE-818](https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/NODE-818) at MongoDB's Jira.

Such an error is fixed in MongoDB driver for Node.js version 2.2.10. Neverhteless, this library uses version 2.1.18.

title: If the config doesn't include a `types` array the register operation crashes
body: Being optional, as they are, the presence of absence of the `types` array should not crash the IoT Agent. Either way, if they are mandatory, the error should be catched and presented properly, or if they are be optional, it should not create an error at all.

body: If not present, the Context Provider registration to the Context Broker returns a 400 error. This situation should be prevented and an error raised in the creation of the agent.

Update device operation ignores static attributes

title: Duplicated TimeInstant when an active attribute is mapped to TimeInstant attributes
body: There is a common scenario for measurement report that is a device recording measures offline for a long period of time, and then reporting all of the measures, each one of them with its own timestamp. For this case, the IoTAgent should allow the provisioned device to define a mapping between the original timestamp attribute sent by the device and the special 'TimeInstant' attribute in the entity. This would make the agent add the appropriate TimeInstant metadata to each updated attribute, so all the measurements reported end up in the NGSI sinks with their appropriate original timestamp. This mechanism was working early this year, at least in the JSON IoTAgent, so, either there is some differences in how both IoTAs treat the TimeInstant attribute, or something broke in the middle. We should add tests to check it, to make sure it doesn't happen again.

Such an error is fixed in MongoDB driver for Node.js version 2.2.10. Neverhteless, this agent uses version *, i.e. the latests version compatible with Node.js version. In order to ensure the correct versioning, a version equals or greater than 2.2.10 must be configured.

title: Should allow to provision LWM2M devices with an explicit internal mapping
body:
The agent currently requires one of two situations to happen:
- Either the device type is configured and has an internal attribute LWM2M mapping.
- o the device has been provisioned and has the needed mapping.

If a device registration arrives which doesn't meet any of this conditions, the agent crashes. The agent should allow a third condition: the device hasn't any kind of mapping, but it can use the OMA Registry mapping. And, in any case, the Agent should return an error instead of crashing.

title: localization is not set up correctly for packaging
body:
after moving some stuff around I noticed that the localization code isn't working properly and was catching the fallback. this generally isnt an issue since we only really have english support right now, so it will always fall back to that and nothing will look different.

after playing around with it and doing some reading, I'm pretty sure the localization stuff isn't set up correctly for a proper python package, which is what we're installing it as in the dockerfile.

the issue is that there isn't great comprehensive documentation on how to properly include it in the python package. there are a few examples I've found, but they don't seem great. need to spend some time reading into what exactly this requires, and then updating synse server appropriately.

title: move ARGs in Dockerfile to improve cache performance
body:
I apparently I misread/misunderstood the documentation on how the ARG keyword works. It seems like when the ARG variable changes, it will cause cache invalidation at the layer where ARG is defined. 

We should move the ARG definitions to below the main dependency install logic so we can actually use the caches and improve build performance.

title: plugin discovery on k8s endpoints only registers the first endpoint subset
body:
this will not always be the case, e.g. if we have a daemonset of a plugin deployed. I remember this being the intended design at the time of implementation because having multiple plugins under the same endpoint would cause them to fall under the same name..

this can be fixed just by extending the name for the plugin. this has implications in how its accessed/cached, etc but I think it should be a mostly easy update. another reason it was done that way was to prevent having dynamic names for what is potentially the same plugin. thinking a bit about it, I'm not sure its a big deal. the plugin name isnt really used externally (other than as info for which plugins are configured and their health), so as long as it remains consistent internally, we should be all set.

title: synse server does not refresh plugin state on cache rebuild
body:
Currently, there are a number of checks to refresh plugins if none are registered, but if any plugins are registered, the only ways to rebuild the plugin state is to either force a scan or hit the /plugins endpoint.

In its current production operation, neither of these cases may be hit for long periods of time, so if a plugin goes down, synse server will not try to reestablish communication with that plugin until either of the two above cases are hit.

To fix this, synse server should always refresh plugin state when rebuilding the device cache. This ensures that when the device cache is being rebuilt, all possible plugins are being accounted for.

title: plugin refresh does not behave correctly
body:
It was discovered that the plugin refresh mechanics are not working correctly. What was done to discover this was:

- create a plugin, have it be registered with synse
- check the /plugin endpoint and see it there and active
- terminate the plugin
- check the /plugin endpoint, see that it is now inactive
- start a new set of plugins

The new set of plugins does not show up in the /plugin output because of various checks/assumptions gating the plugin refresh. 

To fix this, I believe two things can be added:
- a refresh query param on the plugin endpoint -- this should allow a manual triggering of plugins to be refreshed. The API docs should be updated accordingly.
- a background task to periodically refresh plugins. This would likely also need a config value to set the refresh rate.

title: unify responses for 'data not found' from plugin
body:
## Description
It seems like when a device does not have any data (e.g. the plugin SDK fails to read anything off of a configured device) we either:
- get `"null"` back as the reading value in a valid 200 read response
- get a 500 specifying that no readings are found

The behavior here should be unified so we always expect the same thing for the same class of error. I'm not sure what conditions make it so that "null" is returned vs. a 500, so that will need to be investigated first.

To recreate this, there can be a device configured in a plugin that doesn't physically exist, so the SDK can't read off of it. Then read that device off of Synse Server.

I think that returning "null" (or the actual `null` type) should be fine, but I'd like to hear what others think -- does it seem like returning `null` is better, or returning a 500 error when there are no readings for a configured device.

Note that this case of 'no readings' can occur when:
- a device is configured but doesnt exist
- a device is unplugged/unreachable
- a device fails and can no longer be read from

<!-- Please provide more details below this comment. -->
jslog function is
 "extern void jslog(int level, const char *file, int line, const char *logtag, const char *format, ...);"
in packages/logger/binding.cc, you should not fill log content string to "format", if the log content has "%s", it will cause error when dealing with va_list args.
The correct way to use jslog is like this:
jslog(level, NULL, 0, tag, "%s", text);
